articles.title: Download and Install RTrader Pro on Windows
articles.description: Download RTrader Pro from an official source, check Windows requirements, install it and verify the version before signing in.
articles.answer: Download RTrader Pro from Rithmic’s official product page or the installer linked by your account provider. Run the Windows installer, open the application, then use the Rithmic credentials and System assigned to your account. Installation alone does not activate data or trading access.

toc.label: Check the computer and provider instructions

articles.body:
Check the computer and provider instructions

Rithmic's current desktop page lists 64-bit Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server 2016 or later. The Windows desktop app is not a native macOS application. Check the provider's supported platform and current operating-system support as well; a listed minimum is not a reason to run an unsupported operating system.

If the provider supplies a branded installer or a required upgrade sequence, use its current instructions. An already working installation does not need to be removed merely to make its screens resemble this guide. Preserve your workspace and account information before a provider-directed reinstall.

Install the desktop application

  1. Open the official product page and choose Download for Windows. Its current download link points to downloads.rithmic.com/rtraderpro.msi.
  2. Save the file and confirm its origin before opening it. Avoid third-party download mirrors.
  3. Run the installer. Read its licence terms and select installation options only if you agree. Screen wording can change between builds.
  4. Finish the installation and open Rithmic Trader Pro from Windows.
  5. Use the provider's trading username, password, System and Gateway. Do not select a System solely from a “funded” or “evaluation” label.
  6. Follow the first-login checks, including agreements and account visibility.

Confirm what succeeded

Check What it establishes
Application launches Installation can run on this computer
Credentials accepted Authentication succeeded for the selected service
Expected account appears The login exposes that account
Market-data entitlement and quotes Separate evidence of data access
Order acknowledgement and fills Separate execution evidence, not part of installing software

The VPS used for this library runs desktop version 17.106.0.2 with an existing authenticated session. The screenshots below show the download/requirements references and real login controls; they are not a recording of a fresh installation.

If installation or launch fails

Keep the installer filename, Windows version and complete error. Check the provider's supported build and Windows installation policy. Do not disable security controls or delete the Rithmic folder as a generic repair. For a login error after launch, troubleshoot credentials/System rather than repeatedly reinstalling.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Is the installer a Rithmic account?
faq.a: No. Obtain trading credentials from your provider, or use the official trial if eligible.

faq.q: Which System should I choose?
faq.a: The one issued for that login. Apex, Rithmic Paper Trading and Rithmic 01 are distinct entries.

faq.q: Can I install desktop RTrader Pro on a Mac?
faq.a: The desktop build is for Windows. Rithmic offers web/mobile access for eligible accounts; its public demo does not include those interfaces.

faq.q: Must I sign market-data agreements in the installer?
faq.a: Agreement completion is an account workflow after installation or through the provider’s supported route. Read the actual forms and classify yourself accurately.

articles.title: Rithmic First Login: Credentials, System and Status Checks
articles.description: Use your provider-issued Rithmic login and System, check agreements, and confirm account and connection status before configuring a trading workflow.
articles.answer: Get the Rithmic credentials and assigned System from your account provider. Open its supported Rithmic interface, select that System and the documented Gateway, then log in. Review any required agreements and confirm the expected account. Successful login is only the first check; it does not establish trading permission, live-data entitlement or tested order execution.

toc.label: Sign in and check the result
Confirm the native account and agreements
Native desktop references from this VPS

articles.body:
Prepare the correct information

Item Where to get it
Trading username and password Provider's secure account area or account-issued instructions
System The instructions for that specific Rithmic login
Gateway Provider's supported connection instructions
Interface and connection arrangement Platform guide for your provider and version

Do not publish a screenshot containing a password or full account identifier. A funded/evaluation label alone is not a reliable System selector.

Sign in and check the result

  1. Open the provider's recommended interface. Use the desktop download guide if the intended workflow requires desktop RTrader Pro.
  2. Enter the trading credentials, checking for accidental spaces.
  3. Select the issued System and an appropriate supported Gateway. The session captured for this library used Apex / Chicago Area; that is not a default for other providers.
  4. Log in once and preserve any exact error message. Use the login error guide if rejected.
  5. Review the required agreement route. Answer subscriber classification questions accurately rather than choosing a status solely because it is cheaper.
  6. Confirm the expected account and connection. Check market data and the intended trading route separately.

Apex's official setup guide identifies its credentials in the welcome email or Rithmic Account area and specifies the Apex System. Use that guide for Apex-specific desktop settings; do not transfer them to another firm.

What was checked here

An authenticated web session was opened and its System/Gateway, help, agreement-status and instrument controls were observed. No account was created, agreement accepted or order submitted. The login screenshots have empty credential fields. They are layout references rather than proof of a new-account onboarding sequence.

Captured reference images

The captions distinguish observed web screens from vendor documentation and imported desktop references. The native desktop and web references below document their stated controls and authenticated states; neither is an execution test.

Confirm the native account and agreements

Open File → Trader Dashboard and match the expected account privately. Then open File → Agreements & Documents and File → Market Data Entitlements. These panels were opened on the logged-in VPS on 7 October 2026. Agreement status, account visibility and data subscription are separate checks.

Native desktop references from this VPS

The later Windows inspection captured an unused login form with empty credentials and its actual System menu. The authenticated Apex / Chicago Area window was then rechecked with green service indicators. This was an existing login, not first-time account creation or agreement signing.

faq.q: Is my website password the correct Rithmic password?
faq.a: Use the credentials explicitly issued for Rithmic. Do not assume another login is interchangeable.

faq.q: Can I select Rithmic 01 because my account is funded?
faq.a: Use the System assigned to the specific login. Funding labels do not establish the connection environment.

faq.q: Does no agreement popup mean something is broken?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Existing records may already be complete, or the provider may use another supported route. Check status before repeating setup.

faq.q: Am I ready to trade after login?
faq.a: Login alone does not verify the account's limits, data permissions, order route or exit handling. Complete the setup checklist.

articles.title: Rithmic Systems and Gateways: Choose the Issued Connection
articles.description: Understand Rithmic System and Gateway fields, view captured native menus, and choose provider-issued settings without assuming a universal server list.
articles.answer: Use the System assigned to your Rithmic login, then a Gateway supported for that System and workflow. System identifies the connection environment; Gateway identifies an entry point. Do not choose a System from the words “funded,” “demo” or “live” alone. Menu entries vary by interface and version, and an entry does not prove that your account can use it.

toc.label: Find the two fields in desktop RTrader Pro
What the native System menu showed
What the Gateway menu showed for Rithmic 01

articles.body:
Find the two fields in desktop RTrader Pro

The inspected desktop version, 17.106.0.2, has System and Gateway in both the Orders and Market Data login sections. The credentials are empty in this reference. Box 1 marks Orders; box 2 marks Market Data.

  1. Obtain the current Rithmic login and connection instructions from your broker or funding provider.
  2. Find its exact System label in the intended interface.
  3. Confirm the supported Gateway rather than copying another trader's setting.
  4. Check whether the application uses a direct connection or a local RTrader plugin. Its server label may combine several connection details.
  5. After an appropriate connection attempt, verify the expected account and services. Keep an existing working connection intact while investigating alternatives.

What the native System menu showed

The unused login form exposed 31 System labels in the native control on 7 October 2026. Examples included Rithmic 01, Rithmic Paper Trading, Apex, Bulenox, LucidTrading and Earn2Trade. The screenshot below shows a partial visible list; the outline marks Apex.

These labels are an observation of this installed build. They do not establish current signup availability, account-stage eligibility, firm permission for automation or copier access. No login was attempted on the unused form.

What the Gateway menu showed for Rithmic 01

With Rithmic 01 selected in the unused form, the control exposed these 18 labels:

Native label Native label Native label
Aurora Area Chicago Area Colo 75
Colo 75 Summary Europe Frankfurt
Mumbai Singapore Tokyo
Hong Kong Sydney US East
US West MDP3 Summary Seoul
Sao Paolo Cape Town NYC Area

Sao Paolo is the literal spelling in that menu. Do not silently substitute a different string in configuration instructions. The list is scoped to the observed Rithmic 01 form; it is not an Apex gateway list or an API hostname list.

Names containing Summary or Colo are not interchangeable with every regional choice. Ask the provider which entry is appropriate before using an unfamiliar option. This capture measured no latency and tested no alternative gateway.

Use provider-specific instructions

Apex's setup guide names its System. EdgeClear's connection details distinguish connection information for its environment. Quantower's guide uses its own server selector. These examples explain why a single table assigning a universal System to every “funded account” is unreliable.

If a required label is missing, record the application version and current menu, then ask the provider to confirm the supported build and connection. Do not try every System with your password.

faq.q: Are System and Gateway the same thing?
faq.a: No. Use both parts of the issued connection details. A matching Gateway cannot correct a login assigned to a different System.

faq.q: Does a closer geographic name guarantee a faster connection?
faq.a: No. Geography is only one consideration. Follow the supported choices, then compare performance in the intended workflow without interrupting active trading. See gateway selection.

faq.q: Why does my other platform use a different server label?
faq.a: Connectors can combine environment and location into one option or use different wording. Match that platform's guide rather than translating a label by guesswork.

faq.q: Can I use these labels as API server addresses?
faq.a: No. A desktop menu label is not a network hostname or a complete API endpoint. Obtain the API connection specification for the supported application.

articles.title: Rithmic Market Data Agreements: Signing and Status Checks
articles.description: Find the correct Rithmic agreement route, check existing agreement status, and separate subscriber classification from data access and trading permissions.
articles.answer: Use the agreement route supplied by your broker or prop firm. Read the subscription and self-certification forms and answer them accurately. In the R Trader Pro Web session inspected on 7 October 2026, Menu, then ?, then Agreements & Documents showed existing agreement status. That screen does not demonstrate the first-time signing process.

toc.label: How do I choose subscriber status?
What the observed status screen proves
If the forms or prices do not appear
Current native status and data checks

articles.body:
Before you start

Have the account provider's Rithmic login and assigned System. Check that any agreement link comes from the provider's official instructions. A website login and a trading-platform login may be separate.

Complete the required checks

  1. Open the provider's supported agreement route. EdgeClear documents both RTrader Pro and a linked web route; therefore desktop installation is not a universal requirement for every agreement workflow.
  2. Confirm the account/System before entering information.
  3. Read each form presented to you. The inspected web status screen names a Market Data Subscription Agreement and a Market Data Self-Certification. Do not assume that four separate exchange popups must appear.
  4. Answer the eligibility questions from your actual circumstances. Being a beginner, retail trader or evaluation-account holder is not enough information to determine classification.
  5. Submit only after you understand and agree to the terms. Keep the confirmation or status record available for your own reference.
  6. Reconnect as your provider instructs. Check exchange access separately if prices are still missing.

How do I choose subscriber status?

CME's Non-Professional Subscriber FAQ is the primary reference for its classification rules. Ask the distributor to resolve uncertainty before certification. This guide does not determine your eligibility or quote your account's fees.

What the observed status screen proves

The captured web panel displays previously completed records and dates. No agreement was accepted during this review. It establishes the location and labels of that status view for the inspected web version, not the correctness of a person's classification, current entitlement, billing or order access.

If the forms or prices do not appear

Situation Next check
No first-login popup Check the provider's agreement route and existing status
Existing records already shown Ask whether this specific login needs any further action
Still no quotes Check the System, market-data entitlement and competing data sessions
New login after an account change Confirm requirements for the new credentials with the provider

Do not repeatedly change classification, create accounts or reinstall software to force a popup. Escalate with the exact screen and error, excluding personal data.

Captured reference images

The captions distinguish observed web screens from vendor documentation and imported desktop references. The native and web panels record existing agreement status, separately from signing a new legal form or executing an order.

Desktop agreement-navigation reference

The earlier authentic desktop File-menu capture exposes Agreements & Documents, alongside other account-information entries. It establishes a navigation label for that inspection. No desktop agreement was accepted and no subscriber classification was changed.

First-time forms depend on the account and required records. The account used here had completed records, so its forms were not re-signed to manufacture a before/after example.

Current native status and data checks

Open File → Agreements & Documents for the desktop status list. Then open File → Market Data Entitlements to inspect data access. The current native panels below were captured without changing subscriber status.

faq.q: Must everyone install desktop RTrader Pro to sign?
faq.a: No universal requirement has been established. Follow the route documented by your provider; some offer a web route.

faq.q: Does signing guarantee immediate live data?
faq.a: No. Agreements, activation, exchange permissions and the current connection are separate checks. This review did not measure activation time.

faq.q: Do agreements automatically transfer to a new funded login?
faq.a: Confirm with your provider. Do not assume that a different username or System inherits the old login's status.

faq.q: Should I choose Non-Professional because it is cheaper?
faq.a: No. Select the classification for which you meet the applicable criteria. Ask the distributor if you are unsure.

articles.title: RTrader Pro System Requirements: Verify the Platform and Workload
articles.description: Check Rithmic’s published Windows compatibility, distinguish desktop from API requirements, and assess your workload without invented hardware minimums.
articles.answer: Use the current requirements for desktop RTrader Pro and every other application in the intended workflow. Rithmic's product page lists 64-bit Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server 2016 or later. It directs macOS users to web/mobile rather than claiming native desktop support. OS compatibility alone does not establish performance for your charts or safe support status for the operating system.
articles.body:
Which product are you checking?

Product or layer Matching requirements
Desktop RTrader Pro Current desktop product page and provider-supported installer
Web/mobile interface Its browser/device requirements and available features
Another trading application That vendor's current version and connector requirements
Custom Rithmic application The selected API kit and its supported deployment environment
VPS Suitable OS, provider terms, remote access and the complete application workload

Rithmic's desktop product page is the reference for the OS list. Its API page describes different language/OS options; API support on an OS does not establish that desktop RTrader Pro runs natively there.

This observation establishes that the displayed build was present on this Windows VPS. It is not a certification of every Windows Server release or a stress/performance test.

Check the computer before installation

  1. Confirm the OS edition, version and system type using the supported system-information view.
  2. Check whether the OS remains supported by its vendor and receives required security updates. A trading vendor's compatibility list is a separate question.
  3. Obtain the current installer through the provider's supported official link. Follow prerequisites actually reported by that installer; do not install a guessed .NET version.
  4. Check each additional platform's requirements and its Rithmic connector support.
  5. Retain the current working configuration and records before a planned change.

No universal CPU, RAM, disk-space, bandwidth or maximum-symbol figure is established from the sources reviewed for this guide. A generic “recommended trading PC” number should not be labeled an official Rithmic minimum.

Assess the intended workload

Charts, market depth, historical downloads, indicators and multiple applications can place different demands on the system. Measure CPU, memory, disk and network use during a representative permitted workload. Record the number of active charts/symbols and the observed problem. A quiet login window is not a benchmark for that workload.

For a VPS, verify that its Windows environment and remote session can run the required applications and supported plugin arrangement. Geographic proximity does not establish better reliability or order latency. Use the VPS guide as a separate investigation, not a promise that renting a server solves account or connector issues.

faq.q: Is macOS API support the same as desktop support?
faq.a: No. Check the actual product. API language/OS support and the desktop application's compatibility are separate.

faq.q: What .NET version must I install?
faq.a: Use the current installer and official provider prerequisites. This review did not establish a universal .NET version requirement.

faq.q: How much RAM guarantees smooth trading?
faq.a: No amount guarantees the complete workflow. Measure the actual workload and check each application's requirements.

faq.q: Does a speed test verify Rithmic connectivity?
faq.a: It tests the selected speed-test route. It does not confirm account permissions, plugin support or every endpoint the application uses.

articles.title: Rithmic firewall checks: verify the route before changing rules
articles.description: Investigate a blocked Rithmic connection using the exact platform, gateway and current endpoint requirements. Avoid unverified port lists and broad exceptions.
articles.answer: Obtain the current endpoint and port requirements for your exact Rithmic interface and provider before changing firewall rules. Check whether the failure concerns a direct server connection or a local plugin connection. A successful HTTPS test to the public Rithmic website does not test the trading route.
articles.body:
Identify the connection being tested

Record the application/version, System, Gateway and whether it uses a direct connection or a local R Trader Pro plugin host. Preserve the exact error and time. Quantower's connection guide specifically includes the connection between Quantower and R Trader Pro in its plugin checks. That is a different path from a browser opening a public website.

Obtain a precise network requirement

Ask the provider or platform support for the current destination hostnames, protocols, ports and traffic direction. Include your connection mode. Do not rely on a generic list of 443, 80 or unspecified dynamic ports as a verified Rithmic configuration.

Check What it can establish What it cannot establish
Public website loads Access to that website Access to the selected trading endpoint
TCP test to a documented endpoint succeeds A connection to that host and port Credentials, entitlement or order acceptance
Firewall log shows a blocked process Evidence of a local policy event Whether every reported trading problem has the same cause
Platform login succeeds Authentication for that interface Data or order permission for every account

Review a blocked application

  1. Confirm the application came from the official vendor or provider route.
  2. Match the actual executable and blocked destination to the support instructions.
  3. Ask the device or network administrator to review any managed policy.
  4. If an exception is required, limit it to the necessary application, direction and network profile.
  5. Retest the original platform connection and retain the result. Remove temporary rules that are no longer needed.

Microsoft's firewall guidance explains why allowing a known application is generally narrower than leaving a port open. It does not justify enabling every public and private profile or disabling protection as a generic trading fix.

Antivirus, VPN and corporate networks

A security warning is not proof of a false positive. Verify the installer source and publisher and use the vendor's support process before proceeding. Do not exclude an entire trading folder from scanning or bypass a warning merely because a tutorial says the application is legitimate.

If a VPN or managed network appears involved, give its administrator the documented endpoint requirements and failure times. Compare an approved alternative route only when permitted. Do not use a VPS or hotspot to bypass an organization's network policy.

faq.q: Does Rithmic only use port 443?
faq.a: No universal port list was verified in this review. Obtain the requirements for the exact product and connection mode.

faq.q: Does testing rithmic.com prove the trading connection works?
faq.a: No. It tests the public hostname and selected port, which may differ from your trading route.

faq.q: Should I disable the firewall to make login work?
faq.a: No blanket disablement is needed for this diagnostic process. Inspect evidence and use a narrowly scoped, administrator-approved rule when a documented requirement calls for it.

faq.q: Do I need a screenshot of an antivirus exclusion?
faq.a: No. This guide does not recommend creating one. A redacted blocked-connection log is more useful evidence for an actual network incident.

articles.title: RTrader Pro Plugin Mode: Setup and Platform Limits
articles.description: Set up RTrader Pro Plugin Mode for a supported platform, check both ends of the connection, and understand Sierra Chart and session-limit exceptions.
articles.answer: For a platform that supports the RTrader Pro plugin, start desktop RTrader Pro, enable Allow Plugins before login, then select the matching plugin connection in the other application. Keep RTrader Pro running. Plugin compatibility and data-session entitlement are separate from simply supporting a Rithmic connection.

toc.label: Set up a supported plugin connection
Sierra Chart is an important exception
If the second platform does not connect

articles.body:
Check compatibility first

Question Why it matters
Does this platform/version offer an RTrader plugin? A direct Rithmic connector is not proof of plugin support
Are both apps on the supported host? A local plugin is not automatically a bridge to another PC or cloud service
What sessions has the provider enabled? Market-data and order connections can have different limits
What depends on either application? Closing software can interrupt its locally managed workflow

EdgeClear's Bookmap guide distinguishes market-data and order-session limits. Do not claim that every plugin application shares one universal session or that fees are always avoided.

Set up a supported plugin connection

  1. Read the connection guide for your platform and version. Identify its plugin option before changing the current setup.
  2. Start desktop RTrader Pro with the account's assigned System and Gateway.
  3. Turn on Allow Plugins before login, as described by Rithmic.
  4. Connect RTrader Pro. Keep it running throughout the plugin session.
  5. In the other application, choose its RTrader/plugin connection option rather than an independent direct data login. Quantower's connection guide documents its own configuration.
  6. Check both connection statuses and the expected account/symbol. Verify the separate order route before relying on it.

Do not copy settings such as Aggregated Quotes or Market Data On/Off from an unrelated firm's screenshot. Those values must fit your intended data route and provider entitlement.

Sierra Chart is an important exception

Sierra Chart support states that its Rithmic interface cannot share the same account connection with another application in the scenario it addresses. See the 27 May 2026 support response. Use the Sierra Chart guide, not a generic plugin recipe.

If the second platform does not connect

Check that the plugin host is connected, the second application selected the plugin route, and both use the intended account/System. If connecting the second app disconnects the first, record which connection failed and ask the provider about its session limits. Do not repeatedly restart every application while orders may depend on them.

Captured reference images

The captions distinguish observed web screens from vendor documentation and imported desktop references. None proves a successful order or the unobserved desktop workflow.

Native desktop control location

In the empty Windows login form inspected here, box 2 marks Market Data and Allow Plug-ins [Off]. Orders is separate in box 1. The exact native label is Allow Plug-ins in this build. This proves the control location, not an enabled host/client session.

The local host was not reconfigured and no second trading platform was connected. The documented client control below provides the matching Quantower reference; it is attributed vendor documentation, not a second authenticated session.

Match the client-side setting

In Quantower, open the Rithmic connection settings and use its Use RTrader option for this documented route. The host and client must use the same intended credentials/System. A provider-specific NinjaTrader connector has separate eligibility requirements; see its dedicated guide rather than copying Quantower controls.

faq.q: Can I use the web app as the desktop plugin host?
faq.a: The web controls captured here do not establish that capability. Follow the desktop plugin documentation for this workflow.

faq.q: Does Plugin Mode guarantee identical positions in every window?
faq.a: No. Inspect connection status and refresh/account scope before relying on a display. A second window is not a guarantee of synchronized order management.

faq.q: Does Plugin Mode remove every session limit?
faq.a: No. It does not prove your provider's permitted session count, billing treatment or support for another platform.

faq.q: Is this the same as a cloud automation connection?
faq.a: No. A cloud service's Rithmic route has its own requirements. Do not infer how it coexists with local applications from this local-plugin guide.

articles.title: Rithmic Demo Account: Trial Signup and Access Limits
articles.description: Find Rithmic's official 14-day trial, understand its access limits and distinguish a temporary demo from a provider-issued trading account.
articles.answer: Rithmic advertises a one-time 14-day paper-trading trial with live market data. Start from its official signup link, read the current terms, complete the required forms and use the issued desktop connection details. The public trial is not a funded account and does not include every interface or API.

toc.label: Start at the official trial route
Know the trial limits before choosing it
If the trial does not connect

articles.body:
Start at the official trial route

  1. Open Rithmic's desktop product page and select Free Trial for New Rithmic Users, or follow the official trial signup.
  2. Enter your own details and read the terms and subscriber questions. Do not choose Non-Professional solely to obtain a lower rate.
  3. Keep the activation instructions. Use the exact User ID, password and System issued for this trial, rather than another firm's credentials.
  4. Open the supported desktop platform and complete any remaining agreement requirements.
  5. Confirm the paper account, services and intended contract before testing a workflow. Check that the account is a simulation; the application name alone does not establish this.

No new trial was registered for this library. The authenticated Apex session shown elsewhere belongs to a provider-issued account and is not evidence of the public trial signup result.

Know the trial limits before choosing it

Rithmic's current FAQ, checked 7 October 2026, says the trial lasts 14 days, requires no credit card and expires automatically. It does not offer repeated free trials. It also says the web/mobile apps are unavailable to demo users, and R | Protocol API is unavailable for paper demos that include live market data.

An application requiring Protocol access can therefore have different account requirements from desktop RTrader Pro. A developer test environment and a retail live-data trial are not interchangeable.

If the trial does not connect

Check the activation instructions, exact case of the User ID, System, password and required agreements. Check current maintenance notices if the issue is time-dependent. Ask Rithmic support about the issued trial status if those details match. Do not create successive identities or email addresses to evade the trial limit.

After expiry

Rithmic directs users who want continued service to its sales team for a paid subscription. Obtain current pricing and interface entitlement before paying. A subscription to another trading platform may have separate billing. Trial fills cannot establish what a live account would execute, or prove a strategy profitable.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Is a prop-firm evaluation the same as this trial?
faq.a: No. A firm-issued evaluation has its own account, billing and trading rules even if it uses simulated execution.

faq.q: Can I use the trial in Rithmic mobile?
faq.a: Rithmic’s current public documentation excludes its web/mobile interfaces from demo access.

faq.q: Can I test a Protocol-based webhook service with it?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Rithmic excludes Protocol access from the live-market-data paper demo; confirm the receiving service’s account requirements.

faq.q: Will the trial automatically charge me?
faq.a: Rithmic says its own 14-day trial needs no credit card and expires automatically. Check separate vendor subscriptions independently.

articles.title: Rithmic setup checklist: credentials, data and order readiness
articles.description: Prepare a Rithmic connection with the correct System, agreements, entitlements and platform settings. Check each stage before relying on trading or automation.
articles.answer: Obtain the provider's Rithmic credentials and exact System/Gateway instructions, complete the required agreements accurately, then verify account visibility and market data separately. Configure the chosen platform using its own connection guide. A successful login is one checkpoint, not proof that orders or automated exits are ready.

toc.label: 5. Review account limits and exit management

articles.body:
1. Confirm what the provider issued

Record the Rithmic username, System, permitted gateway, account identifier and account type privately. Do not substitute the provider website password. Do not infer the System from the words evaluation or funded.

Apex's current Rithmic setup guide applies to Apex accounts. Ask another provider for its corresponding instructions rather than copying Apex settings.

2. Choose the supported interface

Use the provider's official download or Rithmic's desktop page for Windows desktop access. Web/mobile eligibility and desktop installation are separate. Confirm your account supports the intended route before relying on it.

After login, verify that the expected account appears. During this review, native desktop login succeeded for Apex/Chicago Area and the Order, RMS, Price and History indicators were green. That observation does not establish another account's entitlements or future availability.

3. Complete agreements and check data

Use the provider's agreement route. Read the subscriber criteria and answer the classification accurately. Do not select a category simply to obtain a lower fee or clear an error.

Confirm the exchange entitlement, data level and selected contract. There is no universal activation delay. If the agreement is complete but data is absent, compare entitlement status, price connection and the product's trading schedule before escalating.

4. Configure the trading platform

Follow the exact platform's direct-connection or plugin workflow. Plugin Mode is not required by every Rithmic-connected application. When a supported connector uses R Trader Pro as a plugin host, follow its instructions for keeping that host running. See the plugin guide.

Verify market data, account/position visibility and order routing as separate stages. Do not treat prices on a chart as proof of trading permission.

5. Review account limits and exit management

Read the provider's current position, margin, loss and session requirements. Distinguish administrator-controlled limits from any trader-configurable tools. A control visible in a template is not proof of a working protective order.

Identify which component manages exits and whether it must remain connected. Use the bracket guide to locate observed controls without assuming universal OCO or disconnect behaviour.

6. Define a permitted validation record

Before any simulation test, confirm the environment and provider permission. Document the intended account, contract, quantity and exit mode. The resulting record should distinguish request acceptance, execution, each exit state and final position. Do not use a live order merely to check that login works.

For TradingView automation, use the current generated payload for the selected connection. PickMyTrade's Rithmic setup documentation supplies route-specific prerequisites; compatibility does not establish firm permission or an executed trade.

Captured interface references

These images show the interface in the stated session. They do not reproduce an error or establish the outcome of an order.

faq.q: How long does setup take?
faq.a: It depends on account activation, agreements, entitlement and platform configuration. No universal completion time has been verified.

faq.q: Does every new account require a new login?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Confirm whether the provider added an account under existing credentials or issued a separate login.

faq.q: Must R Trader Pro stay open for every workflow?
faq.a: No universal rule applies. It depends on whether the selected connector relies on its local plugin host and where order management runs.

faq.q: Is completing this checklist a guarantee of safe execution?
faq.a: No. It separates configuration checkpoints; actual orders require their own acceptance and execution evidence.

articles.title: Rithmic Connection Failed: Diagnose Login and Data
articles.description: Troubleshoot a failed Rithmic connection by separating login, market data and account access. Check System, sessions, logs and provider support safely.
articles.answer: Record the exact error, check the Rithmic credentials and System issued by your provider, then identify whether login, market data or account access failed. If another platform is connected, check its direct or plugin route before opening another data session. A successful RTrader Pro login narrows the investigation; it does not prove that every account can trade or that another application is configured correctly.

toc.label: Start with the symptom you actually see
1. Preserve the error before changing anything
2. Check the issued login and System
3. Separate authentication from data and trading
4. Identify the other application's connection route
5. Check maintenance and the network without guessing

articles.body:
Start with the symptom you actually see

Symptom First useful check What it does not prove
Login rejected Issued credentials, selected System, account status That Rithmic has a general outage
Login stalls or times out Dated provider notices, application log, network reachability Whether the failure is local or at the service
Login succeeds, no quotes Data-session route, exchange entitlement, exact contract That the trading route failed
Quotes update, account missing Provider provisioning and the application's account selector That a chart's data login grants trading access
Second app disconnects the first Simultaneous-session entitlement and connector support That enabling one checkbox fixes every platform
Order rejected Exact rejection and account/risk permissions That changing a password will fix the order

If positions or working orders already exist, first establish which connected interface or provider trade desk can confirm their state. A disconnected display is not evidence that an order was canceled. Avoid repeated submissions while you cannot verify the account.

1. Preserve the error before changing anything

Write down the application and version, the error text, when it occurred including timezone, and the selected System and Gateway. Save relevant log lines. Note whether the problem began after an update, a new account, a password change or opening another platform.

Keep passwords, API tokens and full private account identifiers out of shared screenshots. Give account details only through the provider's official support channel when needed.

2. Check the issued login and System

Your broker or funding provider supplies the Rithmic login. Its website login may be different. Compare the User ID, password and System with the current details it issued; check for accidental spaces and case differences.

The captured native login has separate Orders and Market Data sections. Box 1 contains the order-login controls; box 2 contains data-login controls and Allow Plug-ins. This empty form shows Rithmic 01. It is a reference for finding controls, not the setting prescribed for your account.

For example, Apex's setup guide specifies its own System and describes a data-session choice for that workflow. Do not apply an Apex setting to every provider. The System and Gateway guide explains the difference.

3. Separate authentication from data and trading

When it is appropriate to test a login, use the provider's supported RTrader Pro setup. Preserve an existing working connection before opening a second one. If RTrader Pro connects, inspect the expected account, connection indicators and intended instrument separately.

These indicators were green in an Apex / Chicago Area desktop session on 7 October 2026. They are a useful connection reference. They do not establish your individual account permissions, quote freshness or a successful fill.

For missing quotes, check exchange-data access, any incomplete agreement status and the exact contract. FCM means futures commission merchant; IB means introducing broker. An error asking you to contact the FCM/IB may require the account provider to check permissions.

4. Identify the other application's connection route

Before closing programs, identify whether they manage any local stops, brackets or order actions. Then use the vendor's instructions for the route you intend:

Platform situation Matching guidance
Quantower through RTrader Pro Its documented Use RTrader route requires the plugin host and matching connection details
Quantower direct Its vendor guide describes direct-session restrictions; check what else uses that login
Sierra Chart Follow its documented Rithmic service and same-account limitations; a generic RTrader plugin recipe is insufficient
Another application Confirm support in that version's connection guide before changing settings

Quantower's troubleshooting guide describes agreement, credential, plugin-host and direct-session causes. Sierra Chart support documents a same-account limitation in its connector. Those are scoped instructions, not a universal session count.

5. Check maintenance and the network without guessing

Read current notices from Rithmic and your provider, matching the date, System and affected service. A historical forum outage is not proof of today's status. See how to check an outage.

If no matching incident is confirmed, check whether other network services work and whether the application log shows a license, data or trading connection error. A working website does not test every endpoint a trading app uses. Have the appropriate administrator review firewall or VPN restrictions. Use a narrowly scoped app exception when justified; Microsoft explains the risk of firewall exceptions. Turning protection off is not the default troubleshooting step.

Do not delete caches, reinstall software or change gateways as a first response. These actions can remove useful evidence or interrupt a working route. Follow a vendor-specific instruction only when it matches the recorded problem.

6. Send a useful support report

Include the error and timestamp, software version, System/Gateway, which service failed, whether the account appears, and whether another platform is connected. List the checks already completed. Ask the provider to confirm account activation, exchange entitlement, allowed sessions and any relevant incident. Do not send your password.

PickMyTrade is not a general repair for a failed Rithmic login. If you are diagnosing an automation workflow, investigate the alert, bridge connection and broker response as separate stages in the TradingView connection guide.

faq.q: RTrader Pro works but another platform fails. Is my account definitely fine?
faq.a: The successful login is useful evidence for that session. The second platform can still have a different route, permission, version or data-session problem. Confirm the expected account and service instead of declaring every permission verified.

faq.q: Should I enable plugin mode on every platform?
faq.a: No. Use it only where the current connector supports that workflow. The plugin guide separates compatibility from provider session entitlement.

faq.q: Can an outage remove my position?
faq.a: A connection failure alone does not establish the account's state. Confirm positions and working orders through a connected interface or the provider. Check where any order-management logic runs before relying on it during a disconnect.

faq.q: Does logging in again fix a disabled copier?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The inspected native copier reported that copying was not enabled for the user. Provider entitlement is separate from login; see copier troubleshooting.

articles.title: Rithmic Market Data Connection Failed: Check the Data Route
articles.description: Investigate Rithmic market-data failures by checking issued settings, exchange access, agreements, direct/plugin routing and the provider response.
articles.answer: Check the issued Rithmic login and System, the intended data connection, exchange entitlement and any incomplete agreements. If another application is connected, determine whether it uses a direct session or a supported RTrader plugin. The message alone does not identify the cause and does not establish the status of positions or working orders.

toc.label: Work through the checks in order
Find the separate native data section
If login works but prices are missing

articles.body:
What does FCM/IB mean?

An FCM is a futures commission merchant; an IB is an introducing broker. An error asking you to contact the FCM/IB points toward the account provider's support process. A funding-provider account may have its own route for getting that investigation performed.

Quantower's official issues guide lists several data-login causes. Its list is a diagnostic reference for Quantower, not proof of the cause in your account.

Work through the checks in order

Check What to inspect Useful next step
Credentials/System Issued trading login, exact System, accidental spaces Correct a confirmed mismatch
Direct or plugin Client route and whether the required host is connected Follow the matching vendor setup
Another data session Other apps, computers and allowed entitlement Ask the provider which sessions are enabled
Agreements Account's actual status in the supported agreement interface Review the required agreement and truthful classification
Exchange access Subscription for the exact exchange and depth needed Ask the provider to confirm entitlement
Account status Activation, expiration or disablement Use issuer support rather than reinstalling blindly
Service/network Dated notice and exact connection error Preserve logs and investigate the matching service

Do not invent an activation deadline. A vendor's estimated provisioning time is not a guarantee for every firm or account.

Find the separate native data section

Box 2 marks Market Data, its credential/System fields and Allow Plug-ins in the empty native form. Orders appears separately in box 1. The reference shows both services On and Plug-ins Off, but those values are not prescribed for every workflow.

For example, Apex's setup article describes a data-off arrangement for its stated workflow. Quantower's plugin connection guide describes the required host/client route. Do not combine parts of those different arrangements into a universal recipe.

If login works but prices are missing

Check the exact contract and exchange, quote timestamp and type of data required. Top-of-book quotes and market depth are different access questions. A green data indicator is useful connection evidence but does not prove entitlement for every symbol.

If the failure concerns a plugin client, confirm the host is connected and the client selected that route. Sierra Chart's same-account limitation needs its own guide; its support response should not be replaced by generic plugin advice.

If positions exist, establish them through an available supported account interface or the provider. Missing prices do not prove that trading orders were canceled.

A useful escalation message

Give support the application/version, exact error, timestamp/timezone, System/Gateway, intended exchange/contract, direct/plugin route and what else uses the login. Ask it to confirm agreement status, data entitlement, account activation and simultaneous-session permissions. Omit passwords and remove private identifiers from shared screenshots.

faq.q: Does this error mean I must reinstall the platform?
faq.a: No single cause follows from the message. Check settings, session route and provider access first; reinstall only under matching vendor guidance.

faq.q: Should I select Non-Professional to make the error disappear?
faq.a: Classification must be truthful and meet the applicable requirements. It is not a troubleshooting toggle. See market-data agreements.

faq.q: Does a working chart prove I can trade?
faq.a: No. Check the intended account, order route and permissions separately.

faq.q: Is PickMyTrade a fix for this message?
faq.a: No general fix is established. Its own Rithmic workflow has separate account and connection requirements.

articles.title: Rithmic login failed: credentials, System and FCM checks
articles.description: Check a failed Rithmic login without guessing the System. Separate credentials, account activation and provider-side mapping, and collect useful support evidence.
articles.answer: Use the Rithmic credentials and exact System issued by your broker or prop firm. Check account activation and the complete error message. An FCM or IB-related response can require the provider to check account mapping; it is not solved by assuming every evaluation uses Paper Trading or every funded account uses Rithmic 01.

toc.label: Separate authentication from data and order access

articles.body:
Check the login details

  1. Obtain the Rithmic login from the provider's current account instructions.
  2. Confirm the username and password have no unintended surrounding spaces and that letter case is correct.
  3. Match the System and Gateway to those instructions.
  4. Verify the account is activated for the intended platform or interface.
  5. Record the complete response and timestamp if the login is still rejected.

Apex's Rithmic setup documentation describes its own account route. Do not generalize those settings to another provider. In this review, an authenticated Apex/Chicago Area desktop session was established; the clean web image below is a separate interface reference.

Separate authentication from data and order access

Stage What success establishes What it does not establish
Login accepted This interface accepted the supplied session details Every account and data entitlement is active
Quotes update Data is available for the selected view Orders will be accepted
Account visible The account is returned in this session Permission for every product, quantity or strategy

If the login succeeds but the price connection fails, use the market-data troubleshooting guide. Avoid repeated password changes for an entitlement problem.

FCM and IB-related responses

FCM refers to a futures commission merchant; IB commonly refers to an introducing broker in this context. Preserve the exact error instead of treating a generic phrase as a complete diagnosis. Ask the provider to verify the login's System, account association, activation and permitted route.

Do not invent a broker name, FCM identifier or replacement System in the connection settings. A provider-side restriction may not be repairable inside the trading platform.

Check another open session carefully

Session allowances depend on the interface and provider. Plugin Mode is a supported arrangement for specific connectors, not a universal permission to share every login. Quantower's Rithmic troubleshooting guide explains its connection checks.

Before closing another application, identify whether it manages working exits or automation. A blanket instruction to disconnect every session can interrupt that management.

Captured interface references

These images show the interface in the stated session. They do not reproduce an error or establish the outcome of an order.

faq.q: My provider website login works. Does that prove my Rithmic password works?
faq.a: No. The website and Rithmic credentials can be separate. Use the provider-issued Rithmic details.

faq.q: Should I wait a fixed number of minutes for a new account?
faq.a: No universal activation time is established. Use the provider's status and published activation guidance.

faq.q: Should I update other applications after a password change?
faq.a: Any application using the old Rithmic credential needs its stored connection details updated through its supported process. First confirm the change with the credential issuer.

faq.q: What belongs in a support request?
faq.a: Include provider, platform/version, System/Gateway, exact error and time. Share necessary account details privately; never post the password or token.

articles.title: Rithmic Connection Drops: Find the Failing Service and Route
articles.description: Investigate recurring Rithmic disconnects using timestamps, service logs, session checks and connector-specific guidance without promising a universal fix.
articles.answer: Record when the connection drops and which service fails: orders, real-time prices or historical data. Then compare those timestamps with application logs, provider notices and other connected platforms. Session conflicts, local resource problems and connector-specific behavior need different checks. A frozen chart alone does not prove a full Rithmic outage.

toc.label: Protect your investigation from stale account information

articles.body:
Protect your investigation from stale account information

If a connection drops while positions or orders exist, use an available supported route or the provider to confirm account state. Do not infer cancellation from an empty or disconnected window. Check where your software manages brackets, OCO cancellation or trailing adjustments before restarting it.

OCO means one cancels the other: linked-order management may depend on the particular route. The OCO guide explains why an order's location and its management logic must be checked separately.

Build a short incident log

Record Example of the detail to preserve
Time Exact timestamp and timezone
Application Name, version and active connector
Connection Selected System/Gateway; direct or plugin
Failed service Order, price, history, or the exact logged service
Trigger Second app opened, network change, large history request, or no known trigger
Recovery Automatic retry, manual reconnect, or still disconnected

Examples here are record fields, not a reproduced outage. Preserve nearby log lines and redact credentials or private identifiers before sharing them.

Separate the likely branches

Another platform connects at the same time

Investigate session entitlement and routing before blaming network quality. Quantower's issues guide describes direct-session conflicts and plugin-host dependencies. Sierra Chart support identifies a same-account limitation in its Rithmic interface. Do not close a program that manages orders until you have assessed that dependency.

RTrader Pro is the plugin host

For a supported plugin route, confirm that the host remains running and connected and that the client uses the plugin route. A direct connection is a different setup. Use plugin mode guidance to check both applications and the provider's allowed sessions.

Sierra Chart repeatedly reconnects during symbol/history activity

The official Rithmic service guide describes a specific recurring-disconnect pattern involving symbols that do not match its Rithmic format. It identifies a version-related correction and advises inspecting places that request those symbols. Follow that documented branch when the symptoms match. Do not invent heartbeat settings or apply its diagnosis to every platform.

One computer has trouble and others do not

Compare network availability, application resource use and the exact error. Inspect resource use around the incident rather than asserting CPU overload from a chart pause alone. A working website does not confirm every trading endpoint is reachable. Have the relevant administrator review VPN or firewall restrictions; avoid turning security controls off as a routine step.

Multiple services fail together

Check dated official notices, including which System or component they name. Provider notices can differ from a platform vendor's status. Outage checking explains how to record an uncertainty without calling it a confirmed incident.

Verify recovery in stages

  1. Check that the intended connection reports connected.
  2. Confirm the expected account and refresh its positions and orders through the supported interface.
  3. Check the exact contract and quote timestamps for the data service.
  4. Inspect logs for new errors or repeated retries.
  5. Confirm any locally managed order logic is operating as intended before relying on it.

A green indicator records service status at that moment; it does not prove a fill, every exchange subscription or the absence of future drops.

faq.q: Will a VPS fix recurring disconnections?
faq.a: A VPS changes part of the computer/network environment. It does not establish account entitlement, plugin compatibility or provider availability. Diagnose the failing branch before spending money.

faq.q: Are my orders automatically canceled when the app drops?
faq.a: A disconnect alone does not prove cancellation. Confirm the order state and hosting/management rules for the route.

faq.q: Should I keep retrying every few seconds?
faq.a: Avoid an uncontrolled retry loop. Preserve the first error, follow the platform's supported recovery procedure and ask the provider when repeated failures continue.

faq.q: Why do charts work while trading does not?
faq.a: Prices and account/order access can involve different services or permissions. Check them separately.

articles.title: Rithmic Multiple-Session Errors: Check Data and Trading Routes
articles.description: Diagnose Rithmic simultaneous-login conflicts by identifying direct and plugin routes, provider entitlements and connector-specific limits.
articles.answer: List the applications using the login and identify their market-data and trading routes. Check the provider's allowed sessions for each service. A supported RTrader Pro plugin can share a data connection in some workflows, but it does not remove every session limit or make every connector compatible. Do not repeatedly force logins while another program may manage orders.

toc.label: Understand what a session means here
Sierra Chart is a connector-specific exception

articles.body:
Understand what a session means here

A session is a connection used by a service. Prices, orders and historical data do not necessarily share one limit. Opening two windows inside one application is also different from starting a second independent connection on another computer.

Setup What to confirm
Two direct clients Provider-authorized simultaneous connections and which services each uses
RTrader host plus plugin client Plugin support in both apps, matching login/System, and separate trading-session limits
Same login on desktop and VPS Actual enabled entitlement; local plugin sharing is not automatically remote sharing
Different logins Each login's issued settings and the platform's multi-connection support
Sierra Chart plus another same-account app Sierra Chart's connector-specific restrictions

EdgeClear's Bookmap guide illustrates a configuration with one data connection and several order connections. Treat its numbers as that guide's example, not your login's universal entitlement.

Diagnose a conflict safely

  1. Preserve the exact message, timestamp and which application disconnected.
  2. Inventory connections on all relevant computers, including background software and permitted cloud services.
  3. Identify which application currently manages orders or protective logic. Do not use Task Manager to terminate it simply to clear a session.
  4. Compare the intended direct/plugin route with the vendor's guide and provider entitlement.
  5. When interruption is appropriate, follow the supported disconnect sequence and test one route at a time.
  6. If the conflict persists, give the provider the route inventory and ask which data/order sessions are enabled. Avoid guessing a release delay.

Where plugin mode is relevant

Quantower documents Use RTrader for its plugin workflow. It requires the local host and matching connection details. The inspected native login provides an Allow Plug-ins control in the Market Data section, outlined inside box 2 below; it is Off in this empty reference form.

A visible control does not prove a successful two-platform session. Check plugin setup and limits before changing a running workflow.

Sierra Chart is a connector-specific exception

In the Apex same-account support case, Sierra Chart support identifies a limitation that prevents treating a generic RTrader plugin recipe as the solution. Follow its own Rithmic service guide and provider instructions. “Supports Rithmic” is not equivalent to “supports this plugin arrangement.”

faq.q: Does Rithmic always allow only one connection?
faq.a: Do not generalize a single count to every service and provider. Check which data and trading connections are enabled for the actual login.

faq.q: Can plugin mode remove all extra data fees?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Vendor descriptions of sharing a data connection do not establish your classification, billing or provider entitlement.

faq.q: Will changing gateways clear the session conflict?
faq.a: Not necessarily. A Gateway is an entry point; it does not itself establish an increased allowed session count.

faq.q: Can I use the web app as a local plugin host?
faq.a: The inspected web controls do not establish that. Use a documented desktop host for a supported local-plugin workflow.

articles.title: Rithmic Gateway Selection: Supported Choices and Safe Checks
articles.description: Choose a provider-supported Rithmic gateway, understand the native menu, and compare connection behavior without assuming geography guarantees latency.
articles.answer: Start with a Gateway supported by your provider for the selected System. A geographically nearby entry can be a starting point when the provider recommends it, but its name does not guarantee the lowest latency or solve every connection failure. Keep the working route unchanged while identifying the problem; compare alternatives only when you can safely interrupt the connection.

toc.label: What is available in the inspected menu?

articles.body:
Check the System first

A Gateway is an entry point, not a replacement for the account's assigned environment. Selecting Chicago Area under the wrong System does not establish a valid account connection. Obtain the issued System and supported choices before changing either field.

What is available in the inspected menu?

The unused Rithmic 01 form in desktop version 17.106.0.2 exposed 18 Gateway labels on 7 October 2026, including Chicago Area, Frankfurt, Singapore, Tokyo, US East and US West. The complete observed labels appear in the System and Gateway reference.

This is a Rithmic 01 menu observation. It does not prove that every entry works for Apex or another provider. Labels containing Summary or Colo may describe a different service choice; do not treat them as ordinary regional substitutes without matching instructions.

A safe selection sequence

  1. Record the current System, Gateway, platform version and connection route.
  2. Identify the failure: login rejection, timeout, missing data, delay or missing account. Preserve the error and timestamp.
  3. Check the provider's current guide and dated incident notices. Apex's setup guide recommends a nearby area in its own workflow; that is provider guidance, not a measured best route for every trader.
  4. Before a reconnect, confirm positions and working orders and identify any management performed by local software. Arrange a supported backup route where needed.
  5. If an alternative is supported and the interruption is appropriate, change one connection variable at a time using the matching platform instructions.
  6. Recheck the expected account, service indicators, exact contract and quote timestamp. Preserve both sets of observations so the provider can compare them.

Do not switch a working trading session simply to obtain a screenshot or a speed figure.

Interpret measurements carefully

Observation Useful conclusion Limit
One gateway times out and another connects Different behavior occurred in the recorded attempts Does not identify the root cause
Network ping is lower That host answered that network test faster May not measure the application's actual route
Prices appear delayed A timestamp or display problem warrants investigation Does not isolate gateway, feed, chart or CPU cause
Quotes update after a change Data was visible for that symbol at that time Does not establish trading permission or fills

No comparative latency measurements were performed for this guide. Avoid published millisecond promises without a reproducible measurement and account scope.

faq.q: Is Chicago Area always the best gateway?
faq.a: No. Use a supported choice for your System and workflow. Account availability, network routing and service conditions matter alongside location.

faq.q: Should I change gateways after an invalid-password error?
faq.a: First verify the issued credentials and System. A password rejection and a timeout are different symptoms; changing geography is not a verified password repair.

faq.q: Must Orders and Market Data use identical settings?
faq.a: Follow the provider and connector's supported configuration. The presence of two sections does not authorize an arbitrary mixed environment.

faq.q: Does a gateway change remove a session limit?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Ask the provider which data and trading sessions are enabled for the login; see multiple-session diagnosis.

articles.title: Reconnect to Rithmic and Verify Positions and Working Orders
articles.description: Recover a Rithmic connection using the platform-supported procedure, then check account, positions, orders and automation state before resuming.
articles.answer: Use the reconnect procedure documented for your actual platform, then verify the account, positions, working orders and locally managed actions. A restored connection does not establish that an earlier submission failed, that protective orders remain active or that automation should resume. Avoid duplicate submissions while the order outcome is uncertain.

toc.label: Use the procedure for this application

articles.body:
Before reconnecting

  1. Record the disconnect time, exact error and affected service.
  2. Identify the intended account and the applications connected to it.
  3. Determine whether local software manages any brackets, OCO actions or trailing adjustments.
  4. If a position or pending request may exist, use an available supported route or the provider to confirm it.
  5. Pause new automated submissions through the appropriate supported workflow when needed, keeping order/account controls separate from chart connection controls.

Do not treat a stale local display as an authoritative account record. If the situation cannot be confirmed, use the provider's official urgent-trading procedure.

Use the procedure for this application

Application or route What this guide can establish
Desktop RTrader Pro 17.106.0.2 The inspected File menu exposed Positions, Order History and Fill History; it did not expose a File > Reconnect item in that menu
Sierra Chart Rithmic service Its official guide documents File > Reconnect and a separate Connect to Data Feed command
Supported RTrader plugin client Restore the required host/client connection according to that vendor's sequence
Another platform Check its current connection menu and vendor guide; do not transfer another app's command name

The Sierra Chart guide is documentation for that application. It does not prove desktop RTrader Pro has the same command.

No deliberate disconnect or reconnection was induced for this guide. Use current provider instructions when the visible procedure differs; do not invent a menu item or assume every build behaves identically.

Confirm connection, then account state

Check the following in order:

Check What to verify
Connection Intended System/Gateway and required services
Account Correct account selected; expected access restored
Positions Current contract, side and size confirmed through the supported account view
Working orders Actual remaining orders, quantities and statuses
History Acknowledgements, fills, rejects or cancellations for earlier requests
Automation Host/client status and handling of missed or pending signals

Use Order History and Fill History to investigate an earlier order outcome. If a request was sent before the disconnect, find its recorded outcome before sending another. An acknowledgement and a fill are different events.

Check the protective workflow separately

A working parent order, the creation of its child orders and OCO cancellation are separate functions. Confirm which parts live at the exchange, Rithmic service or local application for your connector. The bracket guide explains these distinctions. Do not infer order survival from a restored green status indicator.

For cloud automation, consult the service's documented handling of an unavailable connection and its own logs. This guide does not establish whether any specific bridge queues, rejects or retries a missed signal.

faq.q: Is File > Reconnect available in every Rithmic application?
faq.a: No universal command was verified. Sierra Chart documents it; the inspected RTrader Pro File menu did not show it. Follow the current instructions for your application.

faq.q: Should I resend the order that was pending when the connection dropped?
faq.a: First confirm its outcome in account/order history or with the provider. Resending an uncertain request can create another order.

faq.q: Does a restored connection prove my stop is active?
faq.a: No. Check the actual working order and the associated management route. A service indicator is not the stop's status.

faq.q: Can I resume alerts as soon as quotes return?
faq.a: First verify account, order and automation state. Quotes alone do not prove that the other services are ready.

articles.title: Rithmic Password Reset: Recover the Correct Trading Login
articles.description: Recover a broker-issued Rithmic password through the right provider, distinguish it from a website login, and update dependent connections carefully.
articles.answer: For a broker or funding-provider Rithmic login, use that provider's official recovery instructions or support channel. First distinguish the Rithmic trading password from your provider website password. The inspected desktop login has no visible Forgot Password control. Do not assume a website password reset also changes the trading login or invent a fixed lockout waiting period.

toc.label: After the provider confirms a new password

articles.body:
Identify which password failed

Login Where you use it Who should confirm recovery
Provider website Account administration or billing dashboard That website's official recovery flow
Rithmic trading login RTrader Pro or a supported Rithmic connector Provider that issued the trading credentials
Platform vendor account Software licensing or platform sign-in Platform vendor
Automation service account Its own dashboard That service's official recovery flow

Apex's login guidance explicitly distinguishes its website login from RTrader credentials. A working website password is therefore not evidence that you entered the correct trading password.

Before requesting a reset

  1. Record the exact rejection. A timeout or unavailable service is not the same as an invalid-password response.
  2. Check the current Rithmic credentials issued by the provider and the selected System. Avoid accidental spaces and case changes.
  3. Confirm that the relevant account is active with the provider. An expired or disabled account may need an account-status investigation instead of a password reset.
  4. If you receive an account-locked or too-many-attempts message, stop repeated retries and use official support. No universal retry interval is established by this guide.

Request recovery from the issuer

Use a support link reached from the provider's official website or authenticated dashboard. State that you need recovery of the Rithmic trading login, and include the error and timestamp. Do not send the current or new password in an ordinary message.

For example, Elite Trader Funding's troubleshooting guide routes forgotten or locked Rithmic logins to its support process. That is an ETF workflow; another provider may use a different portal or administrator. This guide does not claim that no interface anywhere can change a password.

Keep password recovery separate from an evaluation-account reset. An account reset can be a different operation with different terms; do not purchase or request one simply because the word “reset” appears in a login article.

After the provider confirms a new password

Inventory the applications that store that trading login, including separate order/data fields and any permitted automation connection. An old stored password can explain why one application works and another fails.

Before interrupting a working route, confirm the account state and any locally managed order actions. Update the appropriate stored fields according to each application's guide, reconnect when appropriate, and verify the expected account and services. Do not assume that entering the new password in one program updates the others.

faq.q: Does resetting my Apex website password reset Rithmic?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Apex identifies separate trading credentials. Confirm which login its recovery process affects.

faq.q: Is there a universal Rithmic Forgot Password button?
faq.a: No such control was visible in the inspected desktop login. Use the issuer's documented recovery route for the specific login; this observation is not a survey of every Rithmic interface.

faq.q: How long does a lockout last?
faq.a: The reviewed sources do not establish a universal duration. Give the exact message to the issuer and follow its instructions rather than repeating guesses.

faq.q: Can password recovery fix a copier-not-enabled message?
faq.a: A successful login and copier entitlement are different. Ask the provider about the specific restriction; see copy-trading troubleshooting.
