articles.title: Is Rithmic Down? Check Dated Notices and Your Connection
articles.description: Check Rithmic and provider notices, separate a local failure from a confirmed incident, and collect useful evidence without relying on old outage posts.
articles.answer: Check dated notices from Rithmic and your provider, matching the affected System and service to your error. Then compare application logs and local network behavior. One failed login, a stopped chart or a historical forum thread does not prove a current Rithmic-wide outage. This is a checking procedure, not a live status claim.

toc.label: Read connection indicators as scoped evidence

articles.body:
Where to check

  1. Open Rithmic System Advisories and inspect the date and affected environment of a relevant notice. The indexed page identifies maintenance and incident notices; this review did not establish a complete live status dashboard.
  2. Open your broker or funding provider's official help/status channel. Its notice may apply to its accounts, a particular connection or account provisioning.
  3. Check your platform vendor's current notices when only that application's connector fails.
  4. Preserve the exact application error and timestamp, including timezone.

Do not treat the absence of a notice as proof of normal service. An old maintenance notice is not evidence that the same event is happening now.

Compare scope before deciding

Observation What you can say Next check
Current provider notice matches your System and service A documented incident may explain the failure Follow the notice and account-specific support instructions
Other apps and websites also lose connectivity Local/network trouble is plausible Check the network and preserve diagnostic evidence
One app fails while an appropriate RTrader connection works The failure may involve the app, connector, session or permissions Read that platform's logs and connection guide
Prices stop but order service appears connected Data and trading need separate investigation Check the exact contract, timestamp and entitlement
Several traders report a problem A useful research lead Seek a dated official confirmation and match scope

The conclusions are deliberately conditional. Shared symptoms do not identify a root cause by themselves.

Read connection indicators as scoped evidence

The native session captured for this guide was Apex / Chicago Area. Its indicators were green at that moment. That observation does not establish availability for every Rithmic System, exchange, account or later time.

If your app is disconnected, confirm any positions and working orders through an available supported route or your provider. Do not assume they disappeared, remained protected or were canceled solely from a local status change.

Is it scheduled maintenance?

Rithmic’s current FAQ describes approximate routine windows, summarized in the linked maintenance guide. Use a current notice for the environment you actually use. Provider help articles give different maintenance descriptions and may use ambiguous timezone wording. Do not publish one permanent universal window or infer that login availability follows every exchange's trading hours. See weekend maintenance checks.

What to send to support

Provide the application/version, System/Gateway, exact failed service, timestamp/timezone, relevant log lines and whether other connections work. Link the notice you think applies and state why. Exclude passwords and redact private identifiers in shared captures.

Avoid changing risk settings, submitting test trades, accepting agreements or repeatedly switching gateways just to diagnose an outage. Reconnection and account verification are separate tasks, covered in the reconnect guide.

faq.q: Is a Reddit outage post enough to confirm today's problem?
faq.a: No. Record its date and what users reported, then seek a matching official notice. Community reports guide investigation but do not establish current service-wide status.

faq.q: Does an invalid-password response prove every server is online?
faq.a: It means the attempt received that response. It does not test every data, order, history or account service.

faq.q: Should I switch gateways during an incident?
faq.a: Use an alternative only if it is supported for your System and the provider's instructions fit the situation. First assess active orders and local management dependencies.

faq.q: Can a cloud automation bridge bypass the outage?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Check the bridge's actual Rithmic route and documented failure handling. Cloud hosting does not prove the underlying service is available.

articles.title: Rithmic Error Messages: Identify the Failing Step
articles.description: Classify Rithmic errors by login, data, order or account state, preserve the full response and follow the matching troubleshooting guide.
articles.answer: Save the complete error, platform/version, timestamp and selected System before changing anything. Classify whether authentication, market data, order handling or account risk failed. Similar words can describe different stages; one phrase alone does not prove a root cause.

toc.label: Route the symptom to the right check

articles.body:
Route the symptom to the right check

Symptom or message family First useful check Detailed guide
Login / FCM / permission Issued credentials, System, account activation and interface permission Login/FCM
Market data unavailable Agreements, exchange/depth entitlement and direct/plugin route Data connection
Connection lost / reconnecting Preserve order state; inspect logs and advisories Reconnect
Risk rejection Full response and actual configured criterion Risk rejection
Liquidation-only restriction Account mode and provider-authorized clearing process Liquidation only
Insufficient margin Exact product/holding requirement and current exposure Margin rejection
Position limit Existing, pending and proposed signed quantity Position limit
Invalid symbol Root, exchange, dated expiry and receiver format Symbol error
Market closed Product/date/timezone and provider cutoff Closed market
Incomplete history Requested range, service cap and platform history source History
Duplicate request Reconcile original delivery, order and fill before retry Duplicates

These are diagnostic categories, not a claim that every platform displays identical error strings.

Two vendor-documented examples

Sierra Chart's Rithmic service guide documents permission-denied messages both during logon and when accessing an exchange's book. The stage matters: an entitlement error is not proof the password was accepted for every service.

Bookmap's connectivity guide documents inconsistent MBO and delayed-data warnings. Do not treat its Continue option as proof the data remains suitable for an MBO-dependent strategy.

Preserve a useful incident record

Record what happened immediately before the message, the connection route, affected contract, account identifier privately, and whether other accounts or instruments were affected. Keep alert, recipient, order and fill timestamps separate. Redact secrets in public screenshots.

Before retrying an order-related action, inspect positions and outstanding orders. Before closing a local platform, determine whether it manages an active strategy or OCO relationship. Avoid generic fixes such as deleting data, disabling security, repeatedly logging in or clearing a provider restriction without authorization.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Is this every possible Rithmic error?
faq.a: No. It is a diagnostic index with source-grounded examples, not an exhaustive error-code catalogue.

faq.q: Does permission denied prove the password is correct?
faq.a: No. Identify which service and operation returned it.

faq.q: Should I retry a timed-out order?
faq.a: First reconcile whether it was accepted or filled; a repeated action can duplicate exposure.

faq.q: Who should receive the incident details?
faq.a: The issuing provider for credentials/account/risk permission; the platform vendor for its connector/UI behavior, with relevant redacted logs.

articles.title: Rithmic Risk Management Rejected: Find the Failed Check
articles.description: Diagnose a Rithmic risk rejection by checking account limits, quantity, exposure and the complete response before retrying an order.
articles.answer: A risk-management rejection means the submitted order did not pass an account or product check. Preserve the full response, then compare the requested quantity, current exposure, available margin and account mode. The words “risk management” alone do not identify the failed rule.

toc.label: Find the rejection and the affected account

articles.body:
Find the rejection and the affected account

Open File → Order History in R Trader Pro. Use Select Accounts and Select Order Date Range to inspect the relevant account and session. Match the response time to the originating platform or alert log. A rejected replacement does not mean the original order was cancelled; inspect the working-order panel too.

Work through the possible checks

Evidence in the response Next check
Quantity or exposure limit Account/product limit, open position and pending orders
Margin or buying power Provider's current requirement for the exact contract and session
Liquidation-only or administrator restriction Account mode and the provider's release procedure
Price or tick increment Instrument, order type and valid price increment
No detailed reason Ask the provider for its RMS response and applicable rule

RMS means Risk Management System. Rithmic's reference describes checks in the server order path. A platform connection can be green while a new order is rejected.

Resolve the cause before retrying

Compare the actual requested order with the intention. A reversal can require more contracts than a simple exit. An automation multiplier can send a different size from the TradingView position. Correct a confirmed configuration mismatch at its source; do not divide an order to evade a total-position restriction.

If the provider's rule appears inconsistent with the account display, retain both records and ask which check failed. Include the timestamp/timezone, contract, side, quantity, order type and response. Send account identifiers privately and omit passwords or tokens. Retry only after the cause is understood and existing orders are reconciled.

Interface reference

faq.q: Is this always a drawdown breach?
faq.a: No. Quantity, margin, account mode and other validations can produce risk rejections. The complete response matters.

faq.q: Can another platform bypass the rejection?
faq.a: Changing the order source does not remove the account restriction. Rithmic describes risk enforcement as server-side.

faq.q: Should I immediately reduce the quantity?
faq.a: First confirm a quantity check caused the rejection. A smaller order does not fix disabled trading, missing margin or an invalid price.

faq.q: Does rejection prove I have no position?
faq.a: No. An earlier order may have filled, and a rejected modification can leave an original order working.

articles.title: Rithmic liquidation-only restriction: checks and recovery
articles.description: Understand a liquidation-only restriction, verify remaining exposure and account status, and obtain provider guidance before retrying new Rithmic orders.
articles.answer: A liquidation-only restriction generally permits reductions of existing exposure while preventing new exposure. Identify the exact account state and reason with the provider. The message alone does not prove a daily loss breach or establish when normal trading will resume.

toc.label: If an intended exit is rejected

articles.body:
Check the restriction in order

  1. Preserve the complete response and timestamp privately.
  2. Verify the System and account used for the rejected request.
  3. Inspect current positions and working orders; a rejected entry says nothing about an earlier request's result.
  4. Confirm whether the intended request reduces the position or could open or reverse exposure.
  5. Ask the provider for the controlling restriction and permitted recovery procedure.

Do not repeatedly send a new entry, change personal risk settings or buy another evaluation merely to test whether the message disappears.

Where to inspect risk information

The native account menu showed separate liquidation-only entries for FCM, IB and Trader scopes. The first two were disabled in the inspected menu. No liquidation-only command was selected. These entries demonstrate separate scopes, not authority to remove an existing provider restriction.

Rithmic's risk overview describes distinct normal, liquidation-only and administrator-controlled account states. The provider must confirm which state applies to your account and why.

If an intended exit is rejected

Compare the actual account position, side, quantity and working exits. An oversized closing instruction can create new exposure. If the request should reduce exposure but still fails, preserve the exact response and contact the provider's trading or risk support through its established channel.

What the documented state permits

Rithmic’s current FAQ distinguishes post-liquidation states from a Soft Loss Limit that resets after firing. Liquidate Only permits position-reducing orders; Admin Only is an administrator restriction. Request the exact mode and its authorized clearing procedure. No genuine rejection was present in the inspected session, so the screenshot above identifies the relevant control rather than inventing an error.

faq.q: Will reconnecting clear liquidation-only status?
faq.a: Not necessarily. A connection refresh does not remove a provider-controlled account restriction.

faq.q: Does the message mean my evaluation failed?
faq.a: It does not establish that by itself. Ask the provider to identify the cause and the exact account-stage rule.

faq.q: Can I still close a position?
faq.a: That is the intended distinction of liquidation-only access, but each submitted request still needs to reduce the actual exposure and pass applicable checks. Escalate a rejected exit promptly through the provider's support process.

faq.q: Does it clear at the next session?
faq.a: Rithmic’s current FAQ says post-liquidation Liquidate Only and Admin Only modes require manual clearing. The provider must identify the account mode and whether restoration is available for its account-stage rules.

articles.title: Rithmic Insufficient Margin: Check Buying Power and Timing
articles.description: Check a Rithmic insufficient-margin response against usable funds, existing exposure, provider requirements and the applicable trading session.
articles.answer: An insufficient-margin response requires checking the provider’s current margin requirement against the account’s usable funds and existing exposure. Use the exact contract, quantity and time of rejection. A displayed account balance or advertised intraday margin alone is not enough.

toc.label: A calculation example, not a margin quote
Prop-firm balances need a separate interpretation

articles.body:
Distinguish the three amounts

Initial margin is required to establish a futures position. Maintenance margin is the continuing minimum. A broker may also publish a different intraday trading requirement, subject to its own hours and conditions. CME explains the initial and maintenance distinction; your broker supplies the applicable account requirement.

Check the rejected request

  1. Save the response, timestamp and timezone from the order log.
  2. Confirm the contract root and expiry. ES and MES are different products.
  3. Confirm the submitted quantity, including any reversal or copier multiplier.
  4. Compare usable funds with the provider's current requirement. Include the effect of other positions, working orders and fees according to its calculation.
  5. Check whether a session cutoff, scheduled event or temporary margin increase applied.
  6. Ask the provider for the exact shortfall and the rule used if the calculation still differs.

A calculation example, not a margin quote

If a provider confirms that an order needs $1,500 and the account has $1,200 available for that request, the arithmetic shortfall is $300. Those numbers are illustrative. They are not the current ES/MES margin, a deposit recommendation or a guarantee that adding $300 would make an order acceptable. Another check can still reject it.

Prop-firm balances need a separate interpretation

A simulated evaluation's advertised balance is not a cash deposit available to satisfy retail futures margin. The firm may enforce contract limits, drawdown or other rules. Ask whether the rejection arose from its exposure rule or an actual margin calculation. Do not apply a retail broker's margin table to an evaluation by account-size label alone.

Interface reference

faq.q: Does Rithmic set one margin for every broker?
faq.a: No universal retail margin is established here. Use your provider’s current account and product schedule.

faq.q: Will a micro contract always solve it?
faq.a: A micro has different contract economics, but its order must still pass the account’s rules. Verify the exact product and quantity.

faq.q: Why did the same size work earlier?
faq.a: Available funds, positions, time-of-day requirements or provider settings may have changed. Compare the two dated records.

faq.q: Should I deposit funds because of the message?
faq.a: First obtain the provider’s calculation and account status. The message alone does not establish an appropriate funding or trading decision.

related.title: Rithmic Margin Requirements: Broker Limits and Account Checks

articles.title: Rithmic Market Closed Error: Check Contract, Session and Date
articles.description: Check the exact contract, exchange state, holiday hours, timezone and provider cutoff behind a Rithmic market-closed response.
articles.answer: Check the exact instrument’s exchange session and current market state, then compare any earlier provider cutoff. Convert the times using the stated timezone and date. Rithmic login availability does not establish that an exchange is accepting or matching your order.

toc.label: Check the session in this order
If the market should be open

articles.body:
Check the session in this order

  1. Record the rejected order's exact contract, timestamp and timezone.
  2. Open the exchange's product specification and trading-hours calendar for that product.
  3. Check the trade date, weekend or holiday schedule, including early closes.
  4. Check the current market state: open, pre-open, pause or closed.
  5. Compare the broker or prop firm's permitted trading window.
  6. Reconcile existing orders before submitting a fresh request during an eligible period.

CME's trading-hours page is the reference for its exchange calendars. A chart session template can filter visible bars without changing the exchange's actual hours.

“Not trading” has several meanings

The CME market-state reference distinguishes matching from order entry and cancellation. A pre-open can accept some instructions without matching trades. A no-cancel phase imposes different restrictions. Do not infer permitted actions merely from an unmoving last price.

Check Common mismatch
Timezone Local VPS clock compared with a schedule in Chicago or New York time
Date Sunday evening belongs to the next trade date for many futures sessions
Product Applying ES hours to an agricultural or other contract
Expiry An expired instrument compared with the active product schedule
Provider policy A required flat time earlier than the exchange close

If the market should be open

Confirm that the symbol resolved to the intended product and expiry. Save the exact server response and the applicable dated schedule. Ask the provider whether it imposed an account/product restriction or received an exchange state change. Do not solve the discrepancy by changing the VPS clock.

Interface reference

faq.q: Do all Rithmic instruments trade 23 hours a day?
faq.a: No. Trading hours are product and exchange specific, with holidays and other exceptions.

faq.q: Does a green connection mean the market is open?
faq.a: It confirms a service connection, not the instrument’s matching state or your account’s permission.

faq.q: Can I leave a DAY order overnight?
faq.a: DAY expiry follows the applicable session rules. Inspect time-in-force and final order state rather than assuming a calendar-midnight expiry.

faq.q: Is a prop-firm cutoff the same as the exchange close?
faq.a: No. Use both schedules and satisfy the provider’s applicable restriction.

articles.title: Rithmic Invalid Symbol: Check Product, Expiry and Entry Format
articles.description: Diagnose an invalid-symbol response without submitting test orders. Verify product, expiry, exchange and the connector’s actual symbol or mapping fields.
articles.answer: Preserve the exact platform/service error and verify the intended product, expiry, exchange and input format. An unknown identifier, an unsupported instrument and an expired contract are different possibilities. Do not submit repeated orders to find a working spelling; first use the supported data/symbol lookup and current provider instructions.
articles.body:
A diagnostic sequence

  1. Record which application generated the message and whether it failed during lookup, data subscription, payload validation or order submission.
  2. Confirm the intended product, not just a familiar root such as ES.
  3. Confirm the listed expiry month/year and relevant exchange.
  4. Check the format accepted by this interface, including a separate exchange field or dotted notation where documented.
  5. For automation, compare the chart identifier, generator trading symbol and receiver's resolved contract.
  6. Ask the provider about instrument availability or entitlement when the identifier is correct but access still fails.

Use CME month codes and its contract-code explanation as references. A month letter does not establish that every product lists that expiry.

What was actually verified

The native Quote Board accepted ESZ6.CME and displayed ESZ6 / E-Mini S&P 500 quotes after leaving the input cell. It demonstrates one valid lookup in desktop 17.106.0.2, Apex / Chicago Area. No deliberately invalid order or error was generated.

Possible mismatch Useful check
Wrong expiry Current exchange/product reference
Continuous label sent as a specific identifier Connector/bridge mapping rules
Wrong exchange notation Actual input labels and vendor guide
Chart root differs from intended execution product Generator settings and recorded resolved symbol
Correct code, unavailable data Entitlement and provider support

Preserve earlier order outcomes

If a request may already have reached the broker, reconcile its acknowledgement/status before sending a replacement. A client display or payload error does not establish every later processing outcome. See Order History.

faq.q: Does every platform show the same invalid-symbol text?
faq.a: No universal wording was verified. Use the exact observed message instead of a fabricated error catalogue.

faq.q: Is dotted notation required everywhere?
faq.a: No. It was observed in the native lookup and documented for specific connectors. Verify each interface.

faq.q: Does PickMyTrade automatically roll every identifier?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Its documented mapping/roll rules and existing-position responsibilities are separate; verify the current generated configuration.

faq.q: Should I place an order to test the symbol?
faq.a: Start with the supported lookup and provider checks. This guide requires no order simply to obtain evidence.

TradingView to Rithmic Symbol Mapping: Check the Actual Contract

articles.title: Rithmic Position Limit Exceeded: Check Orders and Exposure
articles.description: Resolve a Rithmic position-limit rejection by comparing order size, open exposure, pending orders and provider-defined limits.
articles.answer: Compare the requested size with the account’s order and position limits, including existing exposure and any pending orders counted by the provider. A maximum order size, a directional exposure limit and a maximum open position can be different checks.

toc.label: Why a small-looking request can fail
Fix the mismatch at the source

articles.body:
Reconstruct the intended position

  1. Identify the account and exact contract from the rejected request.
  2. Read the current position from the account, not only the strategy chart.
  3. List working entries and exits, including orders from another platform or copier.
  4. Record the new request's side and quantity.
  5. Inspect File → Trader Dashboard → right-click account → View Risk Parameters and compare the applicable administrator/product limits.
  6. Ask the provider how it combines contracts and working orders when the displayed limit is ambiguous.

Why a small-looking request can fail

Situation What to check
One-contract addition to an existing position Resulting exposure, not just the new order size
Reversal Quantity needed to close the old side and establish the new side
Another working entry Whether the provider reserves exposure for it
Mixed micros and minis Provider weighting, not an assumed 10:1 risk-rule conversion
Different expiries Whether the limit aggregates the product across contracts
Copier The actual follower quantity after multiplier/rounding

Rithmic distinguishes pre-trade quantity limits from liquidation thresholds. A personal stop-loss distance does not increase the permitted contract count.

Fix the mismatch at the source

If a template or automation sent the wrong quantity, correct that configuration after checking existing orders. If the account's assigned limit is wrong, request a provider review. Do not split an instruction into smaller orders to circumvent a total exposure limit. Do not raise a risk limit as an error-message experiment.

For support, include the rejection and the before-request position/working-order state. Ask which exact field rejected the request and how the provider calculated the exposure. Keep private identifiers out of public screenshots.

Interface reference

faq.q: Is the account-size label the maximum buying power?
faq.a: No. The provider sets the applicable product and account limits separately.

faq.q: Can I change the limit in the Trader tab?
faq.a: Only if the account permits that particular control. Administrator restrictions still apply; the inspected Trader view did not expose a general editable maximum-position field.

faq.q: Are ten micros always counted as one mini?
faq.a: Their economic size and a firm’s contract-counting rule are different. Obtain the rule for your account.

faq.q: Can this happen on an exit?
faq.a: An oversized or wrong-side request can increase or reverse exposure. If the request truly reduces exposure and fails, escalate its exact response.

articles.title: Rithmic Connection Lost: Confirm Service and Account State
articles.description: Respond to a Rithmic connection-lost message by recording the failure, confirming account state and checking the supported recovery route.
articles.answer: A connection-lost message means the application reported a lost connection; it does not by itself establish that positions were closed or orders canceled. Record the error and timestamp, identify the affected service, and confirm account state through an available supported route or your provider. Use the recovery procedure for the actual platform.
articles.body:
First response

  1. Record the full message and timestamp with timezone before clearing it.
  2. Identify which application and service failed. A chart, price connection and trading connection are not interchangeable observations.
  3. If orders or positions may exist, establish their current state through a connected account view or the provider's supported procedure.
  4. Identify whether local software manages any bracket, OCO or trailing actions before restarting it.
  5. Review the recorded outcome of an earlier submission before sending it again.

The last step matters when the connection drops between submitting a request and seeing its outcome. Repeating the request is not a safe way to find out what happened.

Interpret the visible state

What you see What it tells you What to check next
Disconnected message This application reported a connection failure Log details and the named service
Frozen chart The display has stopped changing Contract, market hours, data timestamp and data service
Empty positions panel This panel shows no rows Connection/account scope and refreshed account state
Green service indicators Services reported connected at that time Account permissions, orders and quote freshness separately

No disconnect was created to obtain an error screenshot for this article. The observed reference is labeled so it cannot be mistaken for a reproduction of the failure.

Find the correct recovery instructions

For repeated losses, use the connection-drop investigation. It separates session conflicts, plugin dependencies, local/network issues and connector-specific behavior.

The Sierra Chart Rithmic guide documents its own commands and a particular recurring-disconnect pattern. Quantower's issues guide covers its direct/plugin causes. Use the matching branch; do not copy another application's command or diagnosis.

After recovery, verify account, positions, working orders and automation state using the reconnect checklist. Restored prices alone do not complete that check.

Escalate with evidence

Share the exact message, application/version, time, System/Gateway, affected service and any other connected apps. Include relevant redacted logs and the checks already completed. Use the provider's official urgent-trading channel if account state requires immediate confirmation. Do not send passwords.

faq.q: Does connection lost mean my trade was closed?
faq.a: No such conclusion follows from the message. Confirm the current account record.

faq.q: Can my stop still be working?
faq.a: Its state depends on the actual order and route. Check the working-order record and where its management runs; do not infer either survival or cancellation from the disconnect alone.

faq.q: Should I immediately send a replacement order?
faq.a: First verify whether the earlier request was accepted, rejected, filled or canceled. The outcome may be uncertain during a disconnect.

faq.q: Do green indicators prove everything recovered?
faq.a: They are service-status observations. Verify the intended account, data and order/automation state separately.

articles.title: Rithmic Account Disabled: Separate Login from Account Permission
articles.description: Investigate a disabled Rithmic account through the issuing provider. Distinguish connection, account access, risk restrictions and password problems.
articles.answer: Ask the broker or funding provider that issued the account to confirm its status and the reason for the restriction. A disabled account, successful Rithmic login and missing trading permission are different states. Preserve the exact message and account context; reconnecting, changing gateways or resetting a password does not establish that a trading restriction has been removed.

toc.label: If positions or orders may remain

articles.body:
Identify what is actually restricted

Symptom Investigation
Entire login rejected Issued credentials, System, login/account status
Login works, account missing Account provisioning, expiry, removal or application scope
Account visible, new order rejected Exact rejection, permissions and applicable risk restrictions
Only liquidation-related actions allowed Provider restrictions and the actual account state
Copier unavailable Copy-trading entitlement separately from ordinary account access

A green connection indicator does not establish that every account under the login can submit an order. The inspected native session also had a separate copier-not-enabled message, illustrating why access to one feature is not proof of access to another.

Check status through the issuer

  1. Preserve the exact message, timestamp/timezone, platform/version and selected account context.
  2. Review the provider's authenticated account-status information and current rules for that account stage.
  3. Check whether the relevant subscription or account has expired, been removed or reached an applicable restriction. Do not diagnose failure from a label alone.
  4. Ask the issuer to confirm which restriction applies and what official process, if any, restores access.
  5. After a confirmed change, reconnect when appropriate and verify the intended account and permissions through the supported workflow.

Apex's login article includes account expiration in its checks. Quantower's issues guide gives a provider-evaluation interpretation for “Only Admins Can Place Trades.” These are scoped examples. They do not establish one universal reason for all disabled accounts or every occurrence of that text.

If positions or orders may remain

Confirm their state with an available supported interface or the provider. Do not assume disablement flattened the position, canceled all orders or guarantees that an exit action is permitted. Ask the provider which urgent procedure applies to the restricted account.

Risk parameters can explain some restrictions, but their visible fields and actual enforcement are separate. Read risk parameters and liquidation-only access without changing controls to experiment.

Keep recovery operations distinct

A password reset concerns a credential. An evaluation-account reset, reactivation, subscription renewal or permission change can be a different operation. Use the provider's exact wording and terms. Do not buy a reset or new subscription merely because an app cannot log in.

Support needs the error, time, application version, System/Gateway and affected account identity through its official channel. Do not send a password or publish private identifiers in an article screenshot.

faq.q: Can I log in while one account is disabled?
faq.a: The login and individual account permissions are separate checks. Verify which account is affected instead of assuming that login success makes all accounts tradable.

faq.q: Does changing gateways restore a disabled account?
faq.a: No restoration is established by a gateway change. The provider must confirm the account restriction and permitted recovery process.

faq.q: Should I reset the password?
faq.a: Only when credential recovery is the actual problem. See password reset for that separate task.

faq.q: Does disabled always mean a drawdown breach?
faq.a: Do not infer a single cause. Ask the issuer to confirm the account-specific reason and evidence.

articles.title: Rithmic Order Cancelled: Find the Origin and Final State
articles.description: Investigate a cancelled Rithmic order using its full history, reason, time-in-force, market state and any fills before cancellation.
articles.answer: An order marked cancelled needs its full history and cancellation reason checked. A platform label alone cannot tell you whether the exchange, provider, OCO manager or your own application initiated it. Confirm any partial fills and the remaining position before replacing the order.

toc.label: Decide whether any replacement is needed

articles.body:
Collect the order timeline

Open File → Order History, choose the account and date range, and locate the order. Record its original request, changes, fills and final response. Compare Fill History and the current position. Keep the originating platform or automation log so you can identify which component requested cancellation.

Compare possible causes with evidence

Candidate cause Evidence needed
DAY order reached session end Time-in-force and the product's session transition
OCO companion filled Linked order response and cancellation acknowledgement
Provider risk action Provider confirmation and trigger timestamp
Application/user cancellation Originator/application log and request time
Exchange session disconnect control Provider's session-level cancellation record
Product halt or exceptional event Dated exchange notice and exact response

These are diagnostic candidates, not a claim that each event always cancels every order. CME documents Cancel on Disconnect for registered exchange iLink sessions, with GTC/GTD exclusions and other limitations. A lost desktop internet connection is not proof that this mechanism fired.

Decide whether any replacement is needed

First determine the original order's cumulative filled quantity. For an entry, a partial fill may already have created a position. For an exit, another linked order may have closed it. A new full-size order can duplicate or reverse exposure if those events are ignored.

If the cause is unclear, ask the provider for the cancellation origin and reason, not simply whether the account is connected. Attach a redacted timeline with timezone, contract and order type. Do not repeatedly resubmit while the market or account remains restricted.

Interface reference

faq.q: Does cancelled mean nothing filled?
faq.a: No. An order can fill partially before its remaining quantity is cancelled.

faq.q: Does disconnecting RTrader cancel all orders?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Working orders, local OCO logic and exchange-session disconnect controls are separate mechanisms.

faq.q: Can a GTC order still be cancelled?
faq.a: Yes. GTC is a duration instruction, not immunity from a user, broker, exchange or other applicable cancellation.

faq.q: What if the platform and broker disagree?
faq.a: Preserve both timestamps and request the provider’s order and fill records. Reconcile the position before another instruction.

articles.title: Rithmic Data Feed Slow: Compare Contract, Time and Display
articles.description: Investigate delayed Rithmic quotes using the exact contract, source timestamps, session route and resource observations without assuming a single cause.
articles.answer: Confirm the same product/expiry, data source and timestamp before calling a price difference latency. Then inspect connection logs, session routing and resource use around the event. A static chart, a delayed subscription and a busy display are different possibilities. No gateway, VPS or aggregation switch guarantees a faster feed for every workflow.
articles.body:
Compare like with like

Check What to record
Instrument Product, expiry and exchange in both displays
Data Provider, real-time/delayed entitlement and depth needed
Time Quote/event timestamp, timezone and clock context
Display Chart interval, session and any continuous adjustment
Connection Direct/plugin route and competing sessions
Workload CPU/memory/network observations around the delay

The native reference below shows a populated ESZ6 Quote Board at one moment. It is not a side-by-side latency comparison:

A practical investigation

  1. Confirm exchange access and the intended contract, especially around expiry changes.
  2. Preserve the exact symptom and timestamp rather than estimating from memory.
  3. Check whether data alone stalled or another service also disconnected.
  4. Review the connector's direct/plugin setup and allowed sessions.
  5. Measure the local workload when the symptom occurs; do not label high CPU without a measurement.
  6. Compare with an appropriate supported reference during a permitted investigation and send the evidence to the provider.

Quantower's issues guide and Sierra Chart's Rithmic guide describe platform-specific data and history issues. Apply the matching branch, not another platform's diagnosis automatically.

Avoid unmeasured fixes

A geographically nearby gateway can be a supported starting point, but its name is not a benchmark. An aggregation or display setting can also change what information the app displays; confirm its meaning and compatibility before changing it. A network ping does not measure the complete quote-to-screen or order-to-fill path.

If positions exist, identify locally managed actions before reconnecting software. A stale display does not establish that orders were canceled or remain protected.

faq.q: Does a price difference prove Rithmic is slow?
faq.a: First match contract, data source, session and timestamp. The two displays may be showing different information.

faq.q: Is high CPU always the cause?
faq.a: No. Measure it at the relevant time and compare it with the symptom; correlation alone may not establish cause.

faq.q: Should I always change gateways?
faq.a: Use supported choices and a controlled comparison after assessing active workflow dependencies. See gateway selection.

faq.q: Does a faster internet speed test guarantee better trading?
faq.a: No. It tests a particular network route, not the complete account/execution workflow.

articles.title: Rithmic Historical Data Not Loading: Diagnose the Missing Range
articles.description: Troubleshoot missing Rithmic history by checking the contract, date range, history connection, platform log and provider entitlement.
articles.answer: Test one exact contract and a small date range, inspect the history connection and platform log, and check the provider’s history entitlement or download limit. Live quotes can continue while a history request fails. Start with those checks before deleting local data.

toc.label: Check the provider allowance and data source

articles.body:
Establish what is missing

Record the contract, bar type, requested dates, timezone and platform version. Separate a blank chart from missing older bars, incorrect session filtering or absent bid/ask-volume data. Compare one other specific contract; do not use a continuous symbol to assume a particular expiry's history exists.

Try one controlled reload

For Quantower, its Rithmic troubleshooting guide documents right-click chart → Reload history (server) and checking the Event Log. Use a small range. Repeated large downloads can consume the allowance without fixing a permissions problem.

In another platform, use that platform's supported reload procedure. Preserve local data and custom settings before any vendor-directed repair; this guide does not prescribe deleting the NinjaTrader database or cache.

Check the provider allowance and data source

Rithmic's FAQ, checked 7 October 2026, describes historical tick coverage from December 2011 and a 40 GB weekly user limit resetting at noon ET on Sunday. This is a service description, not a promise that every platform exposes every instrument and data type back to that date. Ask the provider to confirm actual usage when a limit is suspected.

For Sierra Chart, its Rithmic service guide separates trading, live-data and history credentials and explains the Denali alternative. Use the instructions for the data source actually selected; do not populate Rithmic data fields if that workflow does not use them.

Distinguish the next action

Observation Next action
One contract/range fails Verify expiry, requested range and session filter
Permission response Provider checks entitlement and credentials for that service
Download allowance confirmed exhausted Reduce future requests and use the confirmed reset time
Same range fails in RTrader too Send both observations to provider; this alone does not prove a server outage
RTrader succeeds, one platform fails Send platform version, settings and its log to that platform's support

Interface reference

faq.q: Why do live prices still update?
faq.a: Live and historical requests are different services. A successful live subscription does not establish that a history request was accepted.

faq.q: Should I reload every chart repeatedly?
faq.a: No. Isolate a small reproducible request and check the response before consuming more download allowance.

faq.q: Must an expired contract have no history?
faq.a: No. Expiry prevents treating it as the active tradable contract, but historical availability is a separate question.

faq.q: Does a gap prove corrupted cache?
faq.a: No. Session filters, permissions, source coverage, request limits and connection failures can also explain a gap.

articles.title: Rithmic Duplicate-Order Warning: Verify the Message and Account
articles.description: Identify which application raised a duplicate warning, distinguish a blocked request from actual extra orders, and check records before retrying.
articles.answer: Identify the application that raised the warning and preserve its exact text. Determine whether it blocked a new request, reported a position-stacking restriction or identified an actual second broker order. No universal native Rithmic “duplicate-order warning” text was verified. Do not dismiss or bypass a message on the assumption that it means only one thing.

toc.label: Do not bypass a restriction by guessing

articles.body:
Check the warning's scope

Question Why it matters
Which application produced it? Chart, bridge and broker messages can differ
Was a request accepted or rejected? A warning is not proof of a broker fill
Are there distinct broker orders? Similar rows may be statuses or partial executions
Was repeated delivery recorded? One trigger can have multiple transport attempts
Is adding to a position permitted/configured? Stacking is different from duplicate delivery

Use the current error information from that actual interface. This article does not fabricate an error screenshot or an exact provider string.

Investigate before retrying

  1. Preserve the message, application version, timestamp and account context.
  2. Check the receiving-service record and any broker response.
  3. Reconcile current position and working orders.
  4. Compare alert-event streams and delivery attempts.
  5. Ask the provider/service about the specific restriction when its meaning remains unclear.

TradingView documents conditional resubmission for certain server responses. Its Pine guide also distinguishes multiple event sources. These are possible investigation branches, not proof of a root cause in your account.

Do not bypass a restriction by guessing

Changing quantity, adding another alert or disabling a stacking control can alter the requested exposure without correcting the initial problem. PickMyTrade's published duplicate-position field is not proof of universal delivery deduplication. Follow its current generated workflow and preserve the record of what was blocked or accepted.

If orders may exist, confirm them before any manual action. The duplicate-order guide gives the complete timeline method. No order, cancellation or duplicate-setting change was performed here.

faq.q: Does the warning mean a second trade already filled?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Determine the recorded broker outcome separately.

faq.q: Does every Rithmic client use the same warning?
faq.a: No universal wording or native control was established. Identify the actual issuer of the message.

faq.q: Should I delete one of two similar history rows?
faq.a: History rows are evidence, not automatically extra working orders. Reconcile their identities and events first.

faq.q: Can a resend be safe because the alert triggered only once?
faq.a: One trigger can have multiple transport attempts under the documented conditions. Verify recipient and broker handling before another send.

articles.title: Rithmic FCM-Related Errors: Connection and Account Checks
articles.description: Check provider-issued credentials, System and account provisioning when Rithmic reports an unavailable FCM or asks you to contact the FCM/IB.
articles.answer: For a message referring to an unavailable FCM or asking you to contact the FCM/IB, preserve the exact wording and verify the provider-issued System and trading credentials. Then ask the account provider to check provisioning, permissions or service availability. Similar-looking messages do not have one verified universal cause.

toc.label: What FCM and IB mean here
Check the connection without guessing servers

articles.body:
What FCM and IB mean here

An FCM is a Futures Commission Merchant; an IB is an Introducing Broker. Rithmic supplies trading infrastructure and is not the broker. In an evaluation, contact the firm that issued your trading login rather than assuming you have a personal funded brokerage account at the clearing firm.

Check the connection without guessing servers

  1. Copy the full error text and note which platform/service reported it.
  2. Compare the selected System and Gateway with your provider's setup instructions.
  3. Confirm you used the trading username, not the website login.
  4. Check the provider dashboard for the account stage and current status.
  5. Inspect required agreements and service indicators in the supported RTrader interface.
  6. Check dated provider/Rithmic advisories before repeating a failed connection.

There is no universal rule that every evaluation uses Rithmic Paper Trading or every funded account uses Rithmic 01. The captured Apex session uses its named System. Use the value issued for your own account.

Distinguish wording from a diagnosis

Quantower documents “Market Data Connection Failed. Please contact the FCM/IB”. It lists several possible connection causes. That message does not by itself prove a clearing-firm outage or a failed evaluation. “FCM not available” in a user report must be matched to the actual platform response before assigning a cause.

Escalate with the useful evidence

Send the issuer the platform/version, System/Gateway, error time and timezone, affected service and whether the supported RTrader login works. Provide the account identifier privately if needed. Ask whether the login is provisioned for the selected System and service. Do not send the password or reset an account just to test the message.

A connection message also cannot establish whether funds are safe, lost or available. Financial/account questions require the provider's records, separately from technical troubleshooting.

Interface reference

faq.q: Should I choose a different FCM in the app?
faq.a: Use only the relationship and System supplied by the account provider. Trial-and-error selection can obscure the real mismatch.

faq.q: Does this prove a Rithmic-wide outage?
faq.a: No. One account or service failure is insufficient; compare current official advisories and provider findings.

faq.q: Can the website work while trading login fails?
faq.a: Yes. The website and trading service can use different credentials and account states.

faq.q: Is waiting a fixed fifteen minutes a guaranteed fix?
faq.a: No. Follow a confirmed activation or maintenance notice, otherwise send the exact failure to the issuer.

articles.title: Rithmic troubleshooting: choose the right diagnostic path
articles.description: Diagnose Rithmic login, data, order and disconnect problems. Use a practical decision table, preserve evidence, and avoid unsafe blanket resets.
articles.answer: Identify the failing stage before changing settings: authentication, market data, order routing or the displayed result. Record the exact message and timestamp, then follow the matching checks below. A successful login does not establish working market data or accepted orders.
articles.body:
Choose the symptom

What you observe Start with Evidence to retain
Login is rejected Credentials, provider-specified System and account activation Exact login response
Login works but quotes do not Data connection, instrument, entitlement and product schedule Affected symbols and timestamps
Quotes update but an order fails Order response, account permission and risk rules Request and response sequence
Connection repeatedly drops Session configuration, network and platform load Disconnect times and component status
Display differs from expected result Account, expiry, filters, fills and timezone Comparable records from each layer

Login or authentication problem

Use the Rithmic credentials issued by the provider and its exact System name. Evaluation, funded and demo labels are not enough to choose a System. Apex's setup guide provides Apex-specific instructions; other providers can differ.

Check for surrounding spaces and whether the account is active. If credentials or account mapping are rejected after those checks, contact the issuing provider. Repeated guesses do not diagnose an FCM or IB association.

Connected but no quotes

Check whether the price connection is active, whether the correct contract is selected, and whether your subscription includes the required exchange and data level. Use the provider's agreement process and accurate subscriber classification. Completed agreements alone do not prove the entitlement is active.

Quantower's Rithmic troubleshooting documentation describes platform-specific data checks. Use the market-data guide for a detailed decision table.

Order rejected or apparently missing

Read the exact response and inspect working orders and fills before retrying. A risk rejection, invalid contract and transport timeout are different problems. A restriction may need provider action and may not reset at the next session.

Use order-rejection checks and order history to build the event record. Do not create another trade solely to test a connection whose account state is uncertain.

Repeated disconnections

Compare the timing with another login, a network interruption, platform load or an announced maintenance window. Timing is a clue, not a root-cause finding. Use the exact connector's direct or plugin instructions; there is no universal one-session rule across all Rithmic interfaces.

The Sierra Chart Rithmic documentation illustrates why connector-specific requirements matter. Do not close a platform that manages local exits without first understanding its role and current orders.

Different prices, quantities or P&L

Match the account, expiry, price basis, session, timezone and data feed. For quantity differences, compare executions and remaining orders. For P&L, distinguish realized and open results and determine whether commissions are included. Similar-looking charts can use different contracts or session settings.

Escalate with a useful record

Include the platform version, provider, System/Gateway, symptom, exact time, relevant settings and redacted response. State which checks succeeded and failed. Keep private account identifiers within the provider's approved support channel.

faq.q: Is there a universal reset procedure?
faq.a: No. Restarting every platform can interrupt local order management and erase useful context. Diagnose the failing stage and follow the platform's recovery procedure.

faq.q: Does a working R Trader Pro login prove another platform is at fault?
faq.a: No. The applications can use different interfaces, entitlements and sessions. It narrows the investigation but does not identify the cause by itself.

faq.q: Should I select Non-Professional to fix data access?
faq.a: Only if you meet the applicable criteria. Subscriber classification is a factual declaration, not a troubleshooting switch.

faq.q: Does this decision table need an error screenshot for every branch?
faq.a: No. It is a diagnostic reference, not a catalogue of reproduced errors. An authentic screenshot helps when reporting your particular error; no error was fabricated for this guide.

articles.title: Rithmic order types: execution conditions and limitations
articles.description: Understand market, limit and stop orders, bracket and OCO arrangements, and trailing stops. Compare execution conditions and limitations with clear examples.
articles.answer: An order type defines when an order becomes eligible for execution and what price conditions apply. Market, limit and stop orders serve different purposes. Brackets, OCO arrangements and trailing stops add instructions for managing orders. Availability and behavior depend on the trading platform, connection, broker and exchange.
articles.body:
Market orders

A market order prioritizes execution without specifying a limit price. The price displayed when an order is submitted may differ from the eventual fill.

CME distinguishes market-limit orders from market orders with protection. The exchange's protection range can restrict execution at extreme prices. A platform label alone does not describe every applicable exchange rule. See CME's explanation of futures order types.

Example. A trader submits an order to buy one ES contract while the displayed offer is 5250.00. The order response and execution report establish whether it was accepted and where it filled. The displayed offer is not a promised execution price.

Key limitation. Liquidity, market conditions and the applicable order rules affect execution. Submission does not establish a complete fill.

Limit orders

A buy limit specifies the highest acceptable purchase price. A sell limit specifies the lowest acceptable sale price. An execution may occur at the limit or at a more favorable price.

Example. A buy limit at 5245.00 permits a purchase at 5245.00 or below. It does not require the market to provide a fill.

Key limitation. Reaching the limit price does not ensure that the entire order executes. Queue position and available quantity matter. NinjaTrader's order-type reference also distinguishes partial fills from complete execution.

Stop orders

A stop introduces a trigger condition. The instructions that become active after that condition is met depend on the order type.

NinjaTrader describes stop-market orders as becoming market orders when triggered. CME documents a stop-with-protection mechanism with a defined execution range. Confirm the mapping used by the specific connection.

Example. For an illustrative long entry at 5250.00, a sell stop at 5245.00 places the trigger five points below entry. That distance is not a maximum possible loss. The eventual execution may differ from the trigger price.

Stop-limit orders

A stop-limit combines a trigger with a limit price. Once activated, the limit controls the acceptable execution price.

Example. A sell stop-limit has a trigger of 5245.00 and a limit of 5244.00. After activation, a fill must satisfy the sell limit. If the market moves below that price without sufficient eligible buying interest, the order can remain unfilled.

Key limitation. Price control can leave a position open. A stop-limit does not guarantee an exit during a sharp move.

Bracket orders

A bracket associates an entry with intended exit orders, commonly a stop and a profit target. The platform determines when those exits are submitted and how their quantities are managed.

For an illustrative entry at 5250.00, a bracket might specify a stop at 5240.00 and a target at 5270.00. These prices describe the configuration, not a recommended trade or a completed result.

After the entry fills, inspect each exit's accepted quantity, price and status. Do not infer that both exits are working simply because a bracket setting was enabled.

Read the bracket-order guide for the observed desktop/web controls and platform-specific dependencies.

OCO arrangements

One-cancels-other, or OCO, links orders through a cancellation instruction. In a typical exit arrangement, execution of one order prompts cancellation of its partner.

A cancellation request and a confirmed cancellation are separate events. Partial fills, timing and the location of the managing software can affect the outcome. Confirm the remaining orders and position after either exit executes.

A bracket includes an entry and associated exits. OCO describes the relationship between linked orders. See the OCO guide for platform-specific considerations.

Trailing stops

A trailing stop adjusts its trigger as the reference price moves favorably. In a simple fixed-distance arrangement, the trigger does not move back when the market reverses. Actual behavior depends on the platform's activation, reference-price and adjustment settings.

Illustrative long-position example

Assume an ES entry at 5250.00 and a trailing distance of 10 points. The table assumes the trailing mechanism is active and each adjustment is accepted.

Market event Illustrative stop level Interpretation
Entry at 5250.00 5240.00 The initial trigger is 10 points below entry.
Reference price rises to 5260.00 5250.00 The trigger reaches the entry price, before costs.
Reference price rises to 5280.00 5270.00 The trigger advances while maintaining the assumed distance.
Reference price returns to 5270.00 5270.00 The stop may activate under the configured trigger rules.

The final row does not establish an execution at 5270.00. Realized profit or loss depends on the actual fill, quantity and trading costs.

Benefits. A trailing mechanism can update the stop without repeated manual adjustments.

Limitations. A normal price retracement may activate the stop. Continued adjustment may also depend on local software remaining connected. NinjaTrader's trailing-stop documentation illustrates why activation and update rules must be checked for the specific implementation.

Read the trailing-stop guide for interface references and platform considerations.

Market-if-touched orders

A market-if-touched, or MIT, instruction activates a market order when its specified trigger condition is met. For example, a buy MIT may use a trigger below the current market price.

An MIT trigger does not set a maximum purchase price. This differs from a buy limit, which defines the highest acceptable execution price.

NinjaTrader documents MIT methods, but that documentation alone does not establish availability through every Rithmic connection. Confirm support with the platform and account provider before relying on this order type.

Comparison of order instructions

Instruction Main purpose Principal limitation
Market Request execution without a specified limit price The fill price and complete execution are uncertain.
Limit Set an acceptable execution price The order may remain unfilled or fill partially.
Stop Activate an order when a trigger condition is met A trigger is not a guaranteed execution price.
Stop-limit Combine activation with a limit price The limit can prevent an exit.
Bracket Associate an entry with intended exits Each exit requires its own accepted state.
OCO Link orders through cancellation logic Cancellation must be confirmed.
Trailing stop Adjust a stop according to configured rules Updates depend on the implementation and connection.
MIT Activate a market order at a specified trigger Trigger price does not control fill price.

Observed web interface

In the inspected R Trader Pro Web session, the second panel under the instrument gear displayed Qty, Cancel After (Sec) and Cancel At. Quantity was set to 1 and both timer switches were off.

The image records visible controls. Timer execution, timezone interpretation and order expiry were not tested. The desktop duration menu is documented separately below.

Observed desktop duration controls

In desktop Order Book, select Order Defaults, then Duration. The inspected menu listed DAY, GTC, IOC and FOK. Availability in this menu is not a guarantee of acceptance for every exchange or account.

Documented platform differences

Platform / connection What the current vendor documentation establishes
NinjaTrader 8 / Rithmic Accepted or working orders are held remotely; OCO management is local to the PC.
Sierra Chart / Rithmic Direct Server-managed OCO is supported; server-managed bracket orders are not supported as of the vendor's current writing.
R Trader Pro desktop The native interface references establish control locations, not a completed execution or disconnect test.

Sources checked 7 October 2026: NinjaTrader's Rithmic-specific order-location section and Sierra Chart's service capabilities. A server-held stop and the software that creates, trails or cancels its companion are different parts of the workflow.

faq.q: Does a stop guarantee that a loss stays within the chosen distance?
faq.a: No. The stop defines a trigger and subsequent order instructions. A price gap, execution restriction or different fill price can produce a larger loss.

faq.q: Can a working order be modified?
faq.a: Supported changes depend on the order and platform. A modification request can arrive after a fill or be rejected. Check the acknowledgement and current order state before relying on the change.

faq.q: What if both OCO orders fill?
faq.a: Reconcile the executions and current position immediately. Do not assume a cancellation succeeded or that a subsequent action has removed the exposure.

faq.q: How do DAY and GTC instructions differ?
faq.a: DAY generally applies to the current trading session. GTC is intended to remain working beyond that session until another termination condition applies. Confirm the broker's session, expiry and cancellation rules for the account.

faq.q: How should automated stop and target instructions be configured?
faq.a: Use the current generated message and documented exit mode for the selected connection. Confirm each resulting order separately. The Rithmic JSON guide explains the distinction between message validation and execution evidence.

articles.title: Rithmic Bracket Orders: Controls and Verification
articles.description: Find R Trader Pro Web bracket controls and check entry, stop and target order states. Understand platform-specific exit handling and untested workflow limits.
articles.answer: A bracket combines an entry with intended stop and target exits. Verify the platform's actual behavior rather than assuming every Rithmic connector sends and manages the same orders. In the inspected R Trader Pro Web session, the bracket panel showed target and stop distances in ticks plus a trailing option. No entry or exit was submitted.

toc.label: Where is the exit logic running?

articles.body:
Locate the observed web controls

  1. Open the instrument in R Trader Pro Web.
  2. Open the gear beside the top-left navigation menu.
  3. Select the third dot at the bottom of the settings panel.
  4. Identify Bracket Target (Ticks), Bracket Stop (Ticks) and Bracket Stop Trailing.

The screenshot shows values of 10 with switches off. Those are observed values, not recommended risk settings. Opening a settings panel does not create a working stop or target. Desktop RTrader Pro and other platforms need their own instructions.

Understand the three separate events

Event Evidence to inspect
Entry request sent The order response for the intended account and contract
Entry fills Filled quantity and price, including partial fills
Exit orders become active Separate stop/target status, quantities, prices and linkage

Do not assume an exit exists simply because a bracket switch was enabled. A rejected child order, mismatched quantity or local dependency needs separate investigation.

Where is the exit logic running?

NinjaTrader's order-location guide distinguishes orders from OCO management. Apex's current NinjaTrader guide specifically warns about local OCO dependency for its Rithmic workflow. Do not transfer behavior from RTrader Pro or another connector to NinjaTrader.

For automated alerts, choose the exit-handling mode documented for your exact route. The PickMyTrade Rithmic strategy guide distinguishes strategy-controlled exits from attached exits and multiple-exit arrangements. Use the current generated configuration for the selected account and exit mode.

A useful before-and-after record

In a permitted simulation, record the selected account/contract and configured exit mode before a test. Afterwards, record the entry response, filled quantity, each exit's accepted state and what happened to the remaining exit when one filled. A screenshot of the settings alone cannot satisfy this check. Do not induce a live disconnect to create evidence.

Captured reference

Find the desktop bracket configuration

  1. Open File, then Order Book.
  2. Select Bracket/OCO.
  3. Select Config in the Brackets area.
  4. Inspect Target Only, Stop Only or Both, then the target/stop tick distances and quantities.
  5. Expand Show more options to locate stop-type, trailing and break-even controls.

Observed in desktop version 17.106.0.2, Apex/Chicago Area, 7 October 2026. No template was saved and no order was submitted. These controls do not establish that protective orders are working.

Documented platform differences

Platform / connection What the current vendor documentation establishes
NinjaTrader 8 / Rithmic Accepted or working orders are held remotely; OCO management is local to the PC.
Sierra Chart / Rithmic Direct Server-managed OCO is supported; server-managed bracket orders are not supported as of the vendor's current writing.
R Trader Pro desktop The native interface references establish control locations, not a completed execution or disconnect test.

Sources checked 7 October 2026: NinjaTrader's Rithmic-specific order-location section and Sierra Chart's service capabilities. A server-held stop and the software that creates, trails or cancels its companion are different parts of the workflow.

faq.q: Does a bracket guarantee a maximum loss?
faq.a: No. A configured exit is not a guaranteed fill price or successful order. Inspect the actual stop type and response.

faq.q: Can I cancel one exit and assume the other stays?
faq.a: Do not assume that behavior. It depends on the platform's linkage and cancellation rules; inspect both orders and the position afterwards.

faq.q: Can I use multiple targets?
faq.a: Only if the selected platform and workflow support it. Verify quantities after partial exits and avoid combining incompatible exit-handling methods.

faq.q: Is the screenshot a completed bracket test?
faq.a: No. The desktop and web screenshots verify visible controls. They are not recordings of filled entries, linked working exits or a disconnect test.

articles.title: Rithmic Stop Loss and Take Profit: Setup Checks
articles.description: Check Rithmic stop-loss and take-profit controls, units, quantities and order responses. Separate configured exits from accepted orders and actual fills.
articles.answer: Use the supported exit workflow for your platform and confirm that the intended orders are actually accepted. The inspected R Trader Pro Web bracket panel exposes target and stop distances in ticks. That establishes the controls, not a guarantee that exits will be placed, linked or filled for every configuration.

toc.label: Match exits to the actual position
TradingView automation requires a separate configuration
After an exit or connection failure

articles.body:
Before configuring exits

Record the account, contract, quantity, entry method, exit order types, units and time-in-force. Separate a trigger price from a guaranteed execution price. Do not use a generic number of ticks from a tutorial as a risk recommendation.

Find the observed web settings

  1. Open the instrument in R Trader Pro Web.
  2. Open the gear near the upper-left navigation menu.
  3. Select the third settings-panel dot.
  4. Locate Bracket Target (Ticks), Bracket Stop (Ticks) and Bracket Stop Trailing.

The captured values of 10 and disabled switches are simply the state observed. No settings were changed and no orders were sent. Use the bracket guide for the evidence still needed to verify execution.

Match exits to the actual position

Check Example of a mismatch to investigate
Account and contract Exit points at another account or expiry
Quantity Remaining stop is larger than the remaining position
Side Exit direction would increase rather than reduce exposure
Price units A price was interpreted as a distance, or vice versa
Order state Rejected or pending request mistaken for a working exit
Linkage An independent order mistaken for an OCO companion

These are inspection questions, not a recipe to place independent orders and link them afterwards. Use only a documented arrangement and verify its responses.

TradingView automation requires a separate configuration

With PickMyTrade, distinguish exits requested by later strategy alerts from attached exits. Do not combine settings merely because the fields have similar names. Generate the payload for the selected Rithmic route and use the JSON checks. Exact stop/target units and behavior need to match the chosen mode.

After an exit or connection failure

Inspect the position and every remaining order. Do not assume the unused target or stop disappeared. The OCO guide explains why the order's location and its cancellation logic can differ. Preserve the relevant response and timestamp before troubleshooting.

Captured reference

Find the desktop bracket configuration

  1. Open File, then Order Book.
  2. Select Bracket/OCO.
  3. Select Config in the Brackets area.
  4. Inspect Target Only, Stop Only or Both, then the target/stop tick distances and quantities.
  5. Expand Show more options to locate stop-type, trailing and break-even controls.

Observed in desktop version 17.106.0.2, Apex/Chicago Area, 7 October 2026. No template was saved and no order was submitted. These controls do not establish that protective orders are working.

Documented platform differences

Platform / connection What the current vendor documentation establishes
NinjaTrader 8 / Rithmic Accepted or working orders are held remotely; OCO management is local to the PC.
Sierra Chart / Rithmic Direct Server-managed OCO is supported; server-managed bracket orders are not supported as of the vendor's current writing.
R Trader Pro desktop The native interface references establish control locations, not a completed execution or disconnect test.

Sources checked 7 October 2026: NinjaTrader's Rithmic-specific order-location section and Sierra Chart's service capabilities. A server-held stop and the software that creates, trails or cancels its companion are different parts of the workflow.

faq.q: Do stop orders cap the loss at the selected price?
faq.a: No guaranteed fill or loss cap is established. Check the stop type and its execution conditions.

faq.q: Does changing the settings panel modify an existing order?
faq.a: Do not assume so. A default setting and an acknowledged order modification are different actions; inspect the actual order response.

faq.q: Must every platform use the web panel's tick units?
faq.a: No. The observed labels apply to that web panel. Other platforms and payload modes require their own unit checks.

faq.q: Is this an end-to-end test of exits?
faq.a: No. It is a guide to observed controls and verification requirements. Account-specific execution behavior should be established in a provider-permitted simulation before relying on it.

articles.title: Rithmic trailing stops: controls, distances and limitations
articles.description: Find trailing-stop controls in R Trader Pro desktop and web. Understand tick distances, activation, stop types and connection-dependent behaviour.
articles.answer: A trailing stop adjusts a stop level using a configured price reference and distance. In R Trader Pro desktop, open Order Book, select Bracket/OCO, choose Config, then expand Show more options. The inspected bracket dialog includes Make Trail By Last Trade Price. This is a configuration control; it does not prove that a stop is working.

toc.label: How does the distance affect the trigger?
Desktop, web and NinjaTrader are different implementations
If the stop does not move as expected

articles.body:
Find the desktop controls

  1. Open File, then Order Book in R Trader Pro.
  2. Confirm the instrument and account before configuring any order.
  3. Select Bracket/OCO, then Config in the Brackets area.
  4. Review the bracket components, target and stop distances, and their quantities.
  5. Expand Show more options. Locate the stop type, Make Trail By Last Trade Price and Move To Break Even.
  6. Check the applicable platform instructions before enabling, saving or using a template. A saved template is not an accepted exit order.

The separate Order Defaults popup also contains Buy Stops Trail By and Sell Stops Trail By. Do not combine separate mechanisms without understanding which one will manage the stop. The inspection did not enable these options or determine their interaction.

How does the distance affect the trigger?

Consider an illustrative long entry at 5250.00 with a fixed trailing distance of 10 points. The example assumes trailing is active and every adjustment is accepted.

Reference-price event Illustrative stop trigger
Entry at 5250.00 5240.00
Reference rises to 5260.00 5250.00
Reference rises to 5280.00 5270.00
Reference falls to 5275.00 Remains 5270.00 under the assumed rule

Activation at 5270.00 would not guarantee an execution at that price. A stop-limit can remain unfilled; a market-style stop follows the execution conditions of its route. Tick distances must be converted using the specific contract's tick size. No trail distance is universally suitable.

Desktop, web and NinjaTrader are different implementations

In the observed web app, the third instrument-settings panel has Bracket Stop (Ticks) and Bracket Stop Trailing. Rithmic's web and mobile product page describes server-side brackets with trailing support. That product statement must not be transferred to every third-party connector.

For NinjaTrader ATM templates, Auto Trail documentation separates the stop offset, profit trigger and adjustment frequency. These determine when a trail starts and how it advances. Consult the platform's connection-specific order-location documentation for hosting; a local algorithm and an accepted remote stop can have different dependencies.

If the stop does not move as expected

  1. Check whether the trailing feature is enabled for this order, rather than only stored in another template.
  2. Check whether its activation threshold has been reached using the configured reference price.
  3. Compare the current accepted stop price with the requested adjustment and any rejection response.
  4. Check whether another strategy or manual action is managing the same stop.
  5. After a connection interruption, reconcile the position and working exit orders before restarting automation.

Record timestamps, version, route, units and order responses for support. Do not deliberately disconnect a live position to investigate hosting.

Evidence boundary

Desktop version 17.106.0.2 was inspected in an authenticated Apex/Chicago Area session on 7 October 2026. The controls and navigation were verified without submitting an order. Active trailing movement, partial fills and disconnect behaviour were not tested.

Additional interface references

These earlier captures provide interface context only; they are not completed-order evidence.

faq.q: Does a trailing stop guarantee a profit?
faq.a: No. A trigger above the entry price is not proof of a profitable fill after slippage and costs.

faq.q: Is trailing the same as moving to break-even?
faq.a: No. Break-even logic moves a stop to a level related to the entry under a defined trigger. Trailing can continue adjusting it as its reference price changes.

faq.q: Will trailing continue when I close the platform?
faq.a: That depends on where the managing logic runs. Check the exact platform and connection; an accepted order and future modifications are separate matters.

faq.q: Does a trailing stop expire during the daily break?
faq.a: Inspect its duration and the exchange's session rules. There is no single expiry time that applies to every futures contract or platform.
