articles.title: Rithmic OCO Orders: Linkage, Hosting and Failure Checks
articles.description: Understand Rithmic OCO linkage, local versus server management, cancellation responses and partial fills. Includes platform-specific documentation cautions.
articles.answer: OCO means one-cancels-other: the intended behavior links orders so that an event on one causes cancellation of another. Where that logic runs depends on the platform and connector. It is not enough to know that both orders use Rithmic. Confirm the order states and cancellation result.

toc.label: Separate order storage from OCO management
Questions to resolve before using an OCO workflow

articles.body:
Separate order storage from OCO management

An order can be accepted remotely while the rule deciding to cancel its companion is handled locally. A disconnected platform may therefore leave an unwanted order active even after the position has changed.

The NinjaTrader order-location guide is organized by connection provider. Apex's NinjaTrader/Rithmic guide warns that its OCO functionality needs the local platform connected. Check your exact connector/version rather than extrapolating from a different broker section.

Questions to resolve before using an OCO workflow

  1. Does the selected account/connector support the intended OCO or bracket arrangement?
  2. Which application or server manages the relationship?
  3. What triggers cancellation: any fill, a full fill, manual cancellation, or another event?
  4. What happens after a partial fill or a change in quantity?
  5. What remains active when the platform disconnects?

Keep the platform's answers with the configuration. Do not create two independent live orders first and hope an unverified menu will link them later. Use only the grouping method documented for your platform.

Verify the outcome

Use a provider-permitted simulation or suitable existing order history. Capture the two order states and their linkage before the triggering event, then the fill and cancellation responses afterwards. Compare final position quantity and all remaining orders. Hide account and order identifiers in shareable images.

If the final state is unclear, stop sending replacement signals while you establish what is actually working. A duplicate request can add exposure instead of repairing the original relationship.

Observed desktop OCO area

Open File, then Order Book, and select Bracket/OCO. The inspected window revealed separate Brackets and One Cancels All areas. Both were disabled. This confirms the location and terminology, not a method for grouping existing working orders.

Documented platform differences

Platform / connection What the current vendor documentation establishes
NinjaTrader 8 / Rithmic Accepted or working orders are held remotely; OCO management is local to the PC.
Sierra Chart / Rithmic Direct Server-managed OCO is supported; server-managed bracket orders are not supported as of the vendor's current writing.
R Trader Pro desktop The native interface references establish control locations, not a completed execution or disconnect test.

Sources checked 7 October 2026: NinjaTrader's Rithmic-specific order-location section and Sierra Chart's service capabilities. A server-held stop and the software that creates, trails or cancels its companion are different parts of the workflow.

faq.q: Does a bracket always mean server-managed OCO?
faq.a: No. A bracket configuration does not establish where its management logic runs.

faq.q: Can both orders fill?
faq.a: Do not treat OCO as an absolute protection against every race or failed cancellation. Inspect responses and the resulting position rather than relying on a label.

faq.q: Does changing one quantity update the other?
faq.a: That is platform-specific. Verify the remaining order quantities after any partial fill or modification.

faq.q: Has manual OCO grouping in desktop RTrader Pro been tested here?
faq.a: No. This guide documents the observed configuration area and vendor-defined dependencies. It does not instruct readers to group existing orders through an unverified menu.

articles.title: Rithmic order rejected: read the reason and check the account
articles.description: Investigate a Rithmic order rejection using the exact response, account rules, contract, price and session. Reconcile order state before sending another request.
articles.answer: Read the exact order response, identify which system issued it, and match it to the account, contract and request. Risk restrictions, permissions, price rules and market state require different checks. A connection timeout is not proof of rejection, so reconcile working orders and fills before retrying.

toc.label: Match the response to the next check

articles.body:
Preserve the evidence first

Record the platform/version, System, account, symbol, exchange, side, quantity, order type, duration and timestamp with timezone. Keep the complete rejection text privately. Redact credentials, account and order identifiers from public screenshots.

R Trader Pro's inspected File menu includes Recent Orders, Order History and Fill History. Review order activity separately from executions. The history guide identifies the actual Fill History controls. No rejection was deliberately produced for this article.

Match the response to the next check

Response category What to inspect Who can resolve a restriction?
Risk or position limit Provider rule, current position, working quantity and requested increase The provider for administrator-controlled limits
Liquidation-only Permitted reducing actions and account status Provider or risk desk
Margin or buying power Current requirement for the product, account and session Broker or provider
Symbol or entitlement Exact expiry, exchange and permitted instruments Platform lookup and provider
Price or tick increment Contract specification, stop/limit relationship and exchange price rules Correct the request within applicable rules
Market state Product schedule, holiday adjustment, halt or account-specific cutoff Exchange information and provider
Authentication or routing Correct System, account mapping and order connection Provider and platform support

These are diagnostic categories, not a verified catalogue of literal Rithmic error strings. Do not change risk settings or buy another evaluation merely because a category seems plausible.

Check the contract and price

Use the platform's instrument lookup. In this desktop inspection, ESZ6.CME resolved to E-Mini S&P 500; that confirms the format in this screen only. A TradingView continuous chart symbol is not interchangeable with every execution symbol or JSON field.

Consult the exchange contract specification for permitted increments and the order-type guide for the difference between stop triggers and limit prices. Do not move a price closer to the market as a generic rejection fix without checking the reason and intended trade.

Before retrying

  1. Establish whether the original request was definitively rejected, remains pending, or has fills.
  2. Correct the identified cause, using the provider's current requirements where applicable.
  3. Confirm the current position and remaining orders.
  4. Recheck account, expiry, side and quantity before a new request.

If the error persists, send the private event record through the provider's support channel. A risk restriction may require administrator action; it is not necessarily cleared by reconnecting or waiting until tomorrow.

faq.q: Was every rejected order stopped before reaching the exchange?
faq.a: Do not infer that from a generic label. Rejections can originate at different stages, including an exchange response. Inspect the originating system and event record.

faq.q: Does a rejection count as a trade?
faq.a: A rejected request is not itself a fill. Provider activity rules, fees and reporting definitions should be checked separately rather than inferred from that distinction.

faq.q: Does liquidation-only always reset the next day?
faq.a: No universal reset is established. Confirm the reason, permitted actions and restoration requirements with the provider.

faq.q: Why did a similar order work on another account?
faq.a: Accounts can differ in permissions, limits, balances, session rules and routing. Compare those settings and the exact responses; do not assume evaluation and funded accounts are equivalent.

articles.title: Rithmic Duplicate Orders: Reconcile Alerts and Broker Records
articles.description: Investigate duplicate orders using alert events, webhook deliveries and broker records. Distinguish resends, scaling and partial fills before changing settings.
articles.answer: Confirm whether there are two distinct broker orders, then compare the alert events, deliveries and receiving-service requests that preceded them. Similar display rows can represent different stages or partial fills. Avoid resending, canceling or changing duplicate-position settings before establishing the actual account state and event timeline.

toc.label: Check possible causes without assuming one
A position-stacking switch is not a delivery guarantee

articles.body:
Build the event timeline

Layer Evidence
Script/alert Event source, alert identity and trigger time
Delivery Each webhook attempt and response
Recipient Each accepted/rejected message and generated request
Broker Distinct order identities, status and fills
Account Current position and remaining working orders

Keep private identifiers in the account investigation; redact them from public examples. Use Order History and Fill History to distinguish order events from execution records.

Check possible causes without assuming one

  1. Determine whether two separately active alerts carry the same intended trade.
  2. Check whether both strategy order-fill and alert() streams actually triggered with trade messages.
  3. Check multiple-account routing and quantity scaling; intentional account requests are not automatically duplicates.
  4. Compare transport attempts with recipient and broker records before attributing a resend.
  5. Separate partial fills or status updates for one order from two distinct orders.

TradingView's alert documentation explains the separate event streams. Selecting both does not necessarily double every trade; the actual script and messages matter.

TradingView can resend certain deliveries

The official resubmission rule covers HTTP 500–599 responses except 504, with resends after five seconds and up to four sends per trigger. This is transport behavior. It does not prove duplicate broker orders in a particular incident or certify the recipient's deduplication.

A position-stacking switch is not a delivery guarantee

PickMyTrade's JSON reference includes a duplicate-position option. Do not rename that option into a universal event-id/idempotency guarantee or assume turning it off resolves every duplicate entry. Use current generator instructions and investigate actual requests.

No duplicate incident was induced or account setting changed for this guide. It provides a reconciliation method, not a certified root cause for a particular account.

What to give support

Provide the redacted timeline, relevant timestamps/timezones, event types, connection/account context and recorded outcomes. Ask it to explain the recipient's actual handling of repeated delivery for the affected version/workflow. Do not blindly cancel one of two rows from an article's example.

faq.q: Do two fills prove two duplicate orders?
faq.a: No. One order can have partial executions. Reconcile order identity, quantity and status.

faq.q: Does TradingView retry every error?
faq.a: No. The documented resubmission rule has specific response conditions. Do not broaden it to every timeout or failure.

faq.q: Does disabling duplicate positions prove idempotency?
faq.a: No. Position-stacking behavior and handling the same delivery twice are different questions.

faq.q: Should I resend when the broker outcome is unknown?
faq.a: First reconcile the account/order record or use the provider's supported investigation process.

articles.title: Market vs limit orders on Rithmic: price and fill trade-offs
articles.description: Compare market and limit orders on Rithmic. Learn how price restrictions, liquidity, partial fills and time-in-force affect the execution outcome.
articles.answer: A market order requests execution without a specified limit price. A limit order sets the highest purchase price or lowest sale price you will accept. Neither submission nor a displayed quote proves a fill. Choose the instruction according to the price restriction and execution conditions you need, then inspect the response.
articles.body:
Compare the instructions

Question Market Limit
Is a limit price specified? No Yes
Can the whole quantity remain unfilled? Yes, depending on acceptance and execution conditions Yes
Can it fill in parts? Yes Yes
What price evidence matters? Actual execution reports Executions must satisfy the applicable limit
What must be checked after submission? Acceptance, fills and remaining quantity Acceptance, fills and remaining working quantity

CME's order-type guide distinguishes market-limit orders and market orders with protection. Confirm how your platform maps its label to the exchange instruction. Do not describe every market order as an immediate, unrestricted fill.

An illustrative buy example

Assume a displayed offer of 5250.00. A market request does not promise that price; the available market may change before execution. A buy limit of 5250.00 restricts acceptable purchases to that level or below, but may remain partly or completely unfilled.

A limit above the current offer can be immediately executable. A limit is therefore not necessarily a resting order. Likewise, a price touching a resting limit does not establish that your order received an allocation. NinjaTrader's order reference explains the distinction between order instructions and their fills.

Check duration separately

Order type and duration answer different questions. Type defines price and trigger conditions; duration controls how long or under what immediate-execution condition the order remains eligible.

In the inspected R Trader Pro desktop Order Book, Order Defaults exposed Duration with DAY, GTC, IOC and FOK. Seeing a choice does not establish its acceptance for every product or route.

Measure slippage consistently

Slippage compares an actual fill with a defined reference. Record whether the reference is the signal price, bid, offer or another timestamped quote. For a buy, a higher execution price than the reference is adverse; for a sell, a lower price is adverse. Use filled quantity to calculate a weighted average if several executions occur.

Do not use a generic table of typical ticks as a forecast. Contract, quantity, time, available liquidity and order instruction all matter. No measured slippage distribution was established in this review.

Before resubmitting an unfilled order

  1. Confirm its latest state and remaining quantity.
  2. Check whether a cancellation or modification is still pending.
  3. Reconcile fills and the current position.
  4. Submit another instruction only after resolving the first request's outcome.

An unfilled limit is not automatically an error, and repeated market requests can create unwanted exposure. An automation tool's HTTP acknowledgement is not an exchange fill.

faq.q: Does a limit order have no slippage?
faq.a: A fill should respect its limit, but it can still differ from an earlier signal or benchmark price. State the benchmark when discussing slippage.

faq.q: Is a stop-limit the same as a limit order?
faq.a: A stop-limit first requires its trigger condition, then applies its limit. It can remain unfilled after activation.

faq.q: Does PickMyTrade always send market orders?
faq.a: Do not assume a universal default. Use the current generated message and documented order mode for the selected connection, then inspect the broker response.

faq.q: Which type is best for every trade?
faq.a: There is no universal choice. A price restriction and an execution request involve different trade-offs; neither removes execution risk.

articles.title: Rithmic flatten controls: scope and confirmation checks
articles.description: Locate observed Rithmic cancel and flatten controls. Check account and instrument scope, reconcile positions and orders, and handle an uncertain response.
articles.answer: Flattening requests the reduction of a position to zero. Do not assume that every flatten button covers all accounts or cancels every working order. In the inspected R Trader Pro web and desktop Order Book, the lower controls include Cancel All and Cncl All & Fltn. Verify the documented scope before using them, then inspect both positions and orders.

toc.label: Separate cancellation from closing a position
Automated close requests need route-specific validation

articles.body:
Locate the observed controls

  1. Open the relevant instrument's Order Book or expanded web instrument view.
  2. Identify the selected account and contract.
  3. Locate Cancel All and Cncl All & Fltn below the price ladder.
  4. Confirm their scope and confirmation flow for the platform/version before activating them.

These steps locate the controls; the inspection did not activate them.

Separate cancellation from closing a position

Intended result Evidence to inspect afterwards
Cancel a working order Final cancellation acknowledgement and any intervening fills
Close a position Executions and current position quantity
Finish an account-wide shutdown Every relevant instrument, working order and signal source

An order can fill before its cancellation completes. A platform that displays zero position can still have an unrelated working order. Disable or pause the source of new signals as appropriate to the documented workflow so that another component does not immediately submit a new entry.

If the result is uncertain

Check the latest server-reported orders, fills and positions before repeating the request. A second full close can create an opposite position if the first close already executed. If you cannot establish the state or cannot reach the order connection, use the provider's published trade-desk or emergency-support procedure.

Keep that procedure accessible before a failure occurs. Record the account and instrument privately and retain the original request time and response for reconciliation. A screenshot of a button does not establish that it worked.

Automated close requests need route-specific validation

Use the current generated message for the intended Rithmic route and exit mode. Confirm whether it addresses one symbol, one account or a larger configured set. An accepted webhook is not an executed close. See the Rithmic JSON validation guide.

Do not copy a generic action field or symbol from an unrelated integration. The PickMyTrade Rithmic JSON documentation is a configuration reference, not proof of a successful close on this account.

Apex's documented per-position route

Apex's current instructions say to open File → Positions, identify the position, then use the red X next to that position. This addresses that position; it is not evidence that every account or working order was cleared.

If there are several instruments or accounts, reconcile each individually. Check the final quantity, intervening fills and outstanding orders after a close request. If a copier is involved, follow its leader/follower shutdown sequence first: an independent follower close can be followed by another copied action.

The desktop controls were inspected without activation. Keep the provider's current failure-handling instructions accessible before trading, and use its stated escalation route if you cannot establish the result.

Captured interface references

These images show the interface in the stated session. They do not reproduce an error or establish the outcome of an order.

faq.q: Does Cancel All close a position?
faq.a: Do not treat cancellation and position closing as equivalent. Check the documented function and the resulting position.

faq.q: Can another device be used during a failure?
faq.a: Only if that account and connection allow it. Session conflicts and local order-management dependencies must be considered; another login is not a guaranteed recovery method.

faq.q: Can a flatten request guarantee a particular exit price?
faq.a: No. Acceptance, market conditions and the actual execution determine the result.

faq.q: Has an account-wide emergency close been tested here?
faq.a: No. This guide establishes observed controls and the provider-documented per-position route. It does not certify a one-click, all-account emergency close.

articles.title: Rithmic order history: find fills and export CSV
articles.description: Find Order History and Fill History in R Trader Pro, select an account and trade dates, locate CSV export, and reconcile missing records.
articles.answer: In R Trader Pro desktop, open File, then Fill History for executions or Order History for order activity. Fill History has an account filter, Trade Date range, Fetch button and an export toolbar menu containing Export As CSV. In NinjaTrader 8, the reporting window is New, then Trade Performance.

toc.label: Find and filter desktop fill history
Orders, fills and positions answer different questions

articles.body:
Find and filter desktop fill history

  1. Open File, then Fill History. The Launch panel also provides a Fill History tile.
  2. Select Showing all accounts if you need to inspect the account filter. Match the provider's account identifier, not just a friendly name.
  3. Choose the required Trade Date range and select Fetch.
  4. Inspect Symbol, Exchange, Fill Size, Fill Price and Fill Time. Note the displayed timezone; this session showed IST.
  5. Open the export toolbar dropdown and select Export As CSV to begin an export. Check the chosen destination and contents before sharing a file.

The captured grid was empty. It verifies the controls and columns, not data retention, an exported file or the account's historical trading activity. A blank grid is not proof that no order was submitted.

Orders, fills and positions answer different questions

Record Question it helps answer
Order activity What was requested, accepted, changed, cancelled or rejected?
Fill history What quantity actually executed and at what price?
Current positions What exposure remains now?
Provider statement What official account charges and totals were reported?

An order can have several fills. Do not count every fill row as a separate entry decision. Compare account, contract, side, timestamps and the available order identifiers when reconciling records.

NinjaTrader 8 uses Trade Performance

The official Trade Performance guide locates the window under the Control Center's New menu. Use its date and account filters to generate the relevant view. Older instructions referring to an Account Performance menu should not be followed as an exact NinjaTrader 8 path.

NinjaTrader reporting has not been captured in this local session. For its current display and export details, follow the linked platform documentation rather than transferring R Trader Pro's toolbar instructions.

If expected fills are missing

  1. Confirm the System, login and account match the original request.
  2. Broaden the trade-date range around a session boundary, keeping the timezone in view.
  3. Confirm that the original event was a fill, not a working, cancelled or rejected order.
  4. Compare the provider statement and the platform that submitted the request.
  5. Ask the provider about history availability if records still disagree. Do not assume an unlimited server retention period.

For automation, retain the alert timestamp and receiving-system response alongside the broker record. An alert log establishes that a signal occurred; it is not a replacement for the execution report.

Additional interface references

These earlier captures provide interface context only; they are not completed-order evidence.

faq.q: Does an empty Fill History mean the account has never traded?
faq.a: No. Filters, date selection, access and available history can affect what is returned.

faq.q: Is a platform CSV an official tax statement?
faq.a: No. Use the official records required for your account and jurisdiction. Platform exports support reconciliation but do not replace the provider's reporting.

faq.q: Can the same order produce several rows?
faq.a: Yes, when it executes in parts. Check filled and remaining quantity rather than treating each row as a new order.

faq.q: What should be removed before sharing a screenshot or CSV?
faq.a: Remove credentials, tokens, names and account or order identifiers unless the intended support channel specifically needs them. Keep a private unmodified copy for your own reconciliation.

articles.title: Rithmic Symbol Format: Verify the Contract and Exchange
articles.description: Read futures month codes and verify symbol entry in the actual Rithmic interface. See a native ESZ6.CME quote lookup and keep alert mapping separate.
articles.answer: Confirm the product, expiry and exchange in the interface that will use the symbol. In the inspected native Quote Board, entering ESZ6.CME in the symbol cell and leaving that cell resolved an ESZ6 / E-Mini S&P 500 quote row. This is a verified lookup for that build and environment, not a universal JSON or platform format.
articles.body:
Read a futures contract code

A contract code commonly combines a product root, expiry-month letter and year. CME's code explanation identifies ES for E-mini S&P 500 and warns that formats vary across platforms. The month-code table includes:

Month Code Month Code
January F July N
February G August Q
March H September U
April J October V
May K November X
June M December Z

Do not construct a contract merely because a month code exists; available expiries vary by product. A single-digit year also needs the current product/date context.

Native quote lookup observed here

  1. Open the desktop Quote Board from the launcher.
  2. Activate an empty Symbol cell in this inspected interface.
  3. Enter the intended contract and exchange in its accepted notation. The observed test used ESZ6.CME.
  4. Leave the cell and verify the resolved description and quote row.
  5. Confirm the product/expiry against current exchange/provider references before using it in a trading workflow.

No order was sent and no front-month selection algorithm was tested. A populated row establishes that this lookup returned quotes, not account permission or a guarantee of future quote availability.

Keep entry formats separate

The native Order Book labels its input Symbol.Exchange, while its Account selector is separate:

Sierra Chart documents its own dotted symbol format. PickMyTrade's generator can have a separate trading-symbol field and mapping rules. Do not insert native dotted notation into every connector or alert payload by assumption.

faq.q: Is ES1! the same text as ESZ6.CME?
faq.a: No. A continuous chart label and a specific contract identifier are different. Confirm the execution contract.

faq.q: Can I always type the dotted format?
faq.a: It worked in the observed native lookup. Use the current instructions for each other interface.

faq.q: Does a valid quote symbol prove I can trade it?
faq.a: No. Trading permissions, account and order route are separate.

faq.q: Is a complete symbol-search dialog verified here?
faq.a: No. This article documents direct cell lookup. It does not invent a search-button location or a complete current expiry list.

The CME month-code table defines these letters; it does not mean every product lists every month. The equity contracts above use the March/June/September/December cycle. ESH7 identifies a March expiry with the year suffix 7; confirm the full expiration date rather than inferring a decade from one digit.

Find contracts outside this table

Use the platform's instrument search and the exchange's current contract specifications for energy, metals, rates, currencies and crypto. Confirm product name, exchange, expiry, multiplier and outright tick increment. Similar roots can represent very different contract sizes. A root-only chart label is not an orderable dated contract.

In the inspected desktop session, Trade → Search Symbol opened fields for symbol, description, exchange, product and expiry. A later broad ES search did not complete during the inspection; the earlier exact ES quote lookup did resolve. Do not infer an empty results grid means an instrument does not exist.

Map an automation separately

A continuous chart such as ES1! requires the receiving service's contract-selection rule. PickMyTrade's rollover documentation distinguishes contract mapping from managing an existing position. Use the current generator's selected instrument; do not append .CME merely because it appears in this reference. Recheck both the chart and routed expiry at rollover.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Is this every Rithmic instrument?
faq.a: No. It is a verified reference for common equity futures plus the lookup method for other products. Your provider controls instrument access.

faq.q: Does ES1! mean ESZ6 forever?
faq.a: No. A continuous chart changes its underlying contract according to its mapping rule.

faq.q: Why is Dow listed under CBOT?
faq.a: MYM and YM are CBOT contracts; the other index products in this table are CME contracts.

faq.q: Does a symbol appearing prove permission to trade?
faq.a: No. Data entitlement, account permission and order acceptance are separate checks.

articles.title: Rithmic Exchange Data Fees: 2026 Reference and Billing Checks
articles.description: Compare CME's January 2026 non-professional data fees and distinguish top-of-book, depth, software charges and your provider's invoice.
articles.answer: Your data bill depends on exchange, subscriber classification, depth level and provider pricing. CME publishes exchange fee schedules, but your broker or firm may bundle or add charges. A free trading platform does not automatically include exchange data.

toc.label: Read your subscription and invoice together

articles.body:
CME non-professional reference, effective January 2026

Subscription Per exchange / device / month Four-exchange bundle / device / month
Top of book $1.55 $4.65
Market depth $12.10 $36.50

Source: CME Group 2026 fee list, checked 7 October 2026. The bundle covers CME, CBOT, NYMEX and COMEX under the applicable terms. These are exchange schedule figures, not a quote for your provider's retail package. Professional and non-display uses have different categories; obtain the applicable current schedule instead of applying these non-professional rates.

Read your subscription and invoice together

Record the exchanges, depth level, classification, number of billable devices/connections, billing month and each provider line item. Ask whether the charge is exchange data, Rithmic access/routing, software, copier or another add-on. An invoice can include several of these without any being a duplicate.

For example, needing ES and YM involves CME and CBOT. Compare the provider's two-exchange quote with its bundle offer and the depth needed by your platform. Do not buy depth solely because a ladder window exists.

Check the actual status panels

In the inspected desktop, File → Agreements & Documents shows agreement status and recorded subscriber classification; File → Market Data Entitlements lists exchange access and depth separately. A previously completed form should not be re-signed simply to obtain a screenshot. Classify yourself accurately under the applicable exchange definitions.

Extra connections and order-only workflows

A plugin route can share a supported RTrader Pro data connection, but this does not establish a universal fee exemption. Ask the provider how your actual direct sessions, devices and routing-only service are billed. Logging out partway through a month does not prove the subscription or next charge was cancelled.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Is Level 2 always included with Rithmic?
faq.a: No. Check the depth entitlement and provider package.

faq.q: Can I select non-professional merely to save money?
faq.a: No. Your classification must match the exchange criteria.

faq.q: Are these my final retail fees?
faq.a: No. Confirm your provider invoice, taxes and separate access/software charges.

faq.q: Does deleting the platform cancel data billing?
faq.a: No. Use the provider subscription process and retain confirmation.

articles.title: Rithmic Contract Rollover: Dates and Checklist
articles.description: Check CME roll dates, contract expiry and alert mappings. Understand why changing a chart symbol does not move an existing position.
articles.answer: Rollover means moving activity from an expiring futures contract to another expiry. Changing a chart or alert symbol does not move an existing position. Check the exchange calendar, the provider deadline and volume in both contracts before updating the entire workflow.
articles.body:
Current equity index reference dates

CME's current customary roll calendar uses the Monday before the third Friday for U.S. equity indexes. It permits participants to roll at other times. Check the dated exchange calendar rather than an older Thursday-based convention.

Expiring quarter CME customary roll Published expiration
June 2026 June 15 June 18
September 2026 September 14 September 18
December 2026 December 14 December 18
March 2027 March 15 March 19
June 2027 June 14 June 18

The June 2026 holiday-adjusted expiration shows why mechanically choosing every third Friday is unsafe. These dates are for the table's U.S. index category, not Nikkei, energy or metals.

Update the workflow

  1. Record open positions and working orders by actual expiry.
  2. Check the next listed contract, exchange calendar and provider's last permitted holding time. Deliverable products can have first-notice and delivery restrictions before final trading ends.
  3. Compare activity in both contracts. Volume migration and expiration are separate events.
  4. Change charts, DOMs and instrument lists deliberately. For example, the next quarterly contract after ESZ6 is ESH7.
  5. Update strategy inputs and regenerate receiving-service configuration where required. Recreate TradingView alerts after changing the saved context they use.
  6. Reconcile remaining old-contract orders and positions independently. A new-contract quote does not prove the old exposure is gone.

Closing and reopening exposure can incur a spread, fees and slippage. The price difference between expiries is not itself a trading profit or a promise of a cost-free roll.

PickMyTrade mapping

PickMyTrade documents its rollover rule. Use its selected exact contract when you need explicit control. A service mapping a continuous symbol for new alerts does not necessarily close or transfer an existing position. Keep the old and new contract identifiers in the reconciliation record.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Is rollover the same as expiration?
faq.a: No. Rollover is a change of exposure or activity; expiration is the contract deadline.

faq.q: Must I use the CME customary date?
faq.a: Your permitted timing also depends on the account provider and strategy. CME allows participants to roll at other times.

faq.q: Can changing a chart close the old position?
faq.a: No. Inspect and manage that exposure separately through the supported workflow.

faq.q: Are energy and metal dates the same?
faq.a: No. Use their product calendars and delivery-related deadlines.

articles.title: Rithmic Depth of Market: Read the Ladder and Check Access
articles.description: Find Rithmic depth controls and check exchange access, depth entitlement and platform display settings before diagnosing missing levels.
articles.answer: A depth-of-market display shows visible resting bid and ask quantities by price. A price ladder alone does not prove depth access. Check the exchange entitlement, the selected dated contract and the platform configuration before diagnosing a blank book.

toc.label: Open the observed desktop Order Book
Top of book, depth and market by order

articles.body:
Open the observed desktop Order Book

In R Trader Pro 17.106.0.2, use File → Order Book and resolve the instrument. The inspected ES Order Book exposed the ladder and order controls. Opening the window is a read-only inspection; clicking a price or trading button can send an order, depending on its configured behavior.

Read the information correctly

Information Meaning
Price row A price increment in the selected instrument
Bid / ask quantity Displayed resting buying / selling interest at that level
Last trade Executed activity, different from resting interest
Volume Executed quantity over the display's specified interval
Own orders Your orders, which require their own server states

Orders can be added or cancelled without trading. Displayed size is not a guarantee of future liquidity or a prediction of direction.

Top of book, depth and market by order

Rithmic's FAQ distinguishes top-of-book and depth access. Bookmap's connection documentation describes its Rithmic MBO support. MBO identifies individual displayed orders; market-by-price aggregates quantity at a level. Neither implies that every provider subscription enables the same data.

The native File → Market Data Entitlements panel below shows enabled data access but blank Market Depth cells. That session therefore does not establish a full-depth entitlement. Do not infer five, ten or unlimited levels merely from the word Rithmic.

Diagnose a blank ladder

Check whether the contract's session is open, its quote timestamps change, and the exchange is enabled. Then compare the subscription's depth permission with the platform connection settings. If top-of-book works but depth does not, ask the provider to check depth entitlement before reinstalling software. Preserve the contract, time, platform version and precise missing columns.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Is every ladder a full order book?
faq.a: No. A ladder can show price rows with only top-of-book data or no depth subscription.

faq.q: Does a large bid guarantee support?
faq.a: No. Displayed orders can change or cancel.

faq.q: Do all platforms use the same click actions?
faq.a: No. Learn the selected platform configuration in permitted simulation before using order-entry cells.

faq.q: Can an API use depth data?
faq.a: A supported API and entitlement can provide depth. A visual DOM and a TradingView webhook are different interfaces.

articles.title: Rithmic Tick Size and Tick Value: Calculation Guide
articles.description: Calculate futures tick value and price movement using the contract multiplier. Compare MES, MNQ, MYM and M2K with worked examples.
articles.answer: Tick size is the minimum price increment for the specified contract and trading mechanism. Tick value is that increment multiplied by the contract multiplier. For outright ES, 0.25 points × $50 per point = $12.50 per tick per contract.

toc.label: Calculate a price distance in dollars
Match the units before entering a value
Verify a contract outside the table

articles.body:
Common equity futures

Product Root Exchange Outright tick Dollars / tick Dollars / point
E-mini S&P 500 ES CME 0.25 12.50 50
Micro S&P 500 MES CME 0.25 1.25 5
E-mini Nasdaq-100 NQ CME 0.25 5.00 20
Micro Nasdaq-100 MNQ CME 0.25 0.50 2
E-mini Dow YM CBOT 1.00 5.00 5
Micro Dow MYM CBOT 1.00 0.50 0.50
E-mini Russell 2000 RTY CME 0.10 5.00 50
Micro Russell 2000 M2K CME 0.10 0.50 5

Source: CME Micro E-mini specifications and size relationship. These are outright futures, not options, spreads or an exhaustive product catalogue.

Calculate a price distance in dollars

  1. Divide the price distance by the tick size.
  2. Multiply by the dollar value of one tick.
  3. Multiply by the number of contracts.
  4. Account separately for commissions, fees and any difference between intended and actual execution prices.

Illustration: a 10-point ES distance is 40 ticks. For two contracts, 40 × $12.50 × 2 = $1,000 before costs. The same 10-point distance for two MES contracts is $100. These are arithmetic examples, not recommended stop distances or maximum-loss guarantees.

Match the units before entering a value

Field asks for Ten-point ES distance would mean
Ticks 40
Points 10
Absolute stop price An actual price derived from entry/side; neither 40 nor 10
Dollars Depends on quantity and the field's per-contract or total definition

The inspected desktop bracket dialog labels tick distances. A webhook generator can use different units or sizing modes. Read its calculation details rather than copying a number between unlike fields.

Verify a contract outside the table

Open the exact exchange contract specification and locate its outright minimum price fluctuation and contract unit. Treasury fractional quotes, FX units, options and spread trades need their own calculation. Do not generalize the micro-to-mini relationship to every product called micro.

Screenshot references

faq.q: What is one NQ point worth?
faq.a: $20 for one NQ contract; $2 for one MNQ contract.

faq.q: Does a 40-tick stop guarantee that loss?
faq.a: No. A trigger can lead to a different fill, and costs are additional.

faq.q: Why do spread ticks differ?
faq.a: The exchange can define a different minimum increment for a spread or execution mechanism. Use the relevant row.

faq.q: Does quantity change tick size?
faq.a: No. Quantity changes the total dollars gained or lost per price move.

articles.title: Futures Trading Hours: Contract, Holiday and Provider Checks
articles.description: Check futures trading hours by contract, holiday and timezone. Compare ES, corn and CME crypto schedules with provider restrictions.
articles.answer: Use the exact contract’s exchange schedule, the date-specific holiday notice and the account provider’s cutoff. Rithmic connection availability is a separate schedule. Do not apply a single Sunday-to-Friday timetable to all futures, especially after CME’s 2026 move to 24/7 cryptocurrency trading.

toc.label: Platform chart sessions are another setting

articles.body:
Regular-session references

Product / category Published reference What to check separately
ES Sunday–Friday, 6 p.m.–5 p.m. ET, with a daily 5–6 p.m. ET break Product halts, holidays and provider cutoff
CBOT corn Overnight 7 p.m.–7:45 a.m. CT and daytime 8:30 a.m.–1:20 p.m. CT Trade date, holiday and last-trading-day changes
CME 24/7 cryptocurrency category Sunday–Saturday, with Saturday 2–4 a.m. CT maintenance Exact listed product and provider access

Sources: ES specifications, corn specifications and CME's current trading-hours page, checked 7 October 2026. The corn times are Central; the ES row is Eastern. These rows are reference categories, not a universal timetable for every related instrument.

Check a particular trading date

  1. Identify the exact futures product and expiry, not a similarly named option or spread.
  2. Read its regular hours and the timezone printed beside them.
  3. Open the CME holiday schedule for the intended date and product group.
  4. Check any instrument-specific halt, price-limit state or final trading time.
  5. Compare your provider's earlier close/holding restrictions.
  6. Check Rithmic's maintenance/advisory notices independently.

A market can be in pre-open while accepting certain instructions without matching trades. An active connection therefore does not prove immediate execution is available.

Platform chart sessions are another setting

RTH/ETH templates determine which bars or statistics a chart displays. They do not change exchange hours or grant overnight permission. A chart can appear blank because of a template even when the instrument is open. U.S. Eastern and Central use daylight-saving rules; convert using the actual date rather than a fixed UTC offset.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Does Rithmic maintenance equal CME closure?
faq.a: No. They are different services and schedules.

faq.q: Does an open market guarantee a webhook fill?
faq.a: No. Delivery, account checks and actual order execution remain separate.

faq.q: Can every Rithmic account trade crypto all weekend?
faq.a: The exchange timetable does not establish account, platform or provider permission.

faq.q: Does RTH mean the only tradable session?
faq.a: No. It is a session definition; available trading depends on the exact contract and account rules.

articles.title: Continuous vs Specific Futures Contracts on Rithmic
articles.description: Separate a continuous chart series from an execution contract. Check expiry, alert context, bridge mapping and existing positions when contracts roll.
articles.answer: A continuous chart joins information across expiries; a specific futures contract identifies one expiry. Do not assume that a continuous chart label is directly accepted by your Rithmic connector or that changing its mapping transfers existing positions. Verify the resolved execution contract, the alert's saved context and the account's existing orders separately.

toc.label: What to confirm for alert automation

articles.body:
Compare the identifiers

Identifier Main use Verification
Continuous chart label Charting across successive expiries Chart provider's roll/adjustment rules
Specific contract One expiry's data or trading route Product, month, year and exchange
Generator trading-symbol field Selects or maps the recipient's intended execution instrument Current service configuration and resolved result

CME explains product/month/year codes. Formats can differ by platform. In this native lookup, ESZ6.CME resolved an ESZ6 quote row:

What to confirm for alert automation

  1. Record the chart symbol and timeframe.
  2. Record the running alert's saved script/input/chart context.
  3. Record the generator's selected trading symbol and documented mapping.
  4. Verify the specific contract resolved by the receiving service.
  5. Reconcile existing positions and orders before changing expiry-related settings.

TradingView's alert documentation states that changed chart inputs/context do not automatically update the saved alert snapshot. Do not assume changing the visible chart updates every active alert.

Read rollover claims in scope

PickMyTrade's rollover article recommends specifying the exact contract and describes its continuous-symbol transition rule. It also states that existing expiry positions remain the user's responsibility. The same document discusses planned improvements and current behavior; do not turn that into a universal guarantee that every product, account and alert automatically rolls correctly.

No continuous mapping or position rollover was executed here. Use the current generated configuration and a suitable permitted verification before relying on a particular mapping route.

faq.q: Does rolling a chart move my position?
faq.a: Do not infer that. Existing positions and orders must be reconciled separately for their specific contracts.

faq.q: Can ES1! be sent to any Rithmic application?
faq.a: No universal support is established. Use the exact connector or bridge's current mapping rules.

faq.q: Why can the chart and broker prices differ?
faq.a: First check that they refer to the same product/expiry, session and data source. Continuous-series adjustments can also affect a comparison.

faq.q: Must I recreate an alert after changing expiry?
faq.a: For a script alert's saved chart/input context, follow TradingView's recreate procedure when that context changes. Also verify the receiving service's separate symbol settings.

articles.title: Micro Futures on Rithmic: Sizes, Symbols and Account Limits
articles.description: Compare MES, MNQ, MYM and M2K contract sizes and tick values, then check account limits and margin independently of the micro label.
articles.answer: MES, MNQ, MYM and M2K are smaller equity-index futures, with one-tenth the dollar multiplier of their corresponding E-mini contracts. Smaller contract size does not guarantee small losses, lower total costs or permission to trade a fixed number of micros on every prop account.
articles.body:
Four common equity micros

Contract Exchange Point value Outright tick Tick value
MES CME $5 0.25 $1.25
MNQ CME $2 0.25 $0.50
MYM CBOT $0.50 1.00 $0.50
M2K CME $5 0.10 $0.50

Source: CME Micro E-mini FAQ. This table covers four established equity micros; other micro energy, metal, FX and crypto products have their own specifications.

Select the actual contract

These equity micros use the quarterly March, June, September and December cycle. For a December 2026 illustration, MESZ6 identifies MES with the Z month and year suffix 6; resolve the full expiry through the platform. Use the exact exchange and format required by your connection. A continuous chart symbol is not a perpetual tradable futures contract.

Calculate exposure and costs

An illustrative 20-point move in one MES contract is $100 before costs. Ten MES have the same aggregate point exposure as one ES, but commission schedules, queue position and order limits need not be identical. Ten separately billed contracts can have materially different transaction costs from one larger contract.

Obtain current intraday/holding margin from the provider. A small advertised margin is not a maximum loss. For prop accounts, use the firm's explicit micro-equivalence and scaling rules; the economic 10:1 multiplier relationship does not automatically define its contract-count policy.

Automating a micro instrument

Select the micro in the receiving service's current generator. Check the routed root, expiry, quantity and exit units. Do not perform a text replacement from ES to MES in an unrelated payload and assume every setting scales correctly. Review the calculated dollars and the destination account limits before a permitted simulation.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Are MES and ES tick sizes different?
faq.a: Both use 0.25 points outright, but MES is $1.25 per tick and ES $12.50.

faq.q: Can I offset ES by buying or selling MES?
faq.a: Do not assume the platform nets them. They are separate contracts with separate positions.

faq.q: Does every firm count ten micros as one mini?
faq.a: No. Read its current account-stage rule.

faq.q: Are micros commission-free?
faq.a: No. Check the actual per-side and round-trip charges.

articles.title: Rithmic risk settings: inspect controls and permissions
articles.description: Locate R Trader Pro risk parameters, distinguish administrator and Trader controls, and check liquidation, quantity limits and lock behavior safely.
articles.answer: Open File, then Trader Dashboard. Right-click the correct account and choose View Risk Parameters. Review the FCM Administrator, IB Administrator and Trader tabs separately. Confirm the intended criterion, its units and the account's permissions before changing a value. A liquidation threshold is not a guaranteed maximum loss or an automatic promise of a trading lock.

toc.label: Liquidation and a trading lock are separate

articles.body:
What was verified

In R Trader Pro desktop 17.106.0.2 on 7 October 2026, File, then Trader Dashboard, then the account's View Risk Parameters command opened separate FCM Administrator, IB Administrator and Trader tabs. Only navigation and labels were inspected. No values were edited, applied or tested by placing an order.

Read the settings by purpose

Question What to inspect
Who controls the rule? The selected administrator or Trader tab
What triggers liquidation? Auto Liquidate, Criteria and Threshold
Does the balance threshold trail? Trailing criterion, maximum minimum balance and open-P&L treatment
Is trading restricted afterward? Separate liquidation-only, disable or lock controls and provider policy
How much can be ordered or held? Account and product quantity/exposure fields where available
Is there a timed restriction? No Trading From/To and Auto Liquidate At, including timezone behavior

The observed administrator view included quantity limits; the observed Trader view did not show an editable maximum-position field. Do not assume all controls are available at all permission levels.

Before changing a value

Record the current tab, criterion, unit, account currency and provider rule. Distinguish a dollar balance floor from a loss amount or percentage. Confirm treatment of open profit and loss, fees, deposits and session boundaries. Editing a value can affect an existing position immediately; DayTraders' guidance specifically cautions that changes can trigger liquidation.

The application displayed a notice that scheduled restriction and liquidation times do not automatically adjust when daylight-saving or standard time changes. Confirm the machine's timezone and the provider's intended schedule. Do not copy a time shown in another trader's screenshot.

Liquidation and a trading lock are separate

The Trader tab contains Liquidate Only On Auto Liquidate and Lock On Auto Liquidate. Rithmic's current FAQ, checked 7 October 2026, explains that a liquidation can leave an account in Liquidate Only or Admin Only, depending on its configuration. Those states require manual clearing; do not expect a new trading day or a platform restart to clear them.

That statement describes the resulting account modes. It does not grant a trader permission to edit administrator settings or establish that the two checkboxes are interchangeable. For a restricted account, ask its provider to identify the active mode and the authorized reset route. A Soft Loss Limit is a different criterion: Rithmic describes it as resetting after it fires, so it must not be treated as a persistent daily lock.

Older guidance saying liquidation alone does not disable trading addresses a different configuration. The useful check is the actual resulting mode, rather than the word “liquidation” by itself.

Read the account display

The blank headroom cells in this capture must not be read as zero or unlimited allowance. Use the configured rule and the provider record when a display does not supply a number.

faq.q: Can Trader settings override the provider's rules?
faq.a: Do not assume they can. Provider-controlled restrictions still apply. Ask the provider to explain the effective rule when tabs contain different criteria or scopes.

faq.q: What values should I enter?
faq.a: There is no universal setting for an account size. This guide explains the controls, not a recommended loss allowance or position size.

faq.q: Does a threshold guarantee the final loss?
faq.a: No. A trigger and a completed exit are different events. Execution and market conditions can cause the final result to differ from the threshold.

faq.q: Were these settings activated for this guide?
faq.a: No. The review inspected the interface without editing risk values or submitting orders.

articles.title: Rithmic auto-liquidation: triggers, status and recovery
articles.description: Understand Rithmic auto-liquidation, check the trigger and resulting account state, and distinguish a completed exit from a trading restriction.
articles.answer: Auto-liquidation is a configured response to an account risk condition. Check which criterion triggered, whether closing orders completed, and what account status followed. Do not assume every event cancels every order, permanently disables the account, or clears at the next session.

toc.label: Liquidation and a trading lock are separate
Do not infer the cause from the final balance alone

articles.body:
Reconstruct the event

  1. Record the event time and timezone, System and account privately.
  2. Review current positions and working orders before sending another instruction.
  3. Compare Order History and Fill History to distinguish requests from completed executions.
  4. Inspect the provider's effective risk settings and any trigger-status information.
  5. Ask the provider to confirm the trigger and restoration process if the account remains restricted.

An automated alert or connected platform cannot remove an administrator restriction. Repeated retries can obscure the evidence and do not establish recovery.

What was verified

In R Trader Pro desktop 17.106.0.2 on 7 October 2026, File, then Trader Dashboard, then the account's View Risk Parameters command opened separate FCM Administrator, IB Administrator and Trader tabs. Only navigation and labels were inspected. No values were edited, applied or tested by placing an order.

Rithmic describes its risk controls as server-based, including liquidation triggers and distinct account states. That design does not guarantee an exit price, a specific time to completion, or the availability of every setting to an individual trader.

Older guidance saying liquidation alone does not disable trading addresses a different configuration. The useful check is the actual resulting mode, rather than the word “liquidation” by itself.

Do not infer the cause from the final balance alone

The final balance may reflect fills, fees and market movement after the triggering condition. A profitable closed trade does not rule out an earlier intraday drawdown condition. Ask for the exact trigger value and time rather than estimating them from the ending balance.

Read the account display

The blank headroom cells in this capture must not be read as zero or unlimited allowance. Use the configured rule and the provider record when a display does not supply a number.

faq.q: Will restarting R Trader Pro unlock the account?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Restarting a display does not establish that a provider-controlled restriction has been cleared.

faq.q: Is auto-liquidation the same as a stop loss?
faq.a: No. An account risk condition and an order's stop trigger operate at different scopes. Review both the account rules and the order instructions.

faq.q: Can a liquidation exceed the configured loss amount?
faq.a: Yes, a threshold is not a guaranteed execution price or final account result. Confirm actual fills and remaining exposure.

faq.q: Does the restriction always reset tomorrow?
faq.a: Rithmic says post-liquidation Liquidate Only and Admin Only modes require manual clearing. Ask the provider which mode was set; a Soft Loss Limit and a provider session rule are separate cases.

articles.title: Rithmic position limits: quantity, exposure and permissions
articles.description: Check Rithmic account and product quantity limits, distinguish order size from position exposure, and identify who can change the effective restriction.
articles.answer: Inspect account and product limits in View Risk Parameters, then confirm their meaning and edit permissions with the provider. A maximum order quantity is not necessarily the same as a maximum open position. The inspected Trader tab did not provide a general editable maximum-position field.

toc.label: Check the requested change in exposure

articles.body:
What was verified

In R Trader Pro desktop 17.106.0.2 on 7 October 2026, File, then Trader Dashboard, then the account's View Risk Parameters command opened separate FCM Administrator, IB Administrator and Trader tabs. Only navigation and labels were inspected. No values were edited, applied or tested by placing an order.

Distinguish the limits

Label observed in the administrator view Question to resolve
Buy Limit and Sell Limit Are these directional account limits or product limits?
Max Order Qty What quantity is allowed in one request, including reversals?
Total Exposure Which positions and pending instructions contribute?
Cumulative Position Limit How are products aggregated for this account?

The presence of a label does not establish its unit, aggregation rule or whether a blank value means no restriction. Ask the provider about the effective rule before relying on a number.

Investigate a position-limit rejection

  1. Preserve the exact response and the account, contract, side and quantity of the request.
  2. Inspect both the current position and working orders that could increase exposure.
  3. Check account-level and product-level restrictions separately.
  4. Confirm how the provider counts micros, minis and multiple expiries.
  5. Ask the provider who may change the limit. Do not split an order into smaller requests to bypass an intended exposure restriction.

Optimus support's historical discussion distinguishes broker-side controls from permission-dependent trader functionality. Its examples are not current limits for this or another prop-firm account.

Check the requested change in exposure

Write down the current position, the pending orders and the new instruction separately. For example, selling three contracts while long one is a different request from selling one to exit. This is arithmetic for understanding the request, not an assertion that a provider will accept it.

Rithmic's risk reference distinguishes quantity checks before order acceptance from liquidation criteria. The provider defines product aggregation and any mini/micro weighting. Record its rule instead of copying a numeric acceptance example from another account.

faq.q: Can I set my own maximum number of contracts?
faq.a: Availability depends on the account and permissions. It was not available as a general maximum-position field in the Trader view inspected here. Ask the provider about a supported personal limit.

faq.q: Do ten micros always equal one mini for risk limits?
faq.a: No universal conversion was verified. Contract economics and a provider's exposure-counting rule are separate matters.

faq.q: Does a reducing order always pass?
faq.a: Do not assume that. The actual request, resulting exposure, account state and other checks still matter. Preserve its exact rejection if it fails.

faq.q: Will automation override these limits?
faq.a: A different order source does not establish permission to exceed an account restriction. Reconcile any automation response with Rithmic's order record.

articles.title: Rithmic daily loss limits: calculation and reset checks
articles.description: Check what a Rithmic loss limit measures, how it differs from drawdown, and which provider rules govern fees, open P&L, reset time and account locks.
articles.answer: Confirm the loss calculation, trading-session boundary and post-trigger behavior with your provider before setting a Rithmic loss threshold. A field named Loss Limit alone does not establish which fees or open positions are included, when it resets, or whether it blocks further trading.

toc.label: Define the rule before entering a number
Liquidation and a trading lock are separate

articles.body:
Define the rule before entering a number

Detail What to confirm
Measurement Realized loss, open P&L, fees and the reference balance
Unit Currency amount, percentage or balance floor
Period Session start and end, timezone and holiday treatment
Response Liquidation, order restriction, alert or another provider action
Recovery Automatic release, administrator approval or account failure

A daily loss allowance and a trailing balance floor answer different questions. One concerns the specified session's loss; the other may depend on an earlier account peak. A remaining daily allowance does not mean the account is safely above its drawdown floor.

What was verified

In R Trader Pro desktop 17.106.0.2 on 7 October 2026, File, then Trader Dashboard, then the account's View Risk Parameters command opened separate FCM Administrator, IB Administrator and Trader tabs. Only navigation and labels were inspected. No values were edited, applied or tested by placing an order.

Compare the selected criterion with the provider's current rule for the exact plan and account stage. Keep a private record of the original configuration. A value that appears suitable for another account may use a different basis or produce an immediate trigger here.

Liquidation and a trading lock are separate

The Trader tab contains Liquidate Only On Auto Liquidate and Lock On Auto Liquidate. Rithmic's current FAQ, checked 7 October 2026, explains that a liquidation can leave an account in Liquidate Only or Admin Only, depending on its configuration. Older guidance saying liquidation alone does not disable trading addresses a different configuration. The useful check is the actual resulting mode, rather than the word “liquidation” by itself.

A documented AMP workflow

AMP's Rithmic-support instructions, updated 27 August 2025, use Multiple Simultaneous Criteria with a Loss Limit and a separate liquidation-only flag. AMP says this flag needs manual reset rather than automatically releasing on the next trading day. This is a documented workflow, not confirmation of permissions or reset behavior on the inspected Apex account. The separate Lock On Auto Liquidate control was not activation-tested.

Reconcile a disputed daily result

Use the provider's session dates and timezone when comparing fills, fees and account records. List the components included in the rule. If the result differs from a chart's P&L, check whether the chart shows only one strategy or contract while the account includes other activity. Ask for the provider's calculation rather than changing a threshold to make the display match.

Read the account display

The blank headroom cells in this capture must not be read as zero or unlimited allowance. Use the configured rule and the provider record when a display does not supply a number.

faq.q: Does every limit reset at the CME maintenance break?
faq.a: No universal reset was established. Exchange hours and an account's risk-session rules are different specifications.

faq.q: Does the limit include unrealized losses?
faq.a: Confirm the selected criterion and provider calculation. Do not infer this from the label alone.

faq.q: Does a personal limit guarantee I cannot breach the firm's rule?
faq.a: No. Calculation differences and execution after a trigger can produce a different outcome. A personal limit is not a guarantee of account eligibility.

faq.q: Is there a recommended percentage for all accounts?
faq.a: No. Account label size alone does not determine a suitable risk setting, and this guide does not prescribe one.

articles.title: Rithmic Margin Requirements: Broker Limits and Account Checks
articles.description: Find the applicable futures margin requirement and distinguish exchange margin, broker intraday rates and prop-firm risk limits.
articles.answer: Rithmic applies the risk configuration supplied for the account; it is not a universal margin-price list. Check the broker or firm for the exact instrument, quantity, holding period and current requirement. An advertised account size is not necessarily spendable collateral.

toc.label: Before estimating how many contracts fit
Inspect the account without inventing fields

articles.body:
Distinguish the requirements

Requirement Practical meaning
Initial margin Collateral required to establish the relevant exposure
Maintenance margin Required level while carrying exposure under the applicable rules
Broker intraday concession A provider's conditional intraday requirement; it may change or end before the exchange session closes
Firm contract/loss limits Separate evaluation or funded-account restrictions; not interchangeable with a retail margin quote

CME explains initial and maintenance margins. A broker can impose additional requirements. Use the provider's actual margin schedule and documented account fields.

Before estimating how many contracts fit

Obtain the current product margin, relevant cutoff time and treatment of existing positions and pending orders. Check whether news, volatility, concentration or overnight holding changes the requirement. Separately check order-size and position-size limits. Passing one check does not imply passing the others.

If a hypothetical provider requires $2,000 per contract and reports $5,000 available for that purpose, two contracts would consume $4,000 before other constraints. This is arithmetic, not an actual margin quote or recommendation to use all available capacity.

Inspect the account without inventing fields

Open File → Trader Dashboard and locate the intended account. This session showed P&L and auto-liquidation headroom columns. It did not establish a usable margin-balance field or current broker margin schedule. Blank cells do not prove spare buying power.

If an order is rejected, preserve the full response and time. Reconcile current exposure and ask the provider which requirement failed before resubmitting. Do not automatically close an unrelated position or send repeated smaller orders to probe a limit.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Does a low day margin apply overnight?
faq.a: Only under the provider terms. A different requirement or earlier cutoff may apply.

faq.q: Does account balance equal available margin?
faq.a: No. Existing exposure, pending orders and provider calculations can reduce available capacity.

faq.q: Is a prop account a cash deposit of its advertised size?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Read the program agreement and account-stage rules.

faq.q: Can an automation bridge override a rejection?
faq.a: No bridge should be assumed to bypass the account risk checks.

articles.title: Rithmic trailing drawdown: understand the account floor
articles.description: Understand trailing drawdown, compare a balance floor with a loss allowance, and check the provider rules that determine peaks, caps and breaches.
articles.answer: A trailing drawdown rule moves an account's permitted balance floor upward as its defined reference reaches new highs. The provider determines the reference, trailing distance, cap and breach condition. Check the exact plan and account stage; a Rithmic login does not identify those rules by itself.

toc.label: A worked example with stated assumptions
Confirm five details for your account
Compare the provider record with R Trader Pro

articles.body:
A worked example with stated assumptions

This illustration uses a hypothetical $30,000 starting reference, a $1,200 trailing distance, intraday peaks and no cap. It is not a provider plan or a recommended configuration.

Event Current measured value Highest reference Calculated floor Distance above floor
Start $30,000 $30,000 $28,800 $1,200
New peak $30,600 $30,600 $29,400 $1,200
Pullback $30,200 $30,600 $29,400 $800
Later peak $31,100 $31,100 $29,900 $1,200
Return to $30,200 $30,200 $31,100 $29,900 $300

The floor equals the qualifying peak less the trailing distance under these assumptions. A later decline does not lower that peak. The table shows arithmetic only; it does not establish when an actual account liquidates or the price at which an exit completes.

Confirm five details for your account

  1. Reference: Does the rule use intraday equity, closed balance or a session-close measurement?
  2. Components: Are open P&L, fees, deposits and withdrawals included?
  3. Update time: When does a new reference change the floor?
  4. Cap: Does trailing stop at a defined floor, and does that differ by account stage?
  5. Breach rule: Is touching the floor sufficient, and what account outcome follows?

For example, Apex's EOD guide separates daily recalculation from intraday enforcement. Its intraday guide uses intraday peaks. These are plan-specific sources checked on 7 October 2026, not rules for all Rithmic accounts.

Compare the provider record with R Trader Pro

Open Trader Dashboard and inspect the account's risk parameters through the menu below. Record the selected administrative scope and criterion. The dashboard inspected locally included Account Balance, Min Account Balance and Auto Liquidate Threshold Value. These are distinct labels; do not assume each represents the same personal or provider floor.

If the provider dashboard and trading application disagree, retain timestamps and ask which value governs the account. A manual calculation can help identify a discrepancy but cannot replace a provider's effective rule or account record.

faq.q: Is trailing drawdown a daily loss limit?
faq.a: No. A daily loss rule and a peak-based floor can operate over different periods and use different measurements. Check both if the account has both.

faq.q: Does the floor reset every morning?
faq.a: Do not assume that. The reference and reset conditions are part of the provider's account rules.

faq.q: Does a personal liquidation limit guarantee protection from a breach?
faq.a: No. Different calculations and execution after a trigger can produce a result beyond the intended threshold.

faq.q: Does the headline account size show how much I can lose?
faq.a: No. Use the actual permitted floor and the provider's current rule, not the plan's name or headline balance alone.

articles.title: Monitor Rithmic P&L and Reconcile Account Differences
articles.description: Find Rithmic account P&L and reconcile differences in fills, fees, open exposure, reporting periods and provider loss calculations.
articles.answer: Use Trader Dashboard for account-level inspection, then reconcile fills, positions, fees and the provider reporting period. A displayed P&L number is not automatically the number used by every loss rule. Compare the same account and time window before treating a difference as an error.

toc.label: Connect monitoring to the actual rule

articles.body:
Locate the native account view

In the inspected desktop, open File → Trader Dashboard. The screenshot shows separate account rows, a P&L column and downside/upside auto-liquidation remaining columns. Names and balances are concealed. This evidence does not establish a universal net-liquidation or available-margin field.

For instrument detail, use Positions and the order/fill histories. R Trader Pro Web also exposes P&L: Auto / Open / Total / Off in the instrument settings. Those choices change the display; they do not create a loss limit.

Reconcile a discrepancy

Compare Possible explanation
Account and expiry Different account, contract or stage selected
Start/end timestamps and timezone Different session boundaries
Open versus closed trades Unrealized P&L included on one side only
Fees and commissions Gross versus net result
Current position and fill quantity Missing, partial or delayed records
Price used to mark the position Different snapshot or valuation reference

For illustration, $100 gross realized profit less $8 costs is $92 net realized profit. Adding a current $30 unrealized loss gives $62 under that illustrative combined definition. A provider may define its monitored criterion differently; use its published definition rather than labeling every difference a delay.

Connect monitoring to the actual rule

Rithmic's risk documentation describes multiple account criteria. Establish whether the applicable rule uses equity, realized result, open P&L, a peak or an end-of-day value. The limit's evaluation period and a dashboard's reporting period can differ.

Do not rely on an undocumented P&L alert menu or a generic percentage threshold. Keep the provider's rule and your current orders visible. Monitoring alone does not prevent slippage, liquidation or a breach.

Screenshot references

faq.a: First compare account, period, open exposure, costs and update time. Ask the provider about unexplained differences.

faq.q: Does P&L reset at midnight?
faq.a: The provider defines the reporting period; local calendar midnight is not universal.

faq.q: Are blank headroom cells zero?
faq.a: No. The capture does not establish their meaning for this account.

faq.q: Does changing the web P&L display change my risk rule?
faq.a: No. Display selection and server risk configuration are different controls.

articles.title: Rithmic risk review checklist for manual and automated orders
articles.description: Review account rules, order protection, automation routes and recovery procedures before trading through Rithmic, without assuming universal risk settings.
articles.answer: Before trading through Rithmic, identify the account's effective restrictions, review the intended order and exit behavior, and know how to inspect remaining exposure if something fails. Account risk controls, order-level stops and automation monitoring serve different purposes. None guarantees a maximum loss or a successful evaluation.

toc.label: Review the order and exit plan

articles.body:
Review the account rule

Record the provider, plan and account stage. Confirm the effective balance floor, loss calculation, quantity limits and permitted trading times. Use current account records rather than copying a percentage or a contract count from a generic guide.

The risk-settings guide shows the inspected route into View Risk Parameters. Check permissions and the selected administrative tab before interpreting a field. A personal threshold does not replace the provider's rules.

Review the order and exit plan

Distinguish a stop trigger from an execution price and a limit price from a guaranteed fill. Confirm where brackets, trailing changes and OCO cancellation are managed for the specific platform and connection. Inspect working exits after an entry; a template name alone does not establish that an order was accepted.

Use the order-types guide and bracket guide for these distinctions. Choose contract and size using the actual product specifications and account restrictions, not the headline account balance alone.

Review automation separately

  1. Identify every alert, strategy, copier and manual route that can submit instructions.
  2. Confirm the intended destination account, expiry, side and quantity.
  3. Distinguish alert generation, webhook delivery, order acceptance and fills in the records.
  4. Validate changes in a suitable provider-approved simulation.
  5. Establish how to stop new signals and separately inspect or manage existing orders and positions.

Pausing an alert is not a flatten command. Disabling a copier is not proof that a follower position is closed. Follow the exact control scope in the flatten guide.

Keep an incident record

For a problem, record timestamps with timezone, platform versions, exact responses and the relevant account and order identifiers privately. Compare positions, working orders and fill history before retrying an uncertain request. A missing acknowledgement can require reconciliation rather than an immediate duplicate submission.

faq.q: Is there a universal percentage to risk per trade?
faq.a: No. This operational checklist does not prescribe a suitable loss allowance. Account rules, product exposure and personal circumstances differ.

faq.q: Does a simulation prove live behavior?
faq.a: No. It can validate parts of a workflow, but execution conditions, account permissions and provider rules may differ.

faq.q: Are server controls enough for unattended automation?
faq.a: Do not treat their existence as proof that every failure is covered. Review the configured conditions, monitoring and recovery procedure for the actual system.

faq.q: Is closing the trading application an emergency exit?
faq.a: No. Closing a display does not establish that server-held orders or positions have been closed. Inspect the actual account state through an authorized connection.
