articles.title: EOD versus intraday trailing drawdown on Rithmic
articles.description: Compare when EOD and intraday drawdown floors move, understand enforcement timing, and check the rules for the exact Rithmic account plan.
articles.answer: EOD trailing uses a qualifying end-of-day reference to update the floor; intraday trailing can update it from an intraday peak. The time the floor changes and the time it is enforced are separate rules. Do not assume an EOD account permits a temporary intraday breach.
articles.body:
Compare the two calculations

Question EOD trailing Intraday trailing
Which reference updates the floor? Qualifying session-close value Qualifying intraday peak
Can a temporary open profit raise it? Depends on the closing reference and plan definition Can, when open equity is included
When is the existing floor enforced? Check the provider; it can be intraday Check the provider's stated breach condition
Does the floor stop trailing? Plan- and account-stage-specific cap Plan- and account-stage-specific cap

Neither label establishes a suitable trading strategy or a safe position size.

Hypothetical comparison

Assume a $30,000 initial reference, $1,200 trailing distance and no cap. The account reaches $30,900 intraday and closes at $30,400.

Method Qualifying reference in this example New floor
EOD reference $30,400 close $29,200
Intraday reference $30,900 peak $29,700

These values explain the calculation only. The example assumes both methods count the values stated and omits fees and cash movements. It is not a current provider plan or an execution test.

A documented provider example

Apex's EOD documentation states that its specified EOD floor is recalculated at the session close and enforced during the following session. Its intraday documentation describes a peak-based intraday calculation. Read the source for the exact account stage, platform and cap; do not apply these examples to another firm or a legacy plan without confirmation.

Verify your plan

  1. Find the exact account type and whether it is an evaluation or performance account.
  2. Read the current provider rule for reference, update time and breach condition.
  3. Identify any cap and the effect of payouts or other cash movements.
  4. Compare the provider's displayed floor with the relevant account risk value.
  5. Resolve any discrepancy with the provider before relying on a manual estimate.

faq.q: Is EOD drawdown checked only at the close?
faq.a: Not necessarily. In the cited Apex specification, updating the floor at the close does not prevent intraday enforcement of that floor.

faq.q: Is EOD always safer?
faq.a: The two methods can produce different floors, but the label alone does not determine an account's overall risk. Other limits and breach rules still apply.

faq.q: Can I change a firm's drawdown type in R Trader Pro?
faq.a: Do not assume a personal setting can change the contractual provider rule. Confirm the supported account configuration with the provider.

faq.q: Are screenshots necessary for the arithmetic?
faq.a: The tables explain a hypothetical comparison. They are not presented as account screenshots or proof of a particular account's effective settings.

articles.title: Manage Multiple Rithmic Accounts
articles.description: Organize Rithmic accounts by login, System and account ID. Check account visibility, session limits and separate copying permissions.
articles.answer: First determine which accounts belong to each issued Rithmic login and System. Several accounts can be visible in one session, but that does not enable copying automatically. Different logins require a supported connection arrangement and separate permission checks.

toc.label: Add copying or alert routing deliberately

articles.body:
Build an account map

Record privately Why it matters
Provider and account ID Identifies the actual trading destination
Login and System Identifies the connection that exposes it
Account stage and status Distinguishes evaluation, simulated funded and live arrangements
Permitted platform and session count Prevents assuming every saved connection can run together
Risk rules and copier role Keeps follower limits and independent exposure visible

Keep passwords in an appropriate credential store, not a shared account spreadsheet. The native capture below establishes two account rows under the inspected login, without disclosing their identifiers.

Choose the connection arrangement

For accounts visible under one login, inspect Trader Dashboard and the account selector in each order-entry window. Selection can be local to that window; check charts, DOMs and strategies individually.

For different logins, confirm that the platform supports the exact concurrent connection combination. Saving two profiles is not proof that both can be active. Do not work around a restriction by launching unsupported duplicate instances.

RTrader Pro plugin mode shares a supported host connection with compatible applications. It does not merge credentials, provide universal session exemptions or copy orders by itself. Quantower documents its host/client connection route.

Add copying or alert routing deliberately

The native Trade Copier exists, but the inspected login reports copying is not enabled. Provider activation and account eligibility are separate from account visibility. Cloud alert routing is another workflow; PickMyTrade's Rithmic setup has its own supported connections and exclusions.

For every destination, reconcile acceptance, fills, remaining orders and position independently. One leader fill cannot prove every follower filled. Compare the actual software, data, connection and hosting costs instead of assuming one tool is always cheaper.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Does one login mean one account?
faq.a: No. The inspected login exposed two account rows.

faq.q: Does plugin mode copy trades?
faq.a: No. It provides a supported connection-sharing route; copying requires a separately configured copier.

faq.q: Can I run every saved connection at once?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Verify the platform and provider concurrency rules.

faq.q: Does adding more accounts reduce risk?
faq.a: No. Replicating exposure can increase the combined amount at risk.

articles.title: Switch Between Rithmic Accounts Without Losing Track of Orders
articles.description: Select and verify the intended Rithmic order account. Understand why switching the display does not move positions or existing orders.
articles.answer: For accounts exposed by one connection, select the intended account in the order-entry window and check it again before submitting. Changing the selected account does not close positions or cancel orders on the previous account. Other windows or strategies may retain their own selection.

toc.label: Switch within the inspected desktop workflow
Keep the previous account in view
When the account is not listed

articles.body:
Switch within the inspected desktop workflow

  1. Open File → Trader Dashboard and identify the provider-issued account ID privately.
  2. Open the relevant Order Book and inspect its account selector.
  3. Select the intended destination only after matching the full ID and connection.
  4. Check the instrument, expiry, quantity and active entry/exit configuration in that window.
  5. Recheck other order-entry windows and automated strategies separately.

The captures establish where to inspect accounts and entry controls. The inspection did not submit an order to either account. Do not interpret a changed dropdown as an account-wide transfer of every window.

Keep the previous account in view

Record its positions, working orders and copier participation before switching. A pending order can still execute while another account is selected. A copier can also route subsequent actions to a follower that is no longer on screen.

When the account is not listed

Compare the provider assignment with the current username/System and account status. A website account, trading username and trading account ID are different identifiers. Apex's login guidance illustrates why website credentials do not substitute for trading credentials.

For a different login, follow the platform's supported connection process. Do not assume NinjaTrader can maintain multiple Rithmic providers concurrently simply because it stores their profiles. Establish the effect of disconnecting on existing local order management before switching connections.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Does switching flatten the old account?
faq.a: No. Inspect its positions and working orders separately.

faq.q: Does the selector change every chart?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Check each order-entry panel and strategy.

faq.q: Can a missing account be activated by reinstalling?
faq.a: An installation cannot grant provider account permission. Check the assignment and status first.

faq.q: Can nicknames replace account IDs?
faq.a: Use nicknames as a visual aid, but match the full provider-issued identifier.

articles.title: Rithmic Account ID, Username and Connection Name Explained
articles.description: Distinguish Rithmic usernames, account IDs and connection names. Build a private account map without changing provider identifiers.
articles.answer: A Rithmic username authenticates a connection. An account ID identifies a trading destination exposed by that connection. A connection name or local nickname is a display label. Match the full provider-issued account ID rather than inferring identity from a prefix or numeric suffix.
articles.body:
Distinguish the identifiers

Identifier Use
Provider website login Accesses membership, billing or program information
Rithmic username Authenticates to the assigned Rithmic System
Trading account ID Selects the actual account for orders and records
Local connection name Helps recognize a saved platform configuration
Nickname A visual aid where supported; not evidence of a changed broker identifier

Locate and compare the account

Use the provider's issued account details, then compare them with File → Trader Dashboard in the authenticated desktop. The current capture shows distinct Account and Name columns. Do not substitute a guessed format such as a firm abbreviation followed by digits.

For automation, use the account resolved by the current connection/generator workflow. Do not strip prefixes or match only a shared number when two accounts look similar. If a platform displays an alias, use its documentation or provider support to establish the exact mapping before routing.

Keep a private identification record

Record provider, program/stage, full account ID, associated username/System and a meaningful local label. For example, a local label can describe the provider and evaluation number without pretending to be a real routing ID. Store credentials separately and redact IDs in public screenshots.

After a reset, account replacement or stage transition, compare the newly issued details with saved workspaces, alerts and copier destinations. A provider may retain or replace identifiers; neither behavior is universal. Earn2Trade's setup guide is an example of provider-issued data credentials distinct from general website access.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Can I infer funded status from the prefix?
faq.a: No. Use the provider account status and program documentation.

faq.q: Can one username expose several IDs?
faq.a: Yes. That was observed in the native dashboard.

faq.q: Does a nickname change the routing ID?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Treat it as a display aid unless the provider states otherwise.

faq.q: Should public support screenshots show the whole ID?
faq.a: Hide private identifiers in public material. Provide exact details only through the provider secure support channel when needed.

articles.title: Same Rithmic Login vs Separate Logins
articles.description: Compare multiple accounts under one Rithmic login with separate credentials, including System selection, session limits and copier access.
articles.answer: Compare the issued username and System, then the account IDs visible after authentication. One login can expose several accounts. Separate credentials are separate connection contexts; plugin mode does not combine them and account-stage labels do not determine their System.
articles.body:
Compare the arrangements

Question Several accounts on one login Separate logins
How are accounts found? Inspect the account list for that connection Inspect each supported connection separately
How are orders directed? Select the exact account ID Select both the correct connection context and account
Is copying automatic? No; copier eligibility/configuration still required No; copier must explicitly support the connection arrangement
Does a plugin merge access? It can share a supported host connection It does not merge unrelated credentials

Use the issued System

Do not infer Rithmic Paper Trading versus Rithmic 01 from evaluation versus funded terminology. A simulated funded account can still use a simulation service, and a provider can use a branded System. Apex documents its own Rithmic setup; Bulenox publishes a different connection recipe.

The inspected VPS login exposes two account rows. This establishes that multiple accounts can share a session; it does not prove how every firm groups accounts or that those rows are enabled copier destinations.

Check before adding another connection

Confirm supported concurrency, platform licence, data subscription and session treatment with the relevant vendors. A second login does not imply a second Windows installation is required, but a saved connection list does not prove simultaneous support either.

If using PickMyTrade, follow its current Rithmic setup and resolve the intended accounts in its generator. Connectivity, copier support and firm permission remain separate decisions. Do not choose a service based on an unverified account-count or speed promise.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Does the same firm always use one login?
faq.a: No. Inspect the actual assignment.

faq.q: Does funded always mean Rithmic 01?
faq.a: No. Provider instructions and the actual account stage determine the route.

faq.q: Does plugin mode grant unlimited sessions?
faq.a: No. It is a supported host/client mechanism, not a universal entitlement change.

faq.q: Can copying span separate credentials?
faq.a: Only if the selected copier explicitly supports and permits that arrangement.

articles.title: Size and Organize a VPS for Multiple Rithmic Accounts
articles.description: Plan a VPS around Rithmic applications, charts and automation. Separate account count, connection entitlement and measured resource use.
articles.answer: Size a VPS for the applications, charts, history and automation it runs, not the number of account rows alone. Several accounts in one RTrader session can require less computing work than several separate charting applications. Measure the intended workload before selecting resources.
articles.body:
Inventory the workload

List each platform, supported connection, chart count, instrument subscription, historical-data load and locally managed strategy/copier. Record which applications depend on RTrader Pro plugin mode. A cloud receiver and a local desktop strategy have different hosting requirements.

Measure before buying more capacity

Measurement Interpretation
CPU during market bursts and history load Identifies sustained processing pressure; one busy core can matter
Committed memory and paging Helps distinguish adequate RAM from disk-backed memory pressure
Disk free space and write activity Logs/history can fill a small disk
Quote timestamps and application response Helps separate remote-display lag from delayed platform processing
Connection and order records Required to investigate routing delays; an RDP impression is insufficient

Use Windows Task Manager on the actual intended workload and keep headroom for bursts and updates. There is no verified universal rule that each account needs a fixed amount of RAM or that a Chicago VPS delivers one-millisecond orders.

Organize sessions and recovery

Use only platform-supported connection combinations. Do not bypass single-instance or data-session restrictions with copied installations. Keep account IDs distinct from connection labels and review each destination's state.

Keep the operating system supported, secure remote access, back up configurations and plan updates outside the intended trading session. Disconnecting an RDP viewer, signing out of Windows, rebooting and terminating a platform are different actions. Check which local order-management components would stop before ending the session.

Rithmic's desktop requirements describe Windows compatibility; they do not size a multi-platform workload. Compare current hosting quotes including Windows licensing, backups and management. Add software, data and copier fees separately for the actual intended configuration.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Does adding an account require another VPS?
faq.a: Not inherently. It depends on the supported connection and workload.

faq.q: Does a VPS prevent all disconnects?
faq.a: No. Host, network, provider and application failures remain possible.

faq.q: Should I leave RTrader running for plugin clients?
faq.a: The supported plugin host must remain available to its clients.

faq.q: Does cloud alert routing need my own VPS?
faq.a: A cloud receiving service may host that path, but any separate local strategy or platform still needs its own host.

articles.title: NinjaTrader Rithmic Setup: Check Eligibility Before Connecting
articles.description: Check whether your NinjaTrader account can use Rithmic, then follow the provider-specific connection guide. Includes conflicting onboarding guidance and checks.
articles.answer: Confirm Rithmic connection eligibility with NinjaTrader and your account provider first. Rithmic's platform page says new Rithmic connections are no longer being onboarded while existing users can continue. Apex still publishes a connection guide. These sources do not establish that every new Apex or NinjaTrader account is eligible.
articles.body:
Resolve the eligibility question first

Compare the Rithmic NinjaTrader page with your provider's current instructions. Ask support whether your specific NinjaTrader login, account and version have the required connection option. Keep the answer with your setup notes.

Do not buy software, select a different provider, or reinstall it solely because an old tutorial shows a Rithmic menu item.

For an eligible existing setup

The Apex NinjaTrader guide describes enabling Multi-provider in Tools, then Settings, then General (wording in the current Apex guide; older instructions say Options), restarting, and opening Connections, then Configure. It uses My Rithmic for NinjaTrader Brokerage. Apply these instructions only where the connection is supported for your account.

  1. Record your NinjaTrader version and the provider's instructions.
  2. Locate the provider-issued Rithmic credentials and System. Do not substitute website credentials or choose a server only because the account is called funded.
  3. Complete required agreements through the provider's documented route.
  4. Configure the available connection using the provider guide. If the required option is absent, resolve eligibility with support rather than choosing a similarly named connector.
  5. Connect and verify the intended account and symbol. Check the log for authentication, data and trading errors separately.

NinjaTrader's Connections Menu help explains connection configuration and status. A connection indicator does not establish that an order was accepted or filled.

Direct connection or plugin?

Use the arrangement documented for your platform version and provider entitlement. If a plugin route is supported, both ends must be configured for it. Do not leave an additional direct data connection running by accident. See Plugin Mode.

Captured reference images

The captions distinguish observed web screens from vendor documentation and imported desktop references. None proves a successful order or the unobserved desktop workflow.

Check the actual NinjaTrader entitlement

The current Apex guide directs missing-account users to Control Center → Help → About and the Evaluation (Rithmic) entitlement. It says NinjaTrader, rather than Apex, controls adding that entitlement. This establishes a diagnostic check, not a guarantee that a new request will be approved despite Rithmic's onboarding notice.

The guide applies to eligible existing desktop configurations. No NinjaTrader login or order was tested on this VPS, so the reference image is not a connected-account screenshot.

faq.q: Why is Rithmic missing from my provider list?
faq.a: Eligibility, version and configuration can differ. Confirm the supported connection with NinjaTrader and your provider; this review did not reproduce your desktop menu.

faq.q: Does an Apex setup article guarantee new NinjaTrader access?
faq.a: No. It conflicts in scope with the current Rithmic onboarding notice. Obtain an account-specific answer before treating the guide as applicable.

faq.q: Is Sim101 my prop-firm account?
faq.a: Do not identify accounts by assumption. Compare the selected trading account with the provider's account details and the platform's simulation/live mode before any test.

faq.q: Does a green connection prove everything works?
faq.a: No. It is one status signal. Check the account, instrument, data timestamps and error log; order execution needs separate evidence.

articles.title: Troubleshoot NinjaTrader Rithmic Connections
articles.description: Diagnose NinjaTrader Rithmic access, missing accounts, data and order errors using the correct System, entitlement and log entries.
articles.answer: Start with connection eligibility, the issued System and the complete NinjaTrader log entry. Then distinguish missing accounts, missing market data and rejected orders. Reinstalling or clearing a database is not a first-line fix for every Rithmic connection problem.
articles.body:
Missing Rithmic option or account

Rithmic's platform notice limits new onboarding while describing continued access for existing users. Apex's current guide describes Multi-provider configuration and Help → About → Evaluation (Rithmic) entitlement. Confirm applicability to your NinjaTrader login before adding or replacing connections.

Diagnose the failing layer

Observation Check next
Authentication rejected Trading credentials and provider-issued System; website credentials are different
Connected but only local simulation visible Entitlement, account assignment and the actual account selector
Account visible but no quotes Exact expiry, exchange agreement, data entitlement and session hours
Quotes work but order rejected Selected destination and full rejection; price data is not trading permission
Recent quotes but missing history History range/source, logs and Rithmic's published download limit
Repeated disconnects Timestamped logs, host/client route, resource pressure and current advisories

An RTrader login working narrows the investigation but does not prove the NinjaTrader connector has the same permissions or subscription path.

Reconnect only after preserving state

Before disconnecting, inspect positions, working orders and local strategies. NinjaTrader's Rithmic-specific order-location guide places OCO management on the local PC. A remote order may remain active when that management stops.

Preserve the original log and make one evidence-based change at a time. Do not delete history databases, disable firewalls or select Rithmic 01 solely because an account is called funded. If duplicate orders appear, reconcile their IDs and sources before removing a connection or replaying signals.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Should I choose the generic Rithmic provider by default?
faq.a: Use the connector named in the applicable current provider guide; Apex documents My Rithmic for NinjaTrader Brokerage.

faq.q: Does Help/About grant an entitlement?
faq.a: No. It displays information; NinjaTrader controls the entitlement.

faq.q: Should I delete the database for a login failure?
faq.a: No. Authentication and permission problems need their own evidence.

faq.q: Does a green indicator prove working protective orders?
faq.a: No. Inspect the actual order states and local dependencies.

articles.title: Connect Quantower to Rithmic
articles.description: Connect Quantower to Rithmic using the documented direct or RTrader route. Check server, plugin settings, data access and account status.
articles.answer: In Quantower, open the connection manager, choose Rithmic, enter the issued credentials and select the provider-assigned server. For plugin mode, enable Use RTrader in the connection settings and start the matching RTrader Pro host first.
articles.body:
Configure the intended route

  1. Confirm that the account and your Quantower licence support the connection/features you need.
  2. Open the connection manager and select Rithmic.
  3. Choose the exact provider server. The vendor page's demo/live defaults do not override a firm's issued configuration.
  4. Enter the Rithmic login and password privately.
  5. For a direct connection, use the documented direct route and check the provider's concurrent-data-session allowance.
  6. For plugin mode, open Connection Settings → Use RTrader. RTrader Pro must already be running with plugins enabled and matching credentials/server.
  7. Connect, inspect the account list and resolve a dated contract before enabling strategies.

Enable MBO only when entitled

Quantower documents Enable 'Market by Order' (MBO) mode in the connection settings. Its DOM Trader display uses Settings → Columns → Bids/Ask → Size coloring scheme → MBO, with column wording depending on split mode. Changing a display setting does not buy data entitlement.

If connection or history fails

Distinguish authentication, missing exchange access and an unavailable plugin host. Use the Event Log and Quantower's Rithmic issue guide. For incomplete history, narrow the requested range and inspect the history-server setting; do not start by deleting platform databases.

Source checked 7 October 2026: Quantower official connection guide.

faq.q: Does Use RTrader work without the host?
faq.a: No. The supported plugin host must be running and connected.

faq.q: Are all Quantower features free with Rithmic?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Connection access, multiple connections and analysis features can have separate licence conditions.

faq.q: Does MBO mode grant market depth?
faq.a: No. The provider must authorize the data.

faq.q: Does a connected icon prove trades will fill?

articles.title: Connect ATAS to Rithmic
articles.description: Set up ATAS with a direct Rithmic connection or RTrader Pro plugin. Match server and aggregation settings and check local OCO dependencies.
articles.answer: ATAS supports a direct Rithmic connection and a connection through RTrader Pro. Choose one deliberately. Add Rithmic in Connections and use Connect via RTrader Pro only for the plugin route, with the host running and matching server/aggregation settings.
articles.body:
Add the connection

  1. Open Connections → Add, select Rithmic, then continue with Next.
  2. Read the displayed connection/OCO conditions before agreeing.
  3. Enter the issued credentials and server. Do not infer the server from an account's funded label.
  4. For direct access, leave Connect via RTrader Pro off and follow ATAS's restriction on competing connections using those credentials.
  5. For plugin access, start RTrader Pro with Allow Plugins enabled, then enable Connect via RTrader Pro in ATAS. Match the server and aggregation settings.
  6. Finish and connect, then inspect the connection status, instrument and account before order entry.

Know the plugin limitation

The vendor documents one Rithmic account connection through RTrader Pro for this ATAS route. Do not use it as proof that multiple unrelated Rithmic credentials can be merged in ATAS. Keep the host open.

Diagnose delayed data carefully

ATAS describes aggregation as a way to reduce update frequency and CPU pressure. It is not a universal setting to switch off or on blindly. A change can affect the detail available to analysis. Connection warnings and absent heartbeat data need investigation; a quiet instrument and a failed connection can look similar in a static chart.

ATAS's connection guidance warns about locally managed OCO. Establish the exact behavior of your selected route before depending on local software being closed during an open position.

Source checked 7 October 2026: ATAS official connection guide.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Should I always turn aggregation off?
faq.a: No. Match the host/client requirements and understand the data-detail tradeoff.

faq.q: Can direct and plugin connections be mixed casually?
faq.a: No. Follow the route-specific connection limits.

faq.q: Is an ATAS licence a data subscription?
faq.a: They are separate requirements.

faq.q: Was ATAS connected on this VPS?
faq.a: No. The configuration reference comes from ATAS documentation; the RTrader host controls were inspected separately.

articles.title: Connect Sierra Chart to Rithmic Direct DTC
articles.description: Configure Sierra Chart's Rithmic Direct DTC service, server and credentials. Check package requirements, data sources and support limits.
articles.answer: Sierra Chart documents Rithmic Direct - DTC [Trading] with Service Package 10 or higher. Use the broker-issued server and credentials. Read Sierra’s current Rithmic support policy before selecting market data; it recommends Denali for data issues and limits support for Rithmic functionality.

toc.label: If the account or data is unavailable

articles.body:
Follow the current service setup

  1. Update Sierra Chart using its supported update process and confirm Package 10 or higher.
  2. Open Global Settings → Data/Trade Service Settings.
  3. Select Rithmic Direct - DTC [Trading] under Current Selected Service.
  4. Press OK, wait 5–10 seconds and reopen the settings so the server list can load.
  5. Select the provider-assigned Server and enter Trading Username / Trading Password exactly.
  6. Supply Market Data and Historical Data credentials only if using Rithmic for those data services; follow the vendor's separate Denali instructions otherwise.
  7. Save and use File → Connect to Data Feed. Inspect Window → Message Log for errors.
  8. Use File → Find Symbol to select the intended instrument. Sierra documents [symbol].[exchange] for this service.

These steps follow Sierra's current service guide. The guide also requires the account identifier, username and password to be no longer than 31 characters. Resolve an incompatible identifier with the provider rather than truncating it yourself.

Know what the service supports

The vendor lists server-managed OCO but not server-managed bracket orders as of its current writing. That distinction matters if local software disconnects before creating or updating children. It does not mean every Rithmic platform has the same dependencies.

If the account or data is unavailable

Use the Message Log's full error and the exact service/server. A simulation-mode selection and a provider-issued simulated account are different concepts; do not switch trading modes merely to force an account to appear. If an exchange denies access, ask the account provider to check entitlement. The RTrader reference below helps identify the original issued connection; it is not a screenshot of Sierra connected locally.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Which service should I select?
faq.a: Rithmic Direct - DTC [Trading], as documented by Sierra.

faq.q: Why must the settings window reopen?
faq.a: The initial selection retrieves the current Rithmic server list.

faq.q: Should I shorten a long account ID?
faq.a: No. Ask the provider to resolve the compatibility issue.

faq.q: Does server OCO imply server brackets?
faq.a: No. Sierra lists those capabilities separately.

articles.title: Connect MotiveWave to Rithmic
articles.description: Follow MotiveWave's RTrader Pro gateway instructions and check the host, Market Data choice, account and connection log.
articles.answer: For MotiveWave’s RTrader gateway route, start RTrader Pro with Allow Plugins enabled, then select R|Trader Gateway in the Market Data dropdown of the MotiveWave Rithmic connection. Use the provider-issued service details and keep the host running.

toc.label: Distinguish market data from order handling
When the gateway cannot be reached

articles.body:
Configure the gateway route

  1. Install the supported RTrader Pro application; the vendor distinguishes it from the older regular RTrader product.
  2. Enable Allow Plugins in the host login configuration and connect using the provider's details.
  3. Open the Rithmic connection configuration in MotiveWave.
  4. Set Market Data to R|Trader Gateway as described in the vendor guide.
  5. Match the intended credentials and service configuration, then connect.
  6. Confirm that the desired account and dated instrument are present before enabling any automated strategy.

Distinguish market data from order handling

A chart receiving quotes does not establish the order destination or the behavior of an exit strategy. Check the actual trading account, selected contract and local strategy settings independently. The gateway route does not prove every broker feature or every MotiveWave edition is supported.

When the gateway cannot be reached

Check that the Pro host remains connected, plugins are enabled and the route selected in MotiveWave matches the intended architecture. Preserve the full connection error. Do not silently change to a direct connection if that would create an unapproved extra data session.

Plugin-based sharing can change session usage, but subscriber classification and billing still depend on current exchange/provider rules. It is not a blanket professional-fee exemption.

Source checked 7 October 2026: MotiveWave official connection guide.

faq.q: Is regular RTrader the required host?
faq.a: The cited route requires RTrader Pro.

faq.q: What dropdown selects the gateway?
faq.a: The MotiveWave connection’s Market Data dropdown: R|Trader Gateway.

faq.q: Can I close the host after connecting?
faq.a: Keep the required host running for the gateway route.

faq.q: Does this confirm an automated exit test?

articles.title: Connect Bookmap to Rithmic and Check Market Depth
articles.description: Check Bookmap's Rithmic depth subscription, platform licence and plugin settings. Separate data visibility from chart-trading permission.
articles.answer: Bookmap’s Rithmic connection requires the appropriate depth entitlement. To share a supported RTrader Pro session, enable Allow Plugins in the host and Plugin mode in Bookmap’s Rithmic connection. Keep the credentials consistent and the host open.

toc.label: Establish the licence and data requirements

articles.body:
Establish the licence and data requirements

Bookmap's connectivity guide distinguishes a software package, market-data subscription and trading access. It states that trading a funded account from the chart requires Global+. A charting licence or a data-only subscription does not itself provide an order-routing account.

Configure plugin mode

  1. Start a supported RTrader Pro build with Allow Plugins enabled and authenticate using the issued service details.
  2. In Bookmap, open Connection → Configure.
  3. Choose ADD CONNECTION → Rithmic.
  4. Enable Plugin mode and enter the matching RTrader Pro credentials. Check the System/Gateway combination.
  5. Save with OK, select that connection from the Connection menu and use + to subscribe to the intended instrument.
  6. Keep RTrader Pro running and verify the actual account before any order-entry action.

Resolve permission and data warnings

If Bookmap reports permission denied, its documentation directs broker-provided users to have the provider check Level 2/MBO access. A different platform working on top-of-book data does not disprove a missing depth entitlement.

Bookmap's latency warning concerns delayed market-data timestamps, not a measured order round trip. Its aggregation option reduces data volume but can affect MBO-dependent functionality. Treat aggregation as a considered diagnostic tradeoff, not a routine fix for every warning. Do not ignore inconsistent MBO warnings when analysis depends on that data.

The native entitlement capture below demonstrates why generic data access and market depth must be checked separately. Bookmap was not installed or authenticated on this VPS for the capture.

faq.a: Its Rithmic order-book workflow requires the relevant depth access; top-of-book success is insufficient.

articles.title: Set Up Rithmic on a Windows VPS

articles.answer: Use a supported Windows host, secure remote access and the account provider’s current installer/connection instructions. Verify the actual account and data before adding automation. A VPS hosts software; it does not grant Rithmic entitlement, guarantee uptime or establish a particular execution latency.
articles.body:
Check account permission

Confirm that the firm permits order transmission from a VPS for your exact account and tool. Platform compatibility does not establish that permission. Current TopstepX API rules, for example, prohibit remote-server order flow; that is a separate platform route, not a general Rithmic rule.

Prepare the host

Rithmic's desktop page lists 64-bit Windows desktop/server requirements. Choose a currently supported operating system and size resources for the actual platforms, charts and history load. Obtain a current quote that identifies location, Windows licensing, backup and support costs.

Use the hosting provider's supported secure access method. Protect administrator credentials, keep the firewall enabled and restrict remote access appropriately. Do not copy public forum port lists into broad firewall exceptions.

Install and connect

  1. Download RTrader Pro from the official/provider-supported route.
  2. Preserve any existing workspace before an update or reinstall.
  3. Enter the issued trading credentials and exact System/Gateway.
  4. Complete only required agreements after reading and accurately answering them.
  5. Match the intended account in Trader Dashboard and inspect exchange/data status separately.
  6. Add a client or automation component using its documented connection architecture.

The screenshots here come from a real Windows VPS session. They demonstrate native controls, not a benchmark of a particular hosting plan.

Keep the intended session running

Microsoft distinguishes disconnecting the viewer from ending the remote session. Applications remain active only while the remote session remains active; host timeout policies, sign-out and reboot can terminate it. Confirm the host policy before leaving a local strategy or plugin client dependent on that session.

Prepare recovery

Record startup order, local order-management dependencies and the provider's emergency procedure. Back up configuration, schedule supported updates appropriately and check state after any restart before enabling signals. Do not store plain-text credentials inside a public guide or shared screenshot bundle.

articles.title: Rithmic API Overview: Interfaces, Test Access and Conformance
articles.description: Compare Rithmic API families, separate developer-test access from production and paper-demo access, and identify the approvals and fees to confirm.
articles.answer: Rithmic offers R | API+, R | Protocol API and R | Diamond API for different development environments. Obtain the matching kit and current connection specification from Rithmic. Developer-test access, production conformance, account credentials and provider permission are separate requirements. A desktop login or ordinary paper demo does not establish permission to run a custom API application.

toc.label: Test is not the same as a paper demo

articles.body:
Compare the interface families

The official API page describes:

Family Interface/deployment distinction
R | API+ C++ and .NET library interfaces; check the kit's OS support
R | Protocol API Wire protocol using WebSockets and Protocol Buffers for clients in different languages
R | Diamond API Specialized Linux C/C++ and co-location workflow with additional access prerequisites

An API is the interface a program uses to request data or order actions. Protocol Buffers describe structured messages; they are not the same as a generic JSON webhook. Co-location places computing resources in a specified infrastructure environment; it is not automatically the same as an ordinary retail VPS.

Start with access requirements

  1. Describe the application's purpose, language and intended deployment to Rithmic.
  2. Obtain the appropriate current kit and test-environment instructions. Do not invent endpoints or copy a historical configuration into production.
  3. Develop and validate against the environment approved for that kit.
  4. Confirm the conformance process before production access. Conformance is the vendor's integration review; it is not an investment-performance approval.
  5. Obtain provider-issued account credentials and confirm market-data, session and account entitlements separately.
  6. Confirm fees and any provider/firm restrictions for the specific use before committing to the workflow.

Rithmic's API inquiry page distinguishes Protocol onboarding from other kit requests and states additional gating for Diamond. Follow those current instructions rather than assuming the three interfaces have identical enrollment.

Test is not the same as a paper demo

The desktop System menu contained Rithmic Test, Rithmic Paper Trading and Rithmic 01. It was read without attempting a new login. The official FAQ states that Protocol API access is not available for paper-trading demos that include live market data. Keep that restriction separate from the API page's developer-test workflow and from a provider-issued simulation account.

What an integration must verify

Plan how the application records requests, acknowledgements, fills, rejects and cancellations. Establish recovery when the connection drops between a request and its recorded outcome. Confirm which protective functions are supported and where they run for the exact route. A marketed server-side capability does not prove that every third-party connector uses it.

Do not publish invented working code or JSON fields as the Rithmic API. Use the current kit's message definitions and controlled validation. No kit was requested, custom app registered, order sent or conformance test performed for this article.

faq.q: Is a TradingView webhook the official Rithmic API?
faq.a: No. A bridge's incoming alert format is a separate interface. It may translate requests through its own supported connection.

faq.q: Does my RTrader Pro login authorize custom production code?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Confirm application approval, environment and provider entitlements.

faq.q: Is API access free?
faq.a: This guide establishes no universal price. Obtain current kit, infrastructure, provider and exchange-data fees for the actual setup.

faq.q: Do vendor latency figures predict my fill speed?
faq.a: No. A vendor's stated performance basis is not a measured end-to-end result for your network, application, account and order.

articles.description: Compare Rithmic order-flow platforms by depth, MBO, executed volume, history and trading workflow rather than unsupported speed claims.
articles.answer: Compare the analysis you need—price-level depth, individual displayed orders, executed volume or historical replay—before choosing an order-flow platform. articles.body:
Compare useful capabilities and constraints

Separate the data types

Market-by-price aggregates displayed size at a price. Market-by-order provides individual displayed-order information where supported. Evaluate with the intended workload

Use a permitted trial/account and the exact exchange subscription. Check current quotes, depth completeness, historical/replay availability, CPU/memory use and whether aggregation removes needed detail. Keep account order entry separate from data-only evaluation. Use the same contracts and observation period for comparisons.

There is no measured best-platform or fastest-routing ranking in this library. Screenshots and vendor feature lists cannot establish trading results. Price comparisons should include software, data, add-ons and any hosting cost, with billing period and tax treatment recorded.

Before using an external tool, verify account-stage permission, the supported connection and the actual destination. Do not paste a Rithmic payload into a ProjectX workflow or assume embedded TradingView charts accept TradingView.com webhooks directly.

Resolve a login problem at the correct provider

articles.title: Troubleshoot a Prop-Firm Rithmic Account
articles.description: Troubleshoot a prop-firm Rithmic account by separating provisioning, credentials, data access, account visibility and order restrictions.
articles.answer: First identify the account provider, stage, actual platform and issued Rithmic System. Then separate provisioning, authentication, data entitlement and trading restrictions. A generic reconnect or reset cannot resolve every provider-side problem.
articles.body:
Locate the failure

Symptom Evidence and next step
No credentials issued Check account provisioning with the firm; do not invent a login
Credentials rejected Match trading credentials and assigned System, excluding copied spaces
Account missing Check exact login/account assignment, activation and platform entitlement
Quotes missing Check contract session, exchange agreements and data/depth access
Order rejected Preserve the exact response and compare the account risk rules
Liquidation/admin-only Ask the provider about the current mode and authorized clearing process
Works in one app only Compare connector permission, direct/plugin route and platform licence

Use provider-specific facts

Apex's documented System is Apex; Bulenox and Leeloo publish Paper Trading routes. Earn2Trade changed its provided NinjaTrader access in June 2026. TopstepX credentials are not a Rithmic login. Follow the dated firm setup references, not a generic evaluation/funded server table.

Preserve order state before recovery

Inspect positions, working orders and local strategy/copier dependencies before ending a session or retrying a signal. Rithmic's current FAQ says post-liquidation restrictions can require manual clearing; a new calendar day is not proof of recovery.

Send a useful support record

Use the firm's official support channel with the account ID privately, program stage, platform/build, issued System, timestamp/timezone and full error. Include redacted relevant logs and describe what still works. Keep passwords and API tokens out of screenshots and public posts. The platform vendor handles its connection/software behavior; the issuing provider controls account assignment and risk permission.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Should I change to Rithmic 01 after passing?
faq.a: Only if that is the new issued assignment.

faq.q: Does a blank quote prove an expired account?
faq.a: No. Session, instrument and data entitlement can explain it.

faq.q: Will liquidation-only clear tomorrow?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Follow the current provider/Rithmic mode rules.

faq.q: Should I open a second session to test?
faq.a: Check concurrent-session permission and existing local dependencies first.

articles.title: Bulenox Rithmic Setup and Compatibility Checks
articles.description: Follow Bulenox's Rithmic connection instructions, check Member's Area credentials, agreements, market data and supported platform settings.
articles.answer: Bulenox’s connection instructions specify the User ID/password from its Member’s Area, Rithmic Paper Trading and the Chicago gateway, with Market Data and Allow Plugins on. This does not mean every third-party Rithmic receiver supports Bulenox.

toc.label: Follow the current Bulenox connection recipe

articles.body:
Follow the current Bulenox connection recipe

  1. Open Bulenox's Connection help page and expand Rithmic Connection.
  2. Obtain the trading credentials from the Member's Area and install the supported RTrader Pro build.
  3. Enter the issued User ID/password and select Rithmic Paper Trading.
  4. Use the documented Chicago gateway or a provider-supported alternative appropriate to the connection.
  5. Set Market Data: On and Allow Plugins: On for this documented recipe.
  6. Read the required agreements and select the subscriber classification that actually applies.
  7. Match the expected account and inspect data entitlement before enabling another client.

Understand what is included

The current Bulenox article describes non-professional exchange data as included with its Qualification Account. Do not extend that statement to every stage, classification or add-on. Obtain the current invoice/terms for other arrangements rather than using a general CME schedule as the retail quote.

PickMyTrade is a material exception

PickMyTrade's Rithmic setup documentation excludes Bulenox from that route. Rithmic connectivity in RTrader does not remove this exclusion. Do not purchase or configure the receiver on the assumption that every Rithmic firm is supported.

If another platform fails

Confirm its current licence/connection eligibility, whether it uses the running Pro host, and matching server settings. Preserve the exact error. An active RTrader session cannot prove a separate API route is authorized. Public native references below do not show a Bulenox account authenticated locally.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Where do I get the trading credentials?
faq.a: Bulenox directs users to the Member’s Area.

faq.q: Does this route use Rithmic 01?
faq.a: The cited setup specifies Rithmic Paper Trading.

faq.q: Can I assume PickMyTrade supports it?

toc.label: Set up the issued Rithmic evaluation

articles.body:
Set up the issued Rithmic evaluation

It gives an exception for a personal NinjaTrader licence with Rithmic integration; confirm the actual entitlement before relying on that route.

Keep stage transitions separate

Passing an evaluation does not prove the same credentials, service or rules continue into another arrangement. Use the newly issued account details and agreement. Recheck account IDs in workspaces, strategies and copier destinations rather than applying a generic funded-equals-Rithmic-01 rule.

articles.title: Check Prop-Firm Rules for a Rithmic Account
articles.description: Check the exact prop-firm plan, account stage, risk rules and automation terms. Rithmic connectivity alone does not establish permission.
articles.answer: Rithmic can enforce configured account limits, but the firm’s agreement defines the program rules. Match the exact account stage and plan. A working connection, visible copier or accepted order does not prove a strategy complies with that agreement.

toc.label: Inspect the configured risk without changing it

articles.body:
Build an account-specific rule sheet

Rule Record precisely
Loss / drawdown Amount, equity reference, intraday/EOD update, enforcement timing and threshold behavior
Position size Instrument limits, pending-order treatment and micro-equivalence policy
Holding Daily cutoff, timezone, news/weekend and delivery restrictions
Copying / automation Ownership, allowed tools, leader/follower arrangement and account-stage restrictions
Program progression Scaling, consistency, minimum days and payout eligibility
Fees Current subscription, reset/activation, data and tool charges

Inspect the configured risk without changing it

The native account context menu exposes View Risk Parameters and the risk window distinguishes FCM/IB/Trader controls. Use the provider-enforced values as account evidence while checking the agreement's calculation and timing. Do not assume every visible field is editable or override a provider limit.

Resolve apparent policy conflicts

Apex's current user agreement imposes ownership and other conditions on copying. Its separately labeled legacy PA help contains additional restrictive language. Do not flatten these into a universal yes/no statement for every plan or account generation. Keep the applicable agreement and request written clarification from the firm when the proposed workflow is unclear.

Rithmic risk documentation explains technical criteria; it cannot establish payout permission or the firm's interpretation of a trading method. Likewise, a third-party vendor's compatibility page cannot waive firm restrictions.

Recheck after changes

Review the rule sheet after a reset, stage transition, plan change or provider notice. Record the source date and actual account ID privately. A historical comparison table is useful context only when each cell still matches the current account terms.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Does an accepted order prove compliance?
faq.a: No. Some program conditions are evaluated separately from order-entry checks.

faq.q: Is a visible copier permission to use it?
faq.a: No. Confirm entitlement and the applicable account agreement.

faq.q: Are micros always counted at 10:1?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Use the firm’s explicit contract-count rule.

faq.q: Can I edit FCM limits myself?
faq.a: Do not assume permission or attempt to bypass provider-enforced limits.

articles.title: Rithmic Trade Copier setup and access checks
articles.description: Find the native R Trader Pro Trade Copier, resolve an access restriction, and understand Copy From, Copy To and the checks required before enabling it.
articles.answer: Open File, then Trade Copier in R Trader Pro desktop. First check whether copy trading is enabled for your login. If the application says it is not enabled, ask the account provider about eligibility and activation. A successful trading login does not establish permission to use the copier.

toc.label: Configure only after the provider confirms eligibility
Validate the relationship before relying on it

articles.body:
Check access before configuring accounts

  1. Confirm the correct provider System and account login.
  2. Open File, then Trade Copier.
  3. Read any access message before selecting accounts.
  4. If access is restricted, keep the message and version for a private provider support request. Do not try to solve it by changing risk limits or repeatedly reinstalling the application.

The inspected window also showed Add Copy From, Add Copy To, Copy Status and Disable All. No account pair was configured and no copying was enabled in this review.

Configure only after the provider confirms eligibility

Lucid's provider guide describes selecting a leader with Add Copy From, adding followers with Add Copy To, setting Quantity Multiple, and enabling the configured relationship. Those instructions describe Lucid's documented workflow; they do not establish permission or matching behavior for every provider.

The illustrated sequence is:

  1. Choose Add Copy From and select the intended source account.
  2. Choose Add Copy To and select the intended receiving accounts.
  3. Review the size setting and each relationship's status before enabling it.
  4. Enable only the relationships permitted for your login and intended workflow.

Before activation, confirm each account identifier, ownership permission, eligible products and maximum intended quantity. Establish which application originates orders and whether another copier or alert route can send the same instruction. A connected account can still reject an order.

Validate the relationship before relying on it

Use a provider-approved simulation to record expected source and destination quantities. Include an entry, its partial fills if supported, a modification, cancellation, exit and reconnect case. Record what happens when a follower rejects a request. Checking only that accounts appear in a list does not establish these outcomes.

Keep positions and working orders visible for every account. Disabling a copying relationship is not proof that existing positions are closed. Review the copier settings guide before changing a multiplier or an active relationship.

Native copying and TradingView automation

A native copier and a service that sends TradingView alerts to multiple accounts are different order paths. Review the current PickMyTrade Rithmic setup documentation for supported connections. Provider permission and account compatibility must be checked separately; the availability of a connection does not grant copying rights.

Provider guides and evidence limits

Lucid's illustrated copier guide shows the account-selection dialogs on pages 3–4 and the size/status controls on page 5. This is a provider-issued reference for the native Rithmic interface, not a screenshot of this enabled login.

Rithmic's release notes for 17.61 state that copying requires administrator permission. Check File → User Profile and ask the account provider about the displayed entitlement. Historical release notes establish the permission model; they do not certify every current account.

DayTraders' guide instructs users to disable the affected relationship before adjusting its settings. Check that provider's terms only if it is your provider; its add-on price is not a universal Rithmic fee.

The inspected login was not enabled for native copying. This article is a documented setup or diagnostic guide; it does not claim that copied orders, partial fills, rounding, cancellations or reconnect recovery were tested. Obtain account-specific confirmation before using behavior that the cited guide does not specify.

faq.q: Why can I log in but not use Trade Copier?
faq.a: The inspected login authenticated successfully but the copier displayed an access restriction. Ask the provider whether the feature is available for that user and account type.

faq.q: Will copying continue if I close the application?
faq.a: Hosting and disconnect behavior were not tested here. Obtain the provider's current specification and validate it in an approved simulation before relying on unattended operation.

faq.q: Can I copy across providers or different logins?
faq.a: This session did not establish that capability. Confirm supported account relationships and each provider's rules rather than assuming that two Rithmic accounts can be paired.

faq.q: Does Disable All close positions?
faq.a: Do not treat it as a flatten command. Inspect each account's actual orders and positions, and use the provider's documented controls for the action intended.

articles.title: Rithmic copy trading settings: accounts, size and status
articles.description: Understand R Trader Pro Copy From, Copy To, Quantity Multiple and Copy Status. Check eligibility and unverified behavior before enabling a relationship.
articles.answer: The native Trade Copier identifies a source with Add Copy From and destinations with Add Copy To. Review account selection, size and copy status before activation. Provider documentation describes a Quantity Multiple, but the inspected login was not enabled, so its configuration and execution could not be tested locally.
articles.body:
Controls and their verification status

Control Purpose Evidence
Add Copy From Select the source account Visible in the local native window
Add Copy To Select a receiving account Visible in the local native window
Copy Status Review the relationship's status Column visible locally; no active relationship tested
Quantity Multiple Configure destination size Described in Lucid's guide; not locally configured
Disable All Control copying relationships Visible locally; not used or tested as an exit command

Check quantity with whole-contract examples

Write down the expected destination quantity before enabling a relationship. For simple multiplication, a source quantity of two and a multiplier of two would imply four destination contracts. That is arithmetic, not a verified native copier fill. Confirm whether the system sizes from submitted orders, fills or positions and how it handles a result that is not a whole contract.

Do not assume a particular fractional-rounding algorithm, micro-to-mini conversion, symbol filters, reverse copying or a list of supported order types. Those details were not established by this inspection. A multiplier does not override destination account restrictions.

Review an existing configuration

  1. Match account identifiers against the provider account list.
  2. Check the relationship's current state and intended direction.
  3. Compare the expected destination quantity with its permitted exposure.
  4. Review existing positions and working orders before changing any relationship.
  5. If the intended workflow depends on modifications, partial fills or recovery, obtain its documented behavior and verify it in an approved simulation before relying on it.

Provider guides and evidence limits

See Lucid's annotated size/status illustration, page 5 beside the locally captured controls above. It is documentation of the interface, not a tested fill ratio.

DayTraders' settings instructions say to disable Copy Status, adjust Quantity Multiplier or Fractional Quantity Rounding, then re-enable after checking the configuration. They do not specify a universal rounding algorithm in that article. Ask for the exact rule if a calculation produces a fractional contract; do not guess.

Rithmic's release notes record multi-account selection in 17.64 and the Copy Trading label in User Profile in 17.68. These versioned references explain terminology; the local capture records the installed version separately.

The inspected login was not enabled for native copying. This article is a documented setup or diagnostic guide; it does not claim that copied orders, partial fills, rounding, cancellations or reconnect recovery were tested. Obtain account-specific confirmation before using behavior that the cited guide does not specify.

faq.q: Is a multiplier a guarantee of matching fills?
faq.a: No. Account restrictions, market conditions and the timing of independent orders can produce different outcomes. Compare execution records, not just configured size.

faq.q: Where are the symbol-filter checkboxes?
faq.a: No such checkboxes were verified in this session. Do not follow a generic guide that assumes they exist in this version.

faq.q: Can I edit a follower manually?
faq.a: Confirm how the copier reconciles manual changes before doing so. A local change may interact with later source events; this review did not test that behavior.

faq.q: Why is the configuration unavailable?
faq.a: The inspected login displayed a provider-controlled access restriction. Follow the setup and eligibility checks.

articles.title: Copy Trading on Rithmic Prop Accounts
articles.description: Check account ownership, firm rules, copying permissions and leader/follower controls before using a Rithmic copier across prop-firm accounts.
articles.answer: Confirm the firm’s rules for the exact account stage and proposed copying arrangement before selecting a tool. A Rithmic connection or visible copier does not establish permission. Account ownership, eligible destinations, sizing and each account’s independent risk limits all matter.

toc.label: Keep the route singular and observable

articles.body:
Check the permitted relationship

Record who owns and controls every account, whether copying crosses firms or account stages, which tool generates the actions and whether another strategy/copier is active. Read the applicable current agreement instead of using a generic firm yes/no list.

Apex's current user agreement includes ownership and additional conditions for copying. Separately labeled legacy PA material can be more restrictive. Apply the agreement for the actual account generation; a vendor's tool compatibility statement cannot resolve a firm-policy conflict.

Check the native copier entitlement

The local File → Trade Copier window exists but says copying is not enabled for this login. Ask the issuing provider about eligibility and terms through its official process before relying on an add-on. DayTraders documents its own add-on; its pricing is not a quote for another firm.

Review each destination

Item Why a leader's success is insufficient
Account status A follower can be restricted or inactive
Permitted quantity Scaling and position limits can differ
Existing exposure A copied action may increase or reverse a different starting position
Margin / drawdown Each account can reject or breach independently
Order and fill state An accepted request is not necessarily a complete fill

Keep the route singular and observable

Avoid overlapping copier paths or a circular relationship. Before individually closing a follower, follow the copier's documented disable/leader sequence. Reconcile all remaining orders and positions afterwards. If using a webhook receiver, verify its account mapping and provider compatibility independently; PickMyTrade's current Rithmic guide excludes Bulenox.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Does owning both accounts automatically permit copying?
faq.a: Ownership can be necessary without being sufficient; check all applicable account conditions.

faq.q: Does a copier bypass the follower risk limit?
faq.a: No. Each destination remains subject to its own checks.

faq.q: Can I assume a same-login restriction or unlimited destinations?
faq.a: Use the selected copier’s actual supported relationship and provider entitlement.

faq.q: Is a public forum reply policy approval?
faq.a: No. Use current official rules and account-specific clarification where needed.

articles.title: Trade Copying vs TradingView Automation on Rithmic
articles.description: Compare leader/follower copying with alert-driven automation, including signal sources, account mapping, exit handling and failure recovery.
articles.answer: Copying replicates activity from a configured leader to destinations. Alert automation turns a selected signal into instructions for a receiving service. They can produce similar-looking trades but have different triggers, dependencies and failure records. Combining them can duplicate exposure.

toc.label: Do not assume every leader action is copied

articles.body:
Compare the event paths

Question Copier workflow Alert workflow
What triggers an action? The copier's documented leader event A selected indicator/strategy alert event
What chooses accounts? The configured source/destination relationship The receiving service's generated account configuration
What needs reconciliation? Leader and every follower order/position Alert delivery, receiver response and broker order/fill
What can fail independently? Relationship, sizing, destination permission/execution Alert conditions, webhook transport, schema, account/risk/execution

Do not assume every leader action is copied

Confirm whether the tool reacts to order submissions, fills, position changes or a narrower event set. A manual-order example does not establish treatment of API-origin orders, partial fills, modifications or recovered sessions. DayTraders' native copier guide provides a setup and shutdown sequence; it does not establish every source-event case on this VPS.

Configure the alert route independently

PickMyTrade's Rithmic strategy guide distinguishes strategy-controlled exits and attached exit arrangements. Use the generator for the selected mode. A TradingView backtest fill is an emulator event, not a Rithmic execution report.

Avoid overlapping paths

If an alert routes directly to several accounts and a native copier also mirrors one of those accounts, the same signal can create more than one order. Draw the actual source-to-destination mapping and give each destination a deliberate execution path. Disabling new signals does not automatically cancel existing orders or close exposure.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Is plugin mode a copier?
faq.a: No. It shares a supported connection with compatible clients.

faq.q: Is every TradingView alert a strategy fill?
faq.a: No. Indicator conditions, alert() events and strategy order-fill events differ.

faq.q: Can I stack copiers to improve reliability?
faq.a: That can duplicate or conflict with actions. Follow the tool’s supported architecture.

faq.q: Do matching signals guarantee matching fills?
faq.a: No. Each destination has its own acceptance and execution outcome.

articles.title: Rithmic Copier Troubleshooting for Rejected Followers
articles.description: Diagnose native Rithmic copier access errors, missing copies, size differences and uncertain follower orders using configuration and execution evidence.
articles.answer: Start with copier access, then the configured account relationship, and finally each account's order and fill records. An absent copy, a rejected follower and a delayed display require different checks. Do not assume one cause from the visible position alone.

toc.label: If copy trading is not enabled

articles.body:
If copy trading is not enabled

Open File, then Trade Copier. In the inspected desktop session, the application said copying was not enabled for this user and directed the user to the provider. A login or reinstall cannot establish the missing entitlement.

Match the symptom to evidence

Symptom Next check
No relationship can be activated Provider eligibility, account access and exact message
No follower order appears Source event, relationship status, destination identifier and order history
Destination quantity differs Size setting, rounding rules, partial fills and existing position
One follower rejects Its complete rejection, account permissions and risk state
Display appears delayed Compare event timestamps and execution records before assuming delayed execution
Unexpected extra order Review other copiers, alerts, retries and manual routes for the same account

Do not assume a failed follower leaves all others unaffected. Inspect every participating account. Different fills require examination; this guide does not prescribe a normal delay or slippage allowance.

Reconcile before retrying

  1. Preserve the source event and its timestamp.
  2. Record the expected destination account, contract, side and quantity.
  3. Check whether a destination order exists, is pending, was rejected or has fills.
  4. Compare current positions and remaining working orders.
  5. Resolve the identified cause before a new instruction.

Do not manually recreate an uncertain copy merely because it is absent from one display. Keep new automation changes separate from investigation so the event sequence remains understandable.

Provider guides and evidence limits

DayTraders' troubleshooting guidance warns that acting on a follower while copying remains active can create an unintended position. Follow its leader-first instructions for its supported workflow and reconcile every account afterward. Do not layer another copier over the same relationship to diagnose a failure.

Rithmic's release notes establish administrator-controlled copying permission. An access error therefore belongs with the account provider; an unexplained order result needs the event and order records described above.

The inspected login was not enabled for native copying. This article is a documented setup or diagnostic guide; it does not claim that copied orders, partial fills, rounding, cancellations or reconnect recovery were tested. Obtain account-specific confirmation before using behavior that the cited guide does not specify.

faq.q: Will restarting restore copier access?
faq.a: Not necessarily. If the message identifies a disabled entitlement, ask the provider about activation and supported accounts.

faq.q: Should I switch to another copier immediately?
faq.a: First reconcile existing positions and orders. A different service still needs supported connections and provider permission; it does not resolve uncertain existing exposure.

faq.q: How should I report a missing copy?
faq.a: Provide the version, System, source event, affected destination, timestamps and exact responses privately. Exclude passwords and API secrets.

faq.q: Are fills expected to match exactly?
faq.a: Do not assume identical fills. Compare the actual records and the copier's documented behavior rather than treating a configured size relationship as an execution guarantee.

articles.title: Multiple Rithmic Accounts in NinjaTrader: Supported Setup Checks
articles.description: Distinguish multiple Rithmic trading accounts from multiple NinjaTrader connections. Check eligibility, account selection and copying support.
articles.answer: Distinguish several trading accounts exposed by one Rithmic connection from several separate Rithmic connections. Multi-provider mode does not by itself prove that an arbitrary set of Rithmic logins can run simultaneously. Check entitlement and the supported combination before configuring a copier or strategy.

toc.label: Several account IDs under one connection

articles.body:
Several account IDs under one connection

Connect through the supported provider recipe, then compare the account choices with the actual provider assignment. Check the Account selection independently in every Chart Trader, SuperDOM and strategy configuration. Selecting a different account does not cancel another account's orders or transfer its position.

The native RTrader capture below shows two account rows under one login. It establishes the account relationship on that session; it does not establish a successful multi-account NinjaTrader test.

Separate logins and Multi-provider

Apex's current setup describes enabling Multi-provider, restarting and adding My Rithmic for NinjaTrader Brokerage. Its reference to an additional personal NinjaTrader Brokerage connection must not be expanded into a promise of unlimited simultaneous Rithmic connections.

Before changing a working setup, get the exact supported provider combination and licence/session conditions from NinjaTrader. Rithmic's onboarding notice also requires new-connection eligibility to be resolved. Saving two connection profiles is not evidence of concurrent operation.

Copying and strategies are separate

Account visibility alone does not activate a copier. Confirm the copier's source, destinations and permitted relationship, then reconcile each destination independently. Do not run multiple copier paths over the same accounts or assume plugin mode copies trades.

articles.title: Measure Rithmic Copy Latency and Fill Differences
articles.description: Measure copying delays between source events, submissions, acknowledgements and fills using matched records and synchronized clocks.
articles.answer: Measure separate timestamps for the source event, destination submission, acknowledgement and fill. Report which interval you measured and how clocks were aligned. This library does not establish a native-copier or PickMyTrade millisecond benchmark.
articles.body:
Define the measurement

Interval What it can show
Source event to destination request Replication/dispatch delay under the selected event definition
Destination request to acknowledgement Acceptance response time
Acknowledgement to fill Execution timing, including waiting and partial fills
Source fill price versus follower fill price Fill difference; not solely caused by software delay

Use matching order/event identifiers, timestamps with timezone and known clock precision. Clock skew can make a destination appear to precede the source. A screenshot rounded to whole seconds cannot support a sub-millisecond claim.

Collect comparable observations

Use suitable existing records or a provider-permitted demonstration. Keep contract, side, quantity, order type, account stage and session conditions with every observation. Report sample size, median, upper percentiles, extremes and failures separately; do not remove slow or rejected events to improve the headline.

For illustration only, source-to-destination intervals of 12, 18 and 90 milliseconds have a median of 18 milliseconds and a worst observed value of 90 milliseconds. These invented numbers explain reporting, not measured product performance.

Interpret carefully

An identical signal does not guarantee equal queue position, full quantity or fill price. More destinations can add load and competing orders; no parallel-dispatch architecture was verified here. A VPS affects components actually running on it, not automatically every cloud/server interval.

Use Rithmic order history to locate available records, and distinguish its displayed timestamps from a recipient's delivery log. The empty native history capture below identifies controls only; it is not a timing dataset.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Does a one-millisecond ping mean one-millisecond fills?
faq.a: No. Network round trip and order execution are different measurements.

faq.q: Does ten accounts mean exactly ten times the delay?
faq.a: No universal scaling law was established. Measure the actual configuration.

faq.q: Can source and follower prices differ even with low delay?
faq.a: Yes. Size, queue position and market changes can affect fills.

faq.q: Is the numeric example a benchmark?
faq.a: No. It is explicitly illustrative arithmetic.
