articles.answer: PickMyTrade documents multiple Rithmic connections, but connecting an account does not automatically make it a destination for every alert. Resolve the accounts and quantities in the current generator, then reconcile each destination’s response and broker records independently.
articles.body:
Add supported connections

The current Rithmic setup guide describes Broker Connections → Rithmic → Rithmic Connection → Add Connection, entering the Rithmic credentials and matching System Name, then Connect. The documented resolved status is Connected.

Use the Rithmic-specific registration route described by the guide; it says an existing Tradovate registration does not replace that step. Its stated additional-connection price is $50/month, but confirm the actual current billing unit and invoice before extrapolating a per-account total.

Generate the account-specific message

Choose the intended broker, indicator/strategy mode, symbol and supported destination configuration in Generate Alert Code. Compare the resulting account IDs and quantities with the intended account map. Do not use a generic action/qty template: the published reference uses different fields and route-specific semantics.

Bulenox is excluded from the cited route. The temporary public Rithmic trial also does not provide the required Protocol access. An eligible prop simulation is a different account category; verify it with the provider and service.

Reconcile every destination

For each alert, retain delivery status, recipient validation, destination order IDs, accepted quantity, fills and final positions. One account's success does not establish another's result. Before replaying a failed-looking alert, identify whether any destinations already acted.

On 8 October 2026, the authenticated PickMyTrade session showed an existing Rithmic connection marked Connected and two available accounts. The current generator produced an unsaved documentation message for those two destinations. The displayed 8 September–9 October history range contained no alert logs or orders. The one existing saved configuration was for IB, not Rithmic. No message was sent, no TradingView alert was saved, and no order was submitted. The generated JSON contained two multiple_accounts entries, each with quantity_multiplier: 1 and risk_percentage: 0, against top-level quantity: 1. This establishes selected destinations in the generated configuration, not accepted quantities or fills.

Observed account selection

The authenticated Connected Accounts screen showed one connection and two sub-accounts. In Generate Alert Code, Add Account opened Add Trading Account, with Sub-account of my login and Another Rithmic login choices. The observed sub-account path exposed connection, account and position-sizing controls. Add To Account List, followed by Confirm & Generate Alert Code, generated the documentation message. Save Alert was a separate control and was not used. No new broker login was connected.

Find each destination result

Sources: PickMyTrade Alerts guide and Orders guide, checked 8 October 2026. Compare time, connection, account, symbol and identifiers in your own records. An alert status and an order status describe different stages; reconcile the broker's own order/fill history before concluding that a trade filled. These vendor examples are separate illustrations, not a verified matched execution chain.

articles.title: Rithmic Copy-Trading Risks and Account Reconciliation
articles.description: Review copied exposure, account limits, partial fills and shutdown sequences. Understand why follower outcomes can differ from the leader.
articles.answer: Copying can multiply correlated exposure while each account still has its own starting position, limits and execution result. Review every destination independently. Matching account size or a multiplier setting does not prove equal risk or identical fills.

toc.label: Review before enabling or changing a relationship
Manage a follower independently only through the supported sequence

articles.body:
Common failure paths

Risk Example
Correlated loss Three accounts each losing an illustrative $500 total $1,500 before further costs
Unequal headroom A follower near its actual floor can breach before the leader
Quantity mismatch A multiplier or rounding result exceeds a follower's limit
Different starting exposure The same action closes one account but reverses another
Partial/rejected copies Account positions diverge despite one source event
Duplicate paths A second copier or direct alert adds unintended orders
Policy mismatch A technically working arrangement violates an account-stage rule

Review before enabling or changing a relationship

Match full account IDs and existing positions. Establish expected destination quantity, rounding and supported event handling. Check actual risk criteria rather than using advertised account size as headroom. A smaller multiplier is not proof of an acceptable maximum loss.

The native dashboard below shows relevant account fields, with private details concealed. Its blank headroom cells do not supply a numerical allowance; obtain the provider's actual values and calculation rules.

Manage a follower independently only through the supported sequence

DayTraders' copier instructions warn that an independently flattened follower can receive a later copied action and end up reversed. Disable the affected copying relationship as documented before independent management, and reconcile positions and working orders afterwards. Disabling copying is not itself flattening.

Treat limits as independent

Check the applicable firm rules, technical entitlement and tool compatibility separately. A test in an eligible simulation helps establish behavior but cannot guarantee live fill quality or future availability.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Do several copied accounts diversify the trade?
faq.a: Repeating the same exposure does not diversify that market risk.

faq.q: Can one follower reject while others fill?
faq.a: Yes; reconcile each actual result rather than inferring a shared outcome.

faq.q: Does disabling copying close the follower?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Check orders and positions independently.

faq.q: Can a small micro test guarantee future behavior?
faq.a: No. It covers only its tested configuration and conditions.

Compare by job

Approach Useful when Essential check

Diagnose the native limitation first

Evaluate an alert receiver accurately

That is not a blanket cross-firm copying promise. A cloud receiver needs a valid signal, destination configuration and separate result monitoring.

Build a meaningful comparison

Record eligible source/destination accounts, event types, exit dependencies, reject/reconnect behavior, account limits and total recurring cost. Include exchange data and optional add-ons, not just a headline software price. Require dated evidence for a speed claim. Do not install overlapping copiers on the same destinations while comparing them.

faq.q: Is manual selection copying?

articles.description: Separate TradingView alert triggers, HTTP delivery, PickMyTrade validation and Rithmic order outcomes. Check logs, retries and account scope safely.
articles.answer: Find the first missing stage: the TradingView alert event, webhook delivery, receiving-service record or Rithmic order response. A fired alert is not proof of a fill. Preserve timestamps and logs before changing settings or resending anything. TradingView documents retries for certain HTTP server errors, so do not assume one trigger can produce only one delivery.

toc.label: Start with the evidence you have
4. Check the recipient and Rithmic separately

articles.body:
Start with the evidence you have

Last confirmed stage Next useful check
Strategy/indicator signal on chart Was a running alert created for the intended event?
Alert in TradingView Log Webhook URL configuration and Webhook status
HTTP delivery result Receiving-service record and payload validation
Service accepted the alert Intended connection/account and recorded order request
Broker acknowledged a request Actual working, rejected, canceled or filled state

If an order outcome is uncertain, check the account/order record before resending the alert. A timeout may leave the recipient's processing outcome unknown.

1. Confirm the running alert

Check its enabled state, condition, symbol, timeframe and expiration. For script alerts, TradingView uses a saved script/input/chart context. Changing the chart or script inputs does not update that existing snapshot; recreate the alert when that context must change, following TradingView's alert documentation.

Match the event to the integration: an indicator condition, alert() call and strategy order-fill event are different sources. Selecting both event streams can send two requests only if both actually trigger and contain trade messages. Inspect the timeline instead of assuming duplication.

2. Inspect webhook delivery

The official webhook configuration guide documents the notification field, two-factor requirement and Webhook status column. Use the exact endpoint copied from the receiving application. Do not guess a PickMyTrade URL path.

Result family Investigate
Redirect Changed endpoint or authorization redirect
Client error Access, endpoint, formatting or request limit
Server error Receiving-service failure and possible resend
Timeout/unavailable URL Response time, public reachability and endpoint correctness

These are diagnostic categories from TradingView's error guide, not invented PickMyTrade error strings. A localhost preview address is not a public receiving endpoint.

3. Account for retries

TradingView's resubmission guide says HTTP 500–599 responses, except 504, can cause resends at five-second intervals, with at most four sends for one trigger. Do not extrapolate this to every timeout or every error. It does not establish how the receiving service prevents duplicate orders.

4. Check the recipient and Rithmic separately

For PickMyTrade, use its current generated account-specific message. Compare signal type, connection/account, contract, quantity and exit mode. Its published JSON reference uses data and quantity; replacing them with guessed action and qty is not a verified repair. The reference is not a substitute for the current generator or a tested payload.

Preserve any service validation error and the broker response. Confirm the resolved contract and account before interpreting “success.” The native quote captured here shows ESZ6 data, not a webhook result:

If the service record is missing despite a reported delivery, provide the timestamp/timezone and redacted request context through official support. Do not post tokens, passwords or private account/order IDs publicly.

faq.q: Does HTTP success mean the trade filled?
faq.a: No. Verify receiving-service validation, order acknowledgement and the recorded fill separately.

faq.q: Does TradingView never retry?
faq.a: It documents conditional resubmission for certain server-error responses. Do not infer universal retry or recipient deduplication from that rule.

faq.q: Should I resend a timed-out alert?
faq.a: First reconcile the receiving-service and broker records. A second send can produce another request when the earlier outcome is unknown.

faq.q: Will changing the chart fix an existing script alert?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Its saved context remains separate; recreate it when that context needs to change.

articles.title: Pine Script Alerts for Rithmic: Event and Message Setup
articles.description: Choose the correct Pine alert event for a Rithmic receiving service and distinguish strategy simulation, webhook delivery and broker execution.
articles.answer: Choose the Pine event that should trigger automation, then use the current receiver-generated message for that event type. A strategy’s simulated order-fill alert is not a Rithmic fill. Indicator conditions and alert() events have different behavior and cannot be treated as interchangeable strategy events.

toc.label: Keep order quantity and position size separate
Realtime behavior needs its own check

articles.body:
Choose the event source

Pine / alert feature Role
Indicator alertcondition() Defines a selectable indicator condition
alert() Emits an alert event with a script-defined message when its code executes
Strategy order-fill event Reports a TradingView broker-emulator fill
Order function alert_message Provides order-specific text used with the appropriate strategy alert placeholder

See TradingView's Pine alert documentation. Alerts run on saved server-side context. Changing a chart, input or script does not automatically update an already running alert; recreate it when the intended context changes.

Keep order quantity and position size separate

{{strategy.order.action}} and {{strategy.order.contracts}} describe an order event. {{strategy.position_size}} describes position state. A reversal can require an order larger than the intended final position, so blindly substituting one quantity for another can mis-size the receiver's action.

If the script uses order-specific alert_message, the alert needs the corresponding {{strategy.order.alert_message}} placeholder. Do not assume every order function supplied text, or combine a custom message with an incompatible generator template.

Configure the receiving service

In PickMyTrade, choose the Rithmic strategy or indicator mode that matches the event. Use its current strategy instructions and generated configuration. Preserve the exact account, symbol, sizing and exit mode. This guide deliberately does not invent a runnable order schema.

Realtime behavior needs its own check

Intrabar recalculation, repainting and order timing can make realtime behavior differ from historical results. Record the script settings and event frequency. Prevent duplicate execution paths, and reconcile an emulator event with the recipient response and broker records before treating it as successful automation. See the account-specific JSON verification, which remains distinct from these Pine event concepts.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Does Pine connect directly to Rithmic?
faq.a: The described workflow uses TradingView alerts and a supported receiving service; Pine is not a Rithmic login client.

faq.q: Do strategy placeholders apply to any indicator?
faq.a: No. Use the event and message features supported by the selected script type.

faq.q: Will editing my chart update a running alert?
faq.a: TradingView saves alert context; recreate it when the intended context changes.

faq.q: Does a backtest prove the live order path?
faq.a: No. Emulator events and broker execution are separate.

articles.title: TradingView to Rithmic Symbol Mapping: Check the Actual Contract
articles.description: Distinguish TradingView chart symbols, Rithmic display names and PickMyTrade payload symbols. Verify execution contracts and avoid rollover assumptions.
articles.answer: Keep the chart symbol, generated alert symbol and actual execution contract separate. Do not automatically replace ES1! with a dotted Rithmic display name in the webhook. Use the symbol selected and generated for the intended PickMyTrade connection, then verify the destination contract.

toc.label: Rollover is not the same as moving a position

articles.body:
Three values to compare

Value Example or source Why to check it
TradingView chart symbol A continuous chart or a specific expiry Identifies the series generating the signal
PickMyTrade alert symbol The current generated message Identifies what the route is being asked to resolve
Rithmic execution contract The actual destination order Establishes which contract received the request

In the web session inspected on 7 October 2026, the ES view showed the front month as ESZ6.CME. This is a dated display observation, not evidence that every webhook accepts that string.

Verify a mapping

  1. Record the TradingView symbol and whether it is continuous or expiry-specific.
  2. Select the intended execution symbol in PickMyTrade. The Rithmic strategy guide describes symbol selection and setting up missing mappings.
  3. Generate the alert message for the correct connection. Preserve the generated syntax rather than manually adding an exchange suffix.
  4. Inspect a resolved alert in a suitable permitted test. Compare the requested symbol with the destination order's contract month and exchange.
  5. Repeat the check after a rollover or a change in mapping, strategy, account or alert configuration.

Rollover is not the same as moving a position

PickMyTrade's rollover document, updated 29 September 2026, recommends selecting the exact contract and describes continuous-symbol switching four days before expiry. It also says that existing futures positions are not automatically managed at expiration. Those are different operations.

The document does not prove that every instrument and Rithmic account observed here follows an identical transition. Confirm the destination contract around expiry; retain any open-position management decision separately.

If the symbol is rejected

Compare the generated value, the saved mapping, connection choice and available instrument. Preserve the exact error. Do not use another instrument merely because it produces a successful order, and do not infer that a mini and micro are interchangeable quantities.

Captured reference images

The captions distinguish observed web screens from vendor documentation and imported desktop references. None proves a successful order or the unobserved desktop workflow.

What this mapping reference establishes

The native ES lookup and official generator illustration establish the distinction between a platform contract label and a receiver-selected symbol. They do not establish a completed TradingView-to-Rithmic order. The account-specific generator/outcome check belongs to the linked setup and JSON validation workflow; use its actual result before relying on a new mapping.

The CME customary equity roll calendar now uses a Monday convention. That exchange reference and the receiver's documented mapping schedule are separate; compare both with the actual destination expiry.

Native contract-reference observation

On this VPS, entering ESZ6.CME in the native Quote Board symbol cell and leaving it resolved an ESZ6 / E-Mini S&P 500 quote row. This supports identification of that native contract only. It does not establish PickMyTrade's generated payload format or a TradingView-to-execution mapping result.

faq.q: Must I hardcode every symbol?
faq.a: No universal rule is established. Use the documented generated configuration for the route and verify the intended result.

faq.q: Does a continuous chart determine the execution expiry?
faq.a: Not by itself. The chart and the receiving service may follow different rollover rules.

faq.q: Does automatic mapping close an old position?
faq.a: No such behavior should be inferred. Mapping a new alert and managing an existing position are separate tasks.

faq.q: Is the October screenshot a current symbol list for future dates?
faq.a: No. It records one instrument in one session on 7 October 2026. Check the contract intended at the time you configure the alert.

articles.title: TradingView Alert Types for Rithmic
articles.description: Choose the intended indicator, alert() or strategy order-fill event. Separate simulated strategy fills from broker fills and avoid overlapping trade alerts.
articles.answer: Choose the alert event that the script and receiving integration are designed to use. A strategy order-fill event comes from TradingView's broker emulator; it is not a fill report from your Rithmic account. An alert() event occurs when the script calls that function. Using both is not automatically correct for every integration.

toc.label: When can two streams cause duplicate requests?

articles.body:
Compare the event sources

Source What triggers it What to verify
Price or drawing alert The configured chart condition Whether the message has the recipient's intended meaning
Indicator condition Its supported condition or script event Condition, message and frequency
alert() call Script logic executes the function Which calls carry trade instructions
Strategy order-fill event Emulator fills the strategy's simulated order Required placeholder/message and intended integration

TradingView's Pine alert guide documents these distinctions. Creating an event in code does not itself create a running alert; the user must configure the alert through the supported interface.

Choose using the script's contract

  1. Identify whether the script is an indicator or strategy and obtain its alert instructions.
  2. Determine whether its trade messages come from order-fill events, alert() calls or a specific indicator condition.
  3. Match the receiving service's generated message to that event source.
  4. Check entry, exit, reversal and partial-exit instructions separately. Do not treat every event as an entry.
  5. Recreate a script alert when its saved inputs/symbol/timeframe context must change.
  6. Inspect actual alert, receiving-service and broker records during an appropriate permitted verification process.

No alert was created or trade triggered for this article.

Keep exit modes consistent

PickMyTrade's Rithmic strategy guide distinguishes strategy-controlled exits, attached SL/TP and multiple exits. The vendor illustration below identifies those choices. It is not proof of their behavior on your account, and its NQM6 example is not a current contract recommendation.

When can two streams cause duplicate requests?

If both an order-fill event and an alert() call trigger with trade instructions, they can produce separate messages. Check both sources and the actual timeline. A setting that permits adding to a position is not the same as transport-level deduplication. See duplicate-order reconciliation.

faq.q: Should every strategy use Order fills only?
faq.a: Use the script and integration's current instructions. Some workflows use explicit alert() messages instead.

faq.q: Is a strategy fill a Rithmic fill?
faq.a: No. It is an emulator event; confirm the actual broker result separately.

faq.q: Does selecting both always double trades?
faq.a: No. That depends on which events actually trigger, their messages and receiving-service behavior.

faq.q: Do changed chart inputs update an existing alert?
faq.a: TradingView documents a saved context. Recreate the script alert when that context needs to change.

articles.title: TradingView Plans for Rithmic Alerts: Webhooks and Capacity
articles.description: Check the current TradingView webhook and technical-alert comparison, separate alert capacity from data access, and confirm two-factor authentication.
articles.answer: The official comparison inspected on 7 October 2026 shows webhook notifications from Essential upward; Basic does not include them. Check the separate technical-alert capacity and duration for the alerts you actually need, and enable required two-factor authentication. A subscription does not establish Rithmic account permission, exchange-data access or a tested automation route.

toc.label: Check capacity before choosing a tier

articles.body:
Current published comparison

The official pricing/features page showed:

Plan Webhook notifications Active technical alerts
Basic Not included Not included in the inspected row
Essential Included 20
Plus Included 100
Premium Included 400
Ultimate Included 1,000

Technical alerts are listed separately from price and watchlist alerts. Do not add those different categories and present the sum as available strategy-alert slots. The captured table is a dated public comparison, not an inspection of your subscription or a purchasing recommendation.

Check capacity before choosing a tier

  1. List the technical alerts required by the intended scripts and symbols.
  2. Include separate entry/exit alerts only when the integration actually requires them.
  3. Compare that number with the relevant current capacity, not only the price-alert limit.
  4. Check alert expiration/duration and plan-dependent features used by the script.
  5. Confirm classification, billing period, taxes and current terms directly before any purchase.

No universal monthly price is quoted here. The public page can show annual-billing equivalents and promotional/regional conditions; those are not necessarily the final monthly checkout amount.

Webhook access has separate prerequisites

TradingView's webhook guide requires two-factor authentication for webhooks. Use the account's current security interface to confirm it. This review did not change security settings or inspect a private account's enabled state.

Rithmic exchange data and the bridge/account connection also have separate requirements. Having a TradingView paid plan does not give you every exchange subscription or authorize copying and automation at a funding provider.

faq.q: Is Basic enough for the documented webhook workflow?
faq.a: The inspected comparison does not include webhook notifications on Basic. Verify the current official offering and account features.

faq.q: Can I use the price-alert count as my strategy-alert limit?
faq.a: No. Check the technical-alert category that covers indicators, strategies and drawings.

faq.q: Does a higher plan guarantee faster execution?
faq.a: No execution benchmark was established. Alert triggering, network delivery, recipient processing and broker results remain separate.

faq.q: Does upgrading update my existing script alerts?
faq.a: Do not assume it updates their saved script/input/chart context. Follow the current alert documentation when changing that context.

articles.title: TradingView Backtesting vs Rithmic Execution
articles.description: Distinguish strategy emulator results, live alert events and Rithmic fills. Investigate differences in data, timing, quantity, costs and exit handling.
articles.answer: A TradingView backtest simulates orders with its broker emulator. It does not execute those historical orders in Rithmic. Compare the emulator event, running alert, receiving-service request and actual broker result as separate records. Data, timing, sizing, costs and exit rules can differ; a profitable backtest does not establish later execution or returns.
articles.body:
What are you comparing?

Record What it establishes
Strategy Tester result Simulated behavior under the configured data and assumptions
Running strategy alert An event from the saved alert context
Webhook record Delivery/recipient processing evidence
Rithmic acknowledgement Recorded order-response stage
Broker fill Actual executed quantity, price and time

TradingView's broker-emulator explanation describes the simulation layer. Its Pine alert guide explains strategy order-fill events and saved alert context. Do not call an emulator fill a live broker fill.

Investigate a difference in stages

  1. Match the intended contract, expiry, exchange and timeframe. A continuous chart can differ from the execution contract.
  2. Record strategy inputs and the context saved when the running alert was created.
  3. Check when the live alert event fired rather than assuming the historical bar event occurred identically.
  4. Compare the generated message's intended side/quantity/exit meaning with the receiver's recorded request.
  5. Compare actual acknowledgements and fills, including partial execution or rejection.
  6. Reconcile commission, slippage assumptions, timestamps and position accounting without promising they will match the simulation.

This is a comparison procedure. No strategy was run or trade placed for the article.

Check sizing and exits separately

Strategy position size, order quantity, a receiving-service quantity multiplier and risk-based sizing are different inputs. Likewise, strategy-controlled exits and attached protective orders are different workflows. Use the exact integration instructions; do not impose one numeric slippage setting or exit template on every account.

A native quote view is only market-data evidence:

faq.q: Does an order-fill strategy alert prove a Rithmic fill?
faq.a: No. It comes from the emulator's event; verify the actual broker record.

faq.q: Does a successful webhook prove the backtest can be reproduced?
faq.a: No. It is one transport/processing observation, not a performance comparison.

faq.q: Should I use a fixed two-tick slippage assumption?
faq.a: No universal setting is established. Use a justified assumption for the contract/workflow and compare it with actual recorded outcomes.

faq.q: Can I backtest historical webhook delivery?
faq.a: A historical strategy report is not a historical delivery log for your external integration. Those require separate evidence.

articles.title: Rithmic Latency: Measure the Stage Before Changing the Setup
articles.description: Measure Rithmic delays by stage, distinguish network ping from fills, and compare supported gateway or workload changes without promising a speed result.
articles.answer: Define the delay you want to measure: alert triggering, webhook delivery, recipient processing, order acknowledgement, fill or quote display. Record comparable timestamps before changing the setup. A lower network ping, nearby VPS or marketed API latency is not a measured guarantee of your end-to-end result.

toc.label: What common suggestions do not prove

articles.body:
Identify the stage

Stage Useful evidence Limit
Signal to alert Script context and actual trigger time Historical backtest timing is not a live event
Alert to recipient Delivery/service timestamps Clocks and timezones must be reconciled
Recipient to acknowledgement Recorded request and broker response Does not establish a fill
Acknowledgement to fill Broker execution records Depends on order conditions and market state
Market event to display Source and display timing A screenshot alone does not measure the interval

No benchmark was performed for this guide. The native quote reference supplies actual field context, not a measured elapsed time:

Compare changes deliberately

  1. Fix the same product/expiry, application version and workload for a comparison.
  2. Record the exact event definition and timestamp source, including timezone.
  3. Identify local-plugin, direct or cloud dependencies.
  4. Change one supported variable at a time when interrupting the workflow is appropriate.
  5. Record the resulting observations and failures, not only the best single sample.
  6. Confirm account/order state before relying on a restored or altered route.

The native Rithmic 01 menu exposes specific Gateway labels. These are actual choices in that observed form, not a latency ranking or proof of availability for every provider:

What common suggestions do not prove

Moving software to a VPS changes part of the host/network environment. Reducing a measured workload can help investigate a display bottleneck. Selecting a supported gateway can test a route difference. None establishes that provider entitlement, chart context, signal generation or exchange fill behavior has been fixed.

Quantower documents its local plugin route. TradingView describes webhook delivery, including a receiver-response limit. Those are different stages. Rithmic's API performance descriptions also use their own stated measurement basis; do not present them as your account's order-to-fill benchmark.

faq.q: Is ping the same as order latency?
faq.a: No. A host's network response is different from application processing, broker acknowledgement and a fill.

faq.q: Is the nearest gateway always fastest?
faq.a: No comparison was established here. Use supported choices and measure the intended route.

faq.q: Does a higher TradingView plan guarantee quicker fills?
faq.a: No. Plan features do not establish the complete execution timeline.

faq.q: Can a screenshot prove a millisecond claim?
faq.a: A static image records visible fields at a moment. A reproducible timing method and event records are needed for elapsed-time claims.

articles.title: Rithmic Automated Trading: Choose and Verify the Execution Route
articles.description: Compare desktop strategies, cloud alerts and direct Rithmic APIs, then check account permission, order handling and monitoring for the chosen route.
articles.answer: Choose whether the automation runs in a desktop platform, a cloud alert receiver or a direct Rithmic API application. Each route has different account permissions, hosting dependencies and validation requirements. A working manual RTrader login does not establish every automated route.
articles.body:
Compare the architectures

Route Required configuration Main operational dependency
Desktop strategy Supported platform/edition, connection, account and strategy settings Host application and its order-management logic
TradingView receiver Correct alert event, generated message, endpoint and eligible account Alert service, receiver and broker response chain
Direct API Appropriate API access, developer setup and required conformance/production process Your application, credentials, session and recovery implementation

Rithmic's API directory distinguishes API+, Protocol and other products. Do not choose a protocol or fee from an old blog without current onboarding terms. The public 14-day demo's Protocol restriction matters when evaluating a cloud receiver.

Configure before enabling

Map account IDs, contracts, quantity units, exit handling and the expected source of each event. Document which component creates or trails protective orders, which cancels companions and what survives a lost client session. Native server-held orders and local strategy logic are not the same thing.

For PickMyTrade's Rithmic route, use the supported connection and generator; Bulenox is excluded. Do not substitute generic JSON or infer firm permission from technical compatibility.

Establish a recovery record

Use an eligible provider-permitted simulation or suitable existing records to match signal, request, acceptance, fills and final position. Cover duplicate delivery, partial/rejected orders and restart behavior for the intended architecture. Do not reconnect by blindly replaying the last signal.

Keep current account rules, software/data fees and hosting requirements with the configuration. A cloud receiver may remove the need to host that component yourself, but it does not remove every dependency or prove continuous availability.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Does any Rithmic demo support Protocol?
faq.a: The current public temporary trial does not; verify the eligible account category.

faq.q: Does automation guarantee protective exits?
faq.a: No. Confirm each resulting order and the component managing it.

faq.q: Is a VPS always required?
faq.a: Only for components you choose to host there; architecture determines the requirement.

faq.q: Does API access establish firm permission?
faq.a: No. Read the applicable account agreement separately.

articles.title: Rithmic Colocation vs a Chicago VPS
articles.description: Distinguish a Chicago VPS from exchange colocation and measure the relevant Rithmic connection path before making latency claims.
articles.answer: A VPS in the Chicago area is not automatically exchange colocation. Identify where each software component runs and which network path it uses. Physical proximity can shorten part of a path, but it does not prove end-to-end order latency or fill quality.
articles.body:
Compare hosting terms precisely

Term What to establish
Regional VPS Actual data center, shared/dedicated resources and provider network route
Dedicated host Resource isolation, management and network connectivity
Colocation Named facility, equipment placement and the contracted connectivity
API/service endpoint The supported access point for your account/application

Map the full path

For a desktop strategy, consider signal computation, local processing, network transmission, risk checks and exchange response. For TradingView plus a cloud receiver, the signal and receiver may run elsewhere; moving a monitoring desktop does not relocate those components.

Rithmic's API directory describes distinct API products and access requirements. Marketing latency figures for one product or architecture are not a benchmark for a retail VPS, plugin client or webhook service.

Evaluate a hosting proposal

Ask for the actual facility and permitted endpoint, resource guarantees, Windows licence, backup/recovery provisions, maintenance policy and all recurring charges. Measure the relevant interval using comparable conditions and aligned clocks. Do not probe guessed private gateway addresses or interpret a generic website ping as the order path.

Keep the benchmark honest

Record sample count, load, gateway, timestamps and failures. Ping measures network round trip only where the destination permits it; missing ICMP responses do not prove the trading service is down. Microsoft's time-accuracy guidance explains why merely enabling time synchronization does not establish precise cross-host measurement.

No colocation service was purchased or measured in this library. The native Gateway dropdown below shows available labels, not the machine's physical location or a latency guarantee.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Is Chicago Area proof my VPS is colocated?
faq.a: No. It is a selected gateway label.

faq.q: Does one-millisecond ping prove one-millisecond execution?
faq.a: No. It omits processing, risk, queue and fill behavior.

faq.q: Will moving a desktop speed up a cloud receiver?
faq.a: Only components and paths actually moved can change; measure the whole route.

faq.q: Are price ranges universal?
faq.a: No. Compare dated quotes with the same resources, connectivity and management scope.

articles.title: Monitor Rithmic Trading Results from Fills and Costs
articles.description: Calculate trading performance from reconciled fills, fees and a defined trade-grouping method. Separate execution records from alerts and orders.
articles.answer: Start with reconciled fills, account, contract, timezone and fees. Then calculate result metrics using a stated trade-grouping method. An alert log, working order or screenshot of a P&L field is not a complete performance record.
articles.body:
Obtain the correct records

The inspected desktop exposes File → Order History and Fill History. Order History includes account/date filters; an export control was observed in the earlier native inspection. These captures were empty and do not prove a populated export, its schema or retention period.

Use the available filled-order records and verify the resulting file against the provider statement. Before importing into a journal, check that it supports the actual file format, timezone, commissions and contract naming. Do not assume every CSV importer understands a Rithmic export.

Define the metrics

Metric Definition and caution
Net result Realized gross result minus applicable costs, using a stated period
Win rate Winning closed trades divided by closed trades; define a trade first
Average win/loss Average positive/negative result under the same cost convention
Profit factor Gross winning sum divided by absolute gross losing sum; undefined if no losing sum
Drawdown Peak-to-trough decline in the chosen series; realized-only and marked equity differ
Expectancy Average result per defined trade over the sample; not a future-profit guarantee

For illustration, six $100 winners and four $120 losers produce $120 before costs: $600 minus $480. Win rate is 60%, and gross profit factor is 1.25. Additional costs can reduce or reverse the net result. No universal 1.5 target or 50-trade sample establishes viability.

Reconcile before interpreting

Check partial fills, scaling, reversals, duplicates, fees and missing days. Keep each account separate before combining totals. A prop rule may monitor intraday marked equity even if a journal plots only closed-trade results. Explain the difference rather than forcing the charts to agree.

Protect private IDs and retain source records outside public reports. The figures below locate controls; they are not a real trading-performance dataset.

Screenshot references

faq.q: Is a high win rate sufficient?
faq.a: No. Loss size, costs and sample behavior also matter.

faq.q: Does profit factor above one prove net profitability?
faq.a: Only under the stated calculation; omitted costs and sample limitations matter.

faq.q: Can I import any CSV into any journal?
faq.a: No. Match the actual supported schema and reconcile totals.

faq.q: Is account drawdown the same as journal drawdown?
faq.a: Not necessarily. They may use different equity references and timing.

articles.title: Diagnose Rithmic Network Delays Before Changing Settings
articles.description: Diagnose Rithmic network problems by separating remote-desktop lag, market-data delay and order response time before changing settings.
articles.answer: Separate remote-desktop lag, delayed market data and slow order responses. Compare timestamps and logs before changing the network. A DNS change, VPN removal or nearby VPS does not automatically improve an already established trading connection.
articles.body:
Identify the delayed component

Observation Useful comparison
RDP screen redraw is slow Check host application timestamps and host resource use
Quote timestamps fall behind Compare contracts, sessions and the market-data connection
Order acknowledgement is delayed Match request and broker-response records
Reconnect fails during name lookup Investigate DNS and the supported endpoint
Several applications disconnect together Investigate the shared host/network path and provider notices

Change one justified variable

On a local computer, compare a stable wired connection with the existing link if appropriate. On a VPS, a virtual Ethernet adapter does not prove the underlying network has no congestion. Check scheduled uploads/downloads and bandwidth saturation without disabling necessary security or backups indiscriminately.

A VPN may be part of the required secure access architecture. Do not turn it off as a generic latency fix. DNS mainly affects resolving an endpoint; changing resolvers is not evidence of lower latency on an established session. Router QoS is relevant only when the controlled bottleneck and supported traffic policy justify it.

Use the correct diagnostics

Obtain permitted endpoints and protocols from the provider. Do not assume every gateway answers ICMP or use a public website's HTTPS response as proof the trading service works. Preserve packet-loss/reconnect timestamps and the exact application error; a single successful ping cannot establish stability.

Evaluate the result

Compare the same workload and interval before/after a change. Use aligned clocks and distinguish median behavior from bursts and failures. Microsoft's time guidance identifies network and resource conditions that affect clock accuracy. No fixed millisecond improvement was measured here.

faq.q: Does faster DNS always mean faster fills?
faq.a: No. It is not a measure of the established order path.

faq.q: Should I disable the firewall?
faq.a: No. Use the provider’s exact supported requirements and narrow diagnosis.

faq.q: Does ping failure prove an outage?
faq.a: No. ICMP may be filtered while the application service remains reachable.

faq.a: Yes. The display and trading paths are different; inspect actual state.

articles.title: Reduce Rithmic Platform CPU Load with Measured Changes
articles.description: Use Task Manager to identify processing, memory and disk pressure, then reduce unnecessary chart and history workloads one change at a time.
articles.answer: Use Task Manager to identify sustained processing, memory or disk pressure during the actual trading workload. Reduce unnecessary chart/history work one change at a time. High total CPU can matter, but a universal 70–80% threshold or a process-priority change is not a verified cure for Rithmic disconnects.
articles.body:
Inspect the workload

Open Task Manager with Ctrl+Shift+Esc. Inspect Processes for CPU/memory usage and Performance for CPU, memory, disk and network behavior. Microsoft describes these monitoring tools. A brief snapshot taken while idle does not diagnose a burst at the market open.

Record platform version, active workspaces, chart/indicator count, instruments and requested history. One saturated execution thread can be a problem even when the overall CPU percentage is modest. Memory pressure and disk paging can resemble a CPU problem.

Reduce work deliberately

Change to evaluate What to observe
Remove unused charts/indicators Application response and CPU under comparable data load
Reduce initial history range Startup load and completeness of the required analysis
Reduce unnecessary subscriptions Data-processing volume and missing required instruments
Adjust supported display refresh/aggregation Resource savings versus lost analysis detail
Schedule heavy background work Contention without weakening security or recovery

Do not disable a strategy's needed data or change intrabar behavior merely to make a usage graph lower. Bookmap warns that aggregation can hinder MBO functionality; ATAS also requires matching host/client settings for its plugin route.

Verify the improvement

Repeat the same workload and compare resource pressure, quote age, application responsiveness and logged disconnects. Revert an ineffective change. Preserve diagnostic logs before updates. An upgraded VPS helps only if the relevant bottleneck is improved; extra account rows alone are not a resource-sizing model.

No priority, affinity, firewall or power-policy change was performed on this VPS. A process-priority change should follow a diagnosed need and platform-supported guidance.

faq.q: Should I always set High process priority?
faq.a: No. Diagnose the bottleneck and follow platform-supported guidance.

faq.q: Does low total CPU rule out a processing bottleneck?
faq.a: No. One busy thread, memory pressure or disk activity can still matter.

faq.q: Should I remove all order-flow indicators?
faq.a: Remove only unnecessary work and check whether the strategy still receives its required data.

faq.q: Was a loaded-platform benchmark run here?
faq.a: No. This is a measured-diagnosis procedure, not a claimed performance test.

articles.title: Rithmic Weekend Maintenance: Check the Notice Before Reconnecting
articles.description: Understand how to check Rithmic maintenance notices, distinguish exchange hours from login availability, and verify account state when service returns.
articles.answer: Use the current maintenance notice for your Rithmic System and provider. Weekend maintenance can affect access, but provider articles do not establish one permanent universal opening time. Exchange trading hours and Rithmic login availability are different questions. Preserve the error and verify the affected service before deciding that a login failure is routine maintenance.

toc.label: What routine times does Rithmic currently describe?
Why a dated notice still matters

articles.body:
Find the matching notice

  1. Check Rithmic System Advisories for dated notices.
  2. Check your broker or funding provider's official announcements.
  3. Identify the named System, component, start/end time and timezone.
  4. Compare those details with your recorded error and attempted connection.
  5. If the time or scope is unclear, ask the provider to confirm it rather than converting a guessed schedule into a trading plan.

Do not assume that a weekend rejection is caused by maintenance. Wrong credentials, expired access or a local connection issue can still require a different response.

What routine times does Rithmic currently describe?

In the official FAQ expanded on 7 October 2026, Rithmic describes approximate weekday maintenance of 5:20–5:45 p.m. ET, Monday–Friday, and weekend work from Friday night to around noon ET on Sunday. Treat these as routine guidance, not a guaranteed reopening time. A dated notice for the affected System can identify a different interruption.

Why a dated notice still matters

Elite Trader Funding's login article and Quantower's issues guide describe weekend access in their own help contexts. Their wording is not a substitute for a dated notice for your environment. Rithmic's advisories also identify particular Systems in notices.

If an article uses “CST,” do not silently treat it as the correct local offset throughout daylight-saving time. Preserve the original timezone wording, establish the intended offset with the issuer, and then convert the event time. A one-hour interpretation error can matter when planning access.

Keep three questions separate

Question Matching reference
Can the application log in? Rithmic/provider service notice and connection result
Is this contract trading? Exchange schedule for the exact product and date
Must this account be flat by a firm deadline? Current provider rules for the account stage

An exchange reopening does not establish that every Rithmic service or provider account is ready. A firm deadline may also differ from the exchange session. Do not use a maintenance article to set a liquidation time or change account risk controls.

Prepare useful evidence

Before a planned interruption, record the connection route and how any active order management depends on local software. If orders or positions may exist, use the provider's supported procedure to establish account state. A disconnected display is not a cancellation record.

After service returns, check the intended account, service indicators, current contract data and working orders. Review earlier submissions before sending replacements. The reconnect checklist gives a sequence for this task.

No outage was induced and no maintenance recovery was tested for this article. A checklist and source comparison are more informative here than an unrelated homepage or invented error screenshot.

faq.q: Is Rithmic always unavailable for the whole weekend?
faq.a: No universal period is established here. Match a current notice to the specific System and service.

faq.q: Does Sunday exchange reopening guarantee I can log in?
faq.a: No. Exchange trading hours and application access are separate. Check both when planning your session.

faq.q: Should I reset my password during maintenance?
faq.a: First verify that the maintenance notice actually matches the failure. A timeout alone does not establish a password problem.

faq.q: Can I leave automation running through maintenance?
faq.a: Check the route's documented behavior for missed signals, retries and unavailable connections, along with the account rules. This guide makes no guarantee about a particular automation service.

articles.title: What Is Rithmic? Data, Trading Software and Account Access
articles.description: Understand what Rithmic provides, how RTrader Pro differs from a broker account, and which data, trading and automation permissions to check.
articles.answer: Rithmic provides technology for futures market data, order routing and account risk controls. RTrader Pro is one trading application that uses that technology. A broker or funding provider supplies your account access and its requirements; the word Rithmic alone does not identify a brokerage account, a permitted copier or a ready-to-trade setup.

toc.label: Separate the parts of a setup
What should a new user check first?

articles.body:
Separate the parts of a setup

Part Role What to confirm
Account provider Issues the account/login and applicable terms Account stage, permissions and support process
Rithmic technology Provides data and trading infrastructure Assigned System and service entitlement
Trading application Displays information and sends supported requests Supported connector, version and selected account
Exchange data access Determines the market information you receive Exchange, top-of-book/depth and subscriber requirements
Automation or copier Adds another order-request workflow Compatibility, provider permission and tested behavior

Rithmic's broker page describes the relationship between brokers, FCMs and the technology. An FCM, or futures commission merchant, is part of the live-account access arrangement; it is not another name for a charting program.

What is RTrader Pro?

It is Rithmic's desktop trading interface. The official product page describes its data, trading and account tools. The desktop login inspected here has separate Orders and Market Data sections.

The application title, an account panel, a price display and a service indicator answer different questions. For example, green Price status does not prove that a particular account is allowed to trade. Check the intended account and exchange separately.

Can another platform use Rithmic?

Some platforms document Rithmic connectors, but compatibility is specific to the application, version and account. Quantower's connection guide documents a supported local-plugin route. Sierra Chart support identifies a same-account limitation in its connector. Do not apply one platform's setup to every other platform.

What should a new user check first?

  1. Confirm the account provider actually issued a Rithmic login for the intended account.
  2. Obtain its assigned System and supported Gateway.
  3. Use the application/version its current guide supports.
  4. Review the required agreement and subscriber-status route accurately.
  5. Verify login, expected account and market data as separate checks.
  6. Understand the order/exit workflow before relying on it. Login is not an execution test.

The beginner checklist expands these checks. This article does not quote account prices, current firm signup availability or a universal data fee; those depend on the particular offering.

Where does PickMyTrade fit?

An alert bridge is another application/service layer, not a replacement for the account provider. If that is your intended workflow, review the TradingView and Rithmic guide. Separately confirm broker compatibility, firm permission, generated alert configuration and observed order results. A connection does not establish those other facts.

faq.q: Is Rithmic the same as my broker?
faq.a: No. Distinguish the technology provider from the firm that issued your account and login.

faq.q: Is RTrader Pro the only way to use Rithmic?
faq.a: No universal requirement is established. Use a connector supported for the actual account and workflow.

faq.q: Does Rithmic support mean a copier is available?
faq.a: No. Copier entitlement and provider permission are separate. The inspected native user had a copier-access restriction despite successful login.

faq.q: Does a connected chart prove the account can trade?
faq.a: No. Market data, account selection and order permissions need their own checks.

articles.title: Rithmic FAQ: Accounts, Data, Platforms and Automation
articles.description: Find clear answers about Rithmic credentials, trials, data, account restrictions, orders and automation, with links to detailed setup guides.
articles.answer: Rithmic is trading infrastructure, not the broker holding your retail trading account. Where should I start?

Common account and data questions

Question Answer
Is my website password the trading password? Not necessarily; use the separately issued Rithmic credentials.
Does funded mean Rithmic 01? No. Use the provider-assigned System and actual account stage.
Does a live chart prove live exchange execution? No. Simulated accounts can display live market prices.
Does data access include full depth? Not automatically; check the depth entitlement.
Are all retail users non-professional? No. Answer the exchange classification criteria accurately.
Does one login mean one trading account? No. The inspected login exposed two account rows.

PickMyTrade's Rithmic setup has its own compatibility rules, including Bulenox exclusion. A firm supporting Rithmic does not approve every automation or copier.

What do the screenshots prove?

Native captures show actual visible controls and status in the dated session, with private data concealed. Vendor illustrations are labeled separately. A connection screenshot is not a filled-order record; see the relevant guide for any remaining account-specific validation.

articles.title: Rithmic Glossary: Login, Data, Orders and Risk Terms
articles.description: Learn Rithmic terms in plain language: System, Gateway, plugin, entitlement, DOM, bracket, OCO, acknowledgement, fill and auto-liquidation.
articles.answer: Separate the connection environment, data entitlement, trading account and order state. System and Gateway identify connection choices; entitlement means permitted access; an acknowledgement is not a fill. These distinctions help you interpret Rithmic screens without assuming that one green indicator verifies every part of a workflow.
articles.body:
Login and connection terms

Term Plain-language meaning Practical use
User ID Issued trading login identity May differ from the provider website login
System Named connection environment Use the label assigned to the login
Gateway Supported entry point Do not treat it as a complete API address
Session A service connection Data and order sessions can have separate limits
Direct connection App connects through its own Rithmic connector Check simultaneous-login restrictions
Plugin host Local app serving a supported client connection Confirm both host and client remain correctly connected
Entitlement Permission to use a service or feature Login success alone does not establish every entitlement

Quantower's guide explains its local-plugin arrangement. Other connectors can differ. See Systems and Gateways for scoped native menu observations.

Market-data terms

Term Meaning
Bid / ask Prices at which participants are bidding to buy or offering to sell
BBO / top-of-book Best bid and offer with their quantities
Market depth Additional book price levels supplied by the exchange/data route
MBO Market-by-order information about individual displayed orders
DOM Depth-of-market display, often a price ladder
Historical data Earlier market information used to build past charts or analysis
Specific contract A futures contract for a particular expiry
Continuous chart A chart series connecting expiries; not automatically a tradable contract identifier

Rithmic's FAQ distinguishes top-of-book and depth. Confirm the required data entitlement for the exact instrument. A price ladder's existence does not prove every level is authorized or current.

Order-state and management terms

Term Meaning and limit
Request An application asks for an action; the result still needs confirmation
Acknowledgement A recorded response accepting/recognizing the request at that stage; not a fill
Working order An order reported active, subject to its current status and conditions
Fill / partial fill Recorded execution of all or part of the quantity
Rejection A request was refused; inspect its exact reason
Cancellation A recorded removal of the remaining working quantity
Bracket A related entry/exit arrangement; verify how children are created and managed
OCO One cancels the other; verify where that linked management runs
Trailing stop A stop-adjustment workflow; its trigger and hosting depend on the configuration/route

These are reading aids, not proof of support for every order type. NinjaTrader's order-location guide demonstrates why order hosting and management need connector-specific checks.

Account and risk terms

Position is the account's current exposure in a contract. P&L means profit and loss; confirm whether a displayed measure is realized, unrealized or otherwise calculated. Auto-liquidation is a configured account action whose criteria and effect must be verified for that account. Liquidation-only and locked are separate labels whose allowed actions can depend on the provider and controls.

Do not use a risk-field label to infer a guaranteed maximum loss, reset time or permission to change an administrator setting. Rithmic's risk product description gives product context; the field guide records account-scope limitations.

faq.q: Is an account the same as a login?
faq.a: No. A login can expose account access, but each account's state and permissions still need checking.

faq.q: Does working mean filled?
faq.a: No. Read the recorded order status and actual fills separately.

faq.q: Is a chart symbol always valid in an alert payload?
faq.a: No. Use the relevant connector or service's current symbol requirements and resolved contract.

faq.q: Is broker connectivity the same as copier eligibility?
faq.a: No. Copier support, entitlement and provider permission are separate questions.

articles.title: Rithmic for Beginners: A Practical Access and Setup Checklist
articles.description: Start with the correct Rithmic account, credentials and platform. Learn what to verify before relying on market data, orders, copying or automation.
articles.answer: Start with the provider that issued your Rithmic account. Obtain its trading credentials, assigned System and supported platform instructions. Verify login, account visibility and market data separately, then understand the intended order and exit workflow. Do not buy an evaluation, copier or VPS solely because another trader's screenshot shows a working login.

toc.label: Understand what a working connection establishes

articles.body:
Know which company does what

Your account provider supplies the account and its terms. Rithmic supplies trading technology. RTrader Pro is one application that displays data and account information. Another platform or alert bridge can add a separate connector and configuration. The Rithmic introduction explains those roles.

Prepare your information

Item Check
Account Correct provider, stage and intended environment
Trading login Credentials explicitly issued for Rithmic
Connection Assigned System and supported Gateway
Application Supported version and connector
Data Intended exchange and quote/depth access
Workflow Manual, plugin, automation or copier, with separate permission checks

Apex's setup guide is an example of provider-specific instructions. Use it for that workflow; another provider may differ. Evaluation or funded labels alone do not tell you which System to select.

Find the login fields

The inspected desktop version is 17.106.0.2. Box 1 marks the Orders section; box 2 marks Market Data and its plugin control. Follow the intended route's guide for On/Off choices. Do not copy all visible values into a different account's setup.

Work through the checks

  1. Use the provider's supported official download/interface link.
  2. Enter the issued trading credentials, checking for spaces and case changes.
  3. Select the assigned System and a supported Gateway.
  4. Review any required agreement route and answer classification questions truthfully. This is a certification question, not a cheaper-data toggle.
  5. Confirm that the expected account appears and that the intended data service supplies the exact contract.
  6. Learn the order-status and history views before relying on an order workflow.
  7. If using another application, check its connector and simultaneous-session arrangement.
  8. Use a suitable permitted test process before relying on automation; record the request, broker response and actual result separately.

This article is a preparation checklist. It does not demonstrate first-time agreement signing or a submitted order. Detailed onboarding remains in the first-login guide.

Understand what a working connection establishes

Connection status is useful, but it does not verify every exchange subscription, account risk rule or copier entitlement. The inspected native copier was unavailable for the user even though ordinary login worked. Do not activate copying or change risk values to experiment with those distinctions.

If something fails

Use the connection-failure guide to identify whether login, prices or account access failed. Preserve the error rather than repeatedly reinstalling software. If an order may already exist, verify account state before repeating the request.

For plugins, Quantower's official guide and Sierra Chart's support response show why one universal recipe is insufficient.

faq.q: Is my provider website password also my Rithmic password?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Use the credentials explicitly issued for trading.

faq.q: Must I choose Rithmic Paper Trading for every evaluation?
faq.a: Use the System assigned to the login. A provider can have a named environment.

faq.q: Does successful login mean I am ready to trade?
faq.a: Complete the account, data, permission and workflow checks first. Login is one step.

faq.q: Should every beginner use automation?
faq.a: That is a separate workflow decision. Confirm compatibility, permission and tested behavior; software does not supply a profitable strategy or guaranteed outcome.

articles.title: Rithmic Login Security: Protect Your Credentials
articles.description: Protect Rithmic credentials, use official recovery and download links, redact screenshots and separate general security practice from vendor claims.
articles.answer: Use official provider/download links, protect each login and keep passwords or tokens out of screenshots, alerts and ordinary support messages. Recover a broker-issued Rithmic password through the issuer's supported process. This guide offers account-handling practices; it does not certify Rithmic's encryption implementation, a bridge's security or universal two-factor authentication support.

toc.label: Use the real login layout as a privacy checklist
If credentials may have been exposed
What this review does not claim

articles.body:
Separate the credentials you use

Provider dashboards, Rithmic trading connections, platform licenses and automation services can have different logins. Apex's login guide explicitly distinguishes website and RTrader credentials.

Store credentials securely and avoid reusing passwords across unrelated accounts. Enable additional authentication where the actual service supports it; do not assume a control exists in every Rithmic interface. Microsoft's security guidance covers password protection, updates, malicious links and device protection.

Use the real login layout as a privacy checklist

Before sharing a capture, inspect both Orders and Market Data fields. Also check the title bar, account selectors, history rows, order identifiers and any provider dashboard shown behind the application. A masked password does not automatically make the full screenshot safe to publish.

For a public help image, use an empty-field layout or a bounded crop that retains the relevant control. Keep private original captures separately. Label any redaction so readers understand what was hidden; never substitute fabricated account or order information.

Download and support precautions

  1. Reach installation and recovery links from the provider or Rithmic's official site.
  2. Confirm the domain before entering a password or downloading a file.
  3. Keep the operating system, browser and supported applications updated using their official processes.
  4. Preserve firewall protection. Investigate a documented application restriction with a narrow exception rather than opening every port or disabling protection.
  5. Give support the error, time, version and connection context. Do not give it your password.

Microsoft explains firewall-exception risks. A trading connection problem alone does not justify a broad security change.

If credentials may have been exposed

Use the issuer's official recovery/support process promptly and tell it which credential was affected. Elite Trader Funding's guide provides one provider-specific recovery route. Inventory dependent connections before a password change interrupts them; also establish any active account/order state through the supported process.

Remove exposed material from places you control and follow the relevant service's token/password replacement instructions. Removing a public file does not prove that its contents were never copied. If the credential was an alert bridge token, update that service and the configured alerts according to its actual documentation; a Rithmic password reset is a different task.

What this review does not claim

The Rithmic FAQ states that support cannot retrieve a password and tells users not to send one. That does not disclose every storage, network or third-party implementation detail. No penetration test, credential-storage inspection or provider-security certification was performed here. Do not add an unsupported cipher, protocol version or compliance label to a help article.

faq.q: Is a blurred screenshot enough?
faq.a: Check the full image. Other fields, window titles or history rows may still identify the account. Opaque redaction or a focused crop is easier to verify than a light blur.

faq.q: Should I send a password so support can test the login?
faq.a: Do not send it in an ordinary support message. Follow the issuer's authorized recovery/investigation process.

faq.q: Is Remember Me required?
faq.a: No requirement was established by this review. Consider who can access the device and what the actual option stores; the inspected label alone does not establish its implementation.

faq.q: Does cloud hosting prove an automation service is secure?
faq.a: No. Review the actual service's documented controls and credential handling. Hosting location is not a security certification.

articles.title: RTrader Pro Updates: Check Your Build and Release Notes
articles.description: Find the installed RTrader Pro build, consult official update information and plan changes without confusing a web version with desktop or proving a bug fix.
articles.answer: Record the installed application's build and consult its official product/release information. The inspected desktop was 17.106.0.2; the earlier web session was 3.4.0.0. They are different products and version sequences. Neither observation proves which release is currently recommended for every provider or that an update resolves your particular error.

toc.label: What counts as evidence of a fix?

articles.body:
Find the installed build

The empty desktop login shows its build at the bottom right. If another interface uses a Help/About view, use that interface's current controls. Do not compare a web number numerically with a desktop number to decide which is newer.

Read the matching official information

Start at Rithmic's RTrader Pro product page and your provider's supported installation guide. Inspect the release-note date, version and affected feature. The indexed product page displayed an older release-note excerpt than the installed build recorded here; that excerpt is not proof that the installed build is unsupported or that the excerpt is the latest full changelog.

The previously inspected native File menu includes Check for Updates. This screenshot establishes the control's location in that inspection; the update command was not executed and no package was installed.

Make an update decision deliberately

  1. Record the current application/build, account environment and exact problem.
  2. Find a dated official note that actually addresses the affected feature or prerequisite.
  3. Confirm the build supported by your provider and any dependent plugin/client.
  4. Preserve the existing settings and required records through the supported process.
  5. Plan the interruption after establishing positions, orders and local management dependencies.
  6. After a supported update, verify connection, account, data and required workflow separately.

Do not restart or uninstall a running trading workflow solely to make a screenshot. A saved settings file is not proof that every connector and entitlement will transfer correctly.

What counts as evidence of a fix?

Evidence What it establishes
Release note names a correction Vendor documents that change for that release
New build displayed The application reports that build
Earlier error no longer appears in a scoped check That check did not reproduce it
Required account/order workflow verified Evidence for that recorded workflow, not every future outcome

Keep these stages separate when writing a troubleshooting article. Do not label a current account-specific defect “fixed” merely because a newer installer exists.

faq.q: Is 17.106.0.2 definitely the newest desktop release?
faq.a: This guide records the installed build, not a universal latest-release claim. Check the current official download and provider instructions.

faq.q: Why is my web version much lower?
faq.a: Different applications can have separate version sequences. Compare the correct product's release information.

faq.q: Does Check for Updates install anything immediately?
faq.a: This review did not execute it. Follow the current supported update procedure and review any prompts before applying changes.

faq.q: Should an update be my first response to a login error?
faq.a: Preserve the error and check issued settings, account status and service notices first. Update when official guidance matches the problem or supported-version requirement.

articles.title: Rithmic Pros and Cons: Evaluate the Account and Workflow
articles.description: Evaluate Rithmic by platform support, data needs, account permissions, fees and operational dependencies instead of unsupported speed or reliability rankings.
articles.answer: Evaluate the complete setup: provider account, application, data entitlement, order workflow and costs. Rithmic offers desktop and developer interfaces, but compatibility, session limits and enabled features vary. Do not choose it from a blanket “fastest,” “most reliable” or “best for all prop firms” claim. This guide is a comparison checklist, not a recommendation of a particular account or purchase.

toc.label: Potential advantages and the matching checks
Compare total cost and operational dependency

articles.body:
Potential advantages and the matching checks

Available capability Why it can matter What still needs checking
Desktop account/data tools One supported interface for inspecting a setup Account access and relevant feature entitlement
Third-party connectors Allows a supported platform choice Exact version, account and route
API families Different options for custom development Kit access, conformance, provider permission and fees
Data and risk infrastructure Provides components for a trading workflow Exchange subscription and account-specific enforcement
Local-plugin arrangements Can support sharing data in some setups Host/client compatibility and separate session limits

Rithmic's product page and API page describe available products. These descriptions do not establish measured end-to-end execution or every connector's use of a feature.

Practical limitations to assess

Quantower documents its plugin route; Sierra Chart support identifies a same-account restriction. This is a concrete reason to compare the actual connector rather than only the words “supports Rithmic.”

Desktop, web, mobile and API interfaces also have different requirements. A supported desktop account does not automatically authorize a custom production application. A visible Trade Copier entry does not prove copying is enabled: the native user inspected for this library received an entitlement restriction.

Do not generalize that restriction to every user or promise that logging in again removes it.

Compare total cost and operational dependency

Ask for the actual account offering's platform charges, exchange data classification/depth costs, session fees and optional service fees. This guide quotes no universal monthly total. A free desktop download does not prove every required account or data service is free.

Document what must stay running, where protective logic is managed and what the supported recovery path is. Renting a VPS or using cloud automation changes part of that setup; it does not guarantee availability, firm permission, capped losses or fills.

A decision checklist

  1. Confirm the provider/account stage supports the intended route.
  2. Check the exact application and connector version.
  3. Identify required exchanges, depth/history and agreement eligibility.
  4. Obtain current fees for the complete setup.
  5. Confirm sessions, copier/automation entitlement and provider rules independently.
  6. Verify the intended workflow in a suitable permitted environment before relying on it.

No benchmark or comparison against CQG, Tradovate or another provider was performed here. Use reproducible workflow evidence before publishing comparative speed or uptime rankings.

faq.q: Is Rithmic better than every alternative?
faq.a: No universal ranking is established. Compare your required platform, account, data, costs and operational workflow.

faq.q: Does API availability mean I can automate my account?
faq.a: Confirm application access and provider permission separately. The API guide explains those gates.

faq.q: Does Rithmic connectivity prove copier support?
faq.a: No. Compatibility, enabled entitlement and permission are separate.

faq.q: Does a successful demo prove live execution quality?
faq.a: It supports only the recorded environment and result. It does not guarantee later live fills or trading outcomes.

articles.title: Official Rithmic Resources and Support Routes
articles.description: Find official Rithmic, exchange, platform and account-provider resources for setup, troubleshooting, contract specifications and automation.
articles.answer: Use Rithmic for its platform/API references, the issuing broker or firm for account permission and risk configuration, and the front-end vendor for its connector behavior. Start from current official pages instead of an old download mirror or a public post containing credentials.
articles.body:

Resource Purpose

Exchange and account references

Use CME contract month codes, trading/holiday hours, equity roll dates and the exact product specification. Exchange schedules do not replace a firm's earlier holding cutoff or its account limits.

For provider-specific credentials and rules, use the dated firm references. A public setup article can establish control names without revealing a private account dashboard. Never put passwords, tokens or full private account identifiers in a public screenshot.

Third-party platforms and automation

The platform comparison links current Quantower, ATAS, Sierra, MotiveWave, Bookmap, Jigsaw and conditional NinjaTrader setup guides. For a receiving service, start with PickMyTrade Rithmic setup and TradingView webhook documentation.

Preserve context when requesting help

Keep the full error, timestamp/timezone, application version, account stage, issued System and connection route. Supply private identifiers only through the provider's secure support channel. A Reddit or Discord discussion can identify a common question; it is not proof of current entitlement, firm permission or a platform guarantee.

faq.q: Who can clear an account risk restriction?
faq.a: The authorized account/provider process, not a generic platform reinstall.

faq.q: Do advisory pages prove all services are operational?
faq.a: No. They publish notices with their own scope and timing.

faq.q: Can community posts establish product capability?
faq.a: Use them as question evidence, then verify claims with current primary sources.
